## home
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home>

- [concept] Messages provide direct model access where users construct every turn, manage conversation state, and write their own tool loop. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home
- [concept] Managed Agents offer fully managed agent infrastructure for deploying autonomous agents in stateful sessions with persistent event history. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home
- [fact] Claude is available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry cloud platforms. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home
- [fact] The Claude Fable 5 model is identified by the token `claude-fable-5` and is designed for long-running agents, research, and multi-day tasks. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home
- [fact] The Claude Opus 5 model is identified by the token `claude-opus-5` and is intended for complex agentic coding and enterprise work. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home
- [fact] The Claude Sonnet 5 model is identified by the token `claude-sonnet-5` and offers a combination of speed and intelligence for everyday tasks. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home
- [fact] The Claude Haiku 4.5 model is identified by the token `claude-haiku-4-5` and is the fastest model with near-frontier intelligence. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home
- [idea] Users should utilize interactive courses, code samples in the Cookbook, and deployable starter apps to master Claude. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home
- [concept] Claude Code is an agentic coding assistant that operates directly within the terminal. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home
- [idea] To begin building, users should follow the Quickstart guide for either Messages or Managed Agents. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/home

- [definition] Why use Skills — Skills are reusable, filesystem-based resources that give Claude domain-specific expertise: workflows, context, and best practices that turn a general-purpose agent into a specialist. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#why-use-skills
- [definition] Using Skills — Anthropic provides pre-built Agent Skills for common document tasks (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, PDF), and you can create your own custom Skills. Both work the same way: once a Skill is available in your environment, Claude uses it automatically when relevant to your request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#using-skills
- [definition] How Skills work — Skills use Claude's VM environment to provide capabilities beyond what's possible with prompts alone. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#how-skills-work
- [definition] Level 1: Metadata (always loaded) — The Skill's YAML frontmatter provides discovery information: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#level-1-metadata-always-loaded
- [definition] Level 2: Instructions (loaded when triggered) — The main body of SKILL.md contains procedural knowledge: workflows, best practices, and guidance: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#level-2-instructions-loaded-when-triggered
- [definition] The Skills architecture — Skills run in a code execution environment where Claude has filesystem access, bash commands, and code execution capabilities. Skills exist as directories on a virtual machine, and Claude interacts with them using the same bash commands you'd use to navigate files on your computer. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#the-skills-architecture
- [definition] Example: Loading a PDF processing Skill — Here's how Claude loads and uses the custom `pdf-processing` Skill from the earlier examples (not the pre-built `pdf` Skill): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#example-loading-a-pdf-processing-skill
- [definition] Where Skills work — Skills are available across Claude's agent products: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#where-skills-work
- [definition] Claude API — The Claude API supports both pre-built Agent Skills and custom Skills. Both work identically: specify the relevant `skill_id` in the `container` parameter along with the [code execution tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#claude-api
- [definition] Claude Code — [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) supports custom Skills. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#claude-code
- [definition] claude.ai — [claude.ai](https://claude.ai) supports both pre-built Agent Skills and custom Skills. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#claudeai
- [definition] Skill structure — Every Skill requires a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#skill-structure
- [definition] Security considerations — Use Skills only from trusted sources: those you created yourself or obtained from Anthropic. Skills give Claude new capabilities through instructions and code, which also means a malicious Skill can direct Claude to invoke tools or execute code in ways that don't match the Skill's stated purpose. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#security-considerations
- [definition] Pre-built Agent Skills — The following pre-built Agent Skills are available for immediate use: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#pre-built-agent-skills
- [definition] Open-source Skills — Anthropic also publishes open-source Skills in the [skills repository](https://github.com/anthropics/skills): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#open-source-skills
- [definition] Custom Skills examples — For complete examples of custom Skills, see the [Skills cookbook](https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/skills-notebooks-01-skills-introduction). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#custom-skills-examples
- [definition] Data retention — Agent Skills is not covered by ZDR arrangements. Skill definitions and execution data are retained according to Anthropic's standard data retention policy. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#data-retention
- [definition] Limitations and constraints — Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry follow the same limitations as the Claude API in the following subsections. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#limitations-and-constraints
- [definition] Sharing scope — Skills have different sharing models depending on where you use them: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#sharing-scope
- [definition] Runtime environment constraints — The exact runtime environment available to your Skill depends on the product surface where you use it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#runtime-environment-constraints

- [concept] Skills bundle three content types: Instructions (procedural knowledge), Code (executable scripts), and Resources (reference materials). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#how-skills-work
- [fact] Executable scripts like `fill_form.py` run via bash, where only the output enters context while the script code itself remains on the filesystem. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#how-skills-work
- [idea] Use executable scripts for deterministic operations to ensure reliability without incurring context costs for the code itself. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#how-skills-work
- [fact] Claude accesses additional files like `FORMS.md` or database schemas only when explicitly referenced by instructions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#how-skills-work
- [fact] There is no practical limit on bundled content in Skills because files do not consume context tokens until they are accessed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#how-skills-work
- [concept] The Skills architecture allows Claude to run bash commands and execute code within a virtual machine environment with filesystem access. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#how-skills-work
- [fact] A Skill can include dozens of reference files, but only the specific file needed for a task (e.g., sales schema) is loaded into context. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#how-skills-work
- [problem] If a Skill description does not clearly state when to use it, Claude may fail to trigger the Skill for relevant requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#how-skills-work

- [definition] Feature availability — The Availability column in each of the following tables lists the platforms that offer a feature. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview#feature-availability
- [definition] Model capabilities — Ways to steer Claude and Claude's direct outputs, including response format, reasoning depth, and input modalities. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview#model-capabilities
- [definition] Tools — Built-in tools that Claude invokes through `tool_use`. Server-side tools are run by the platform; client-side tools are implemented and executed by you. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview#tools
- [definition] Tool infrastructure — Infrastructure that supports discovering, orchestrating, and scaling tool use. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview#tool-infrastructure
- [definition] Context management — Infrastructure for controlling and optimizing Claude's context window. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview#context-management
- [definition] Files and assets — Manage files and assets for use with Claude. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview#files-and-assets
- [concept] Claude's API surface is organized into five areas: model capabilities, tools, tool infrastructure, context management, and files and assets. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [concept] Model capabilities allow developers to control how Claude reasons and formats responses. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [concept] Tools enable Claude to take actions on the web or in the user's environment through `tool_use`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [fact] The Models API returns `max_input_tokens`, `max_tokens`, and a `capabilities` object for every available model. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [concept] The ZDR column indicates whether a feature is available under a Zero Data Retention arrangement. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [fact] A platform listed without a label offers features as stable, fully supported, and recommended for production use with standard API versioning guarantees. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [concept] Server-side tools are run by the platform, while client-side tools are implemented and executed by the user. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [fact] For structured outputs, only JSON schemas are cached for up to 24 hours since last use; prompts and outputs are not stored. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [fact] Web search and web fetch are ZDR-eligible except when dynamic filtering is enabled. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [problem] Fallback credit and server-side fallback handle refusals from Claude Fable 5, which is not available under ZDR. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [fact] On Microsoft Foundry, features are available on Hosted on Anthropic deployments but not on Hosted on Azure deployments. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [idea] New users should start with model capabilities and tools before optimizing for cost, latency, or scale. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [concept] Tool infrastructure supports discovering, orchestrating, and scaling tool use. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [concept] Context management provides infrastructure for controlling and optimizing Claude's context window. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview
- [fact] Platform labels include Claude API, Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview

- [concept] Pre-built Agent Skills extend Claude's capabilities with specialized expertise for tasks such as creating documents, analyzing data, and processing files. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] Anthropic provides four pre-built Agent Skills in the API: PowerPoint (pptx), Excel (xlsx), Word (docx), and PDF (pdf). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] The Skills API returns metadata for each Skill, including its name and description. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [concept] Claude loads Skill metadata at startup to determine available Skills without loading their full instructions, representing the first level of progressive disclosure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [actionable] Use the Skills API to list all Anthropic-managed Skills before creating a request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] To create custom Skills, refer to the Agent Skills Cookbook for examples of building domain-specific expertise. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [actionable] Specify Skills using the `container` parameter in the Messages API to enable them for a request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] The request must include a model that supports the code execution tool to use Agent Skills. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] To define an Anthropic-managed Skill, set `type` to `anthropic`, specify the `skill_id` (e.g., `pptx`), and set `version` to `latest`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] The `tools` parameter must be enabled to allow code execution, which is required for Skills. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [concept] When a request is made, Claude matches the task to a relevant Skill and loads its full instructions as the second level of progressive disclosure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] The `code_execution_20260521` tool version is used in examples, but any current code execution tool version satisfies the Skills requirement. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] Older code execution tool versions such as `code_execution_20250825` also work with Skills. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] If using a different code execution tool version, use the `type` listed on the code execution tool page. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [actionable] Extract the file ID from the Step 2 response and download the file using the Files API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [fact] Generated files are saved in the code execution container and referenced by a file ID in the response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart
- [idea] For complete details on working with generated files, consult the Retrieve generated files section in the code execution tool documentation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/quickstart

## Recommended path for new developers
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro>

- [parameter] **What it is**: Messages API=Direct model prompting access; Claude Managed Agents=Pre-built, configurable agent harness that runs in managed infrastructure — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro
- [parameter] **Best for**: Messages API=Custom agent loops and fine-grained control; Claude Managed Agents=Long-running tasks and asynchronous work — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro
- [definition] Recommended path for new developers — Follow these steps to go from zero to a working Claude integration. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro#recommended-path-for-new-developers
- [definition] Make your first API call — Set up your environment, install an SDK, and send your first message to Claude. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro#recommended-path-for-new-developers
- [definition] Secure your credentials — Set an expiration when you create your API key. Keep the key out of source control, client-side code, and prompts. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro#recommended-path-for-new-developers
- [definition] Understand the Messages API — Learn the core request and response structure, including multi-turn conversations, system prompts, and stop reasons. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro#recommended-path-for-new-developers
- [definition] Choose the right model — Compare Claude models by capability and cost to pick the best fit for your use case. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro#recommended-path-for-new-developers
- [definition] Explore features and tools — Discover what Claude can do: extended thinking, web search, file handling, structured outputs, and more. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro#recommended-path-for-new-developers
- [definition] Develop with Claude — Anthropic provides developer tools to help you build and scale applications with Claude. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro#develop-with-claude
- [definition] Key capabilities — Claude can assist with many tasks that involve text, code, and images. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/intro#key-capabilities

## How it works
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview>

- [snippet] cURL: curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages \ — `curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages \` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api
- [snippet] CLI: ant beta:messages create --beta mcp-client-2025-11-20 <<'YAML' — `ant beta:messages create --beta mcp-client-2025-11-20 <<'YAML'` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api
- [snippet] Python: client = anthropic.Anthropic() — `client = anthropic.Anthropic()` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api
- [snippet] TypeScript: const anthropic = new Anthropic(); — `const anthropic = new Anthropic();` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api
- [snippet] C#: AnthropicClient client = new(); — `AnthropicClient client = new();` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api
- [snippet] Go: client := anthropic.NewClient() — `client := anthropic.NewClient()` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api
- [snippet] Java: import com.anthropic.models.beta.messages.BetaMcpToolset; — `import com.anthropic.models.beta.messages.BetaMcpToolset;` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api
- [snippet] PHP: $client = new Client(); — `$client = new Client();` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api
- [snippet] Ruby: client = Anthropic::Client.new — `client = Anthropic::Client.new` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api
- [parameter] Setup component: Destination=`api.anthropic.com`; Port / protocol=443 TCP; Used during=Provisioning and token rotation — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#network-requirements
- [parameter] cloudflared: Destination=Tunnel edge (`198.41.192.0/19`, `2606:4700:a0::/44`); Port / protocol=7844 TCP and UDP; Used during=Runtime — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#network-requirements
- [parameter] Proxy: Destination=Your upstream MCP servers; Port / protocol=As configured; Used during=Runtime — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#network-requirements
- [parameter] Outer mTLS between Anthropic and the transport provider, with IP validation: Unauthorized clients reaching the tunnel — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#security-layers
- [parameter] Inner TLS from Anthropic's back end to your proxy: Payload inspection by the transport provider or any network intermediary — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#security-layers
- [parameter] OAuth on each MCP server: Unauthorized use of MCP tools by authenticated tunnel traffic — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#security-layers
- [parameter] Tunnel access control: All content and traffic that transits your tunnel, and compliance with applicable third-party acceptable-use policies (including Cloudflare's) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#shared-responsibility-model
- [parameter] Validating your CA certificate before connecting to your proxy: Adherence to the deployment guidance on these pages — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#shared-responsibility-model
- [parameter] Ensuring Claude only sends requests to tunnels owned by your organization: Securing tunnel tokens and TLS private keys — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#shared-responsibility-model
- [definition] How it works — The [tunnel stack](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components) is two components that run inside your network: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#how-it-works
- [definition] Security layers — Three independent layers protect every request: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#security-layers
- [definition] What the transport provider can observe — Cloudflare provides the outbound transport. It cannot read MCP request or response payloads, but it does receive the following connection metadata: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#what-the-transport-provider-can-observe
- [definition] Deploy a tunnel — If you're new to MCP tunnels, start with the quickstart to get a working tunnel locally before configuring a production deployment. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#deploy-a-tunnel
- [definition] Use the tunneled MCP servers — Once your tunnel is active (it has an active CA certificate and your tunnel stack is connected), the upstream MCP servers are reachable from Claude Managed Agents and the Messages API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#use-the-tunneled-mcp-servers
- [definition] Managed Agents (Console) — 1. In **Managed Agents > Sessions**, create a session and choose **Create new agent** so you can edit the MCP server list. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#managed-agents-console
- [definition] Messages API — Pass the upstream MCP server's URL in the `mcp_servers` array, the same way as any other remote MCP server. The request body and `anthropic-beta` header follow the standard [MCP connector](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector) format; only the `url` is tunnel-specific. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview#messages-api

- [snippet] Generate a CA and server certificate: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes \ — `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes \` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart#what-you-need

- [snippet] Start it: docker compose up -d — `docker compose up -d` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart#what-you-need
- [definition] What you'll build — A two-container [tunnel stack](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components) (the [proxy](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components) and… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart#what-youll-build
- [definition] Create a tunnel — In the Claude Console sidebar, go to **Manage > MCP tunnels** and click **New tunnel**. Give it a name. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart#what-you-need
- [definition] Generate a CA and server certificate — The proxy terminates [inner TLS](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components) using a certificate signed by a CA you control. Generate both: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart#what-you-need
- [definition] Call it from Claude — In the Console, go to **Managed Agents > Sessions** and create a session. In the agent picker choose **Create new agent**, give the agent a name, and keep the pre-filled model. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart#what-you-need
- [definition] Next steps — The tunnel is verified end to end. To swap in your own MCP server, add it to `docker-compose.yaml` (or run it on the same Docker network), add a route for it in `config/mcp-proxy.yaml`, then restart the proxy (`docker compose restart mcp-proxy`). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart#next-steps
- [concept] MCP tunnels are in research preview and require a request for access to try them. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [fact] The quickstart uses Docker Compose with manual credential provisioning, which is the shortest path for local testing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [concept] A tunnel stack consists of a proxy and cloudflared containers plus a sample MCP server running alongside them. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [fact] When running, the sample server is reachable from Claude at `https://echo.<your-tunnel-domain>/mcp` even though nothing listens on a public port. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [fact] OpenSSL 1.1.1 or later is required, and the `openssl` binary must be on your PATH for Windows users. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [actionable] In the Claude Console sidebar, go to **Manage > MCP tunnels** and click **New tunnel** to create a new tunnel. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [actionable] Leave **Set up programmatic access** off during creation because this quickstart uses manual credential provisioning. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [actionable] Copy the **Domain** (e.g., `abcd1234.tunnel.anthropic.com`) and **Token** from the tunnel's **Connection** section. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [actionable] Generate a CA and server certificate using OpenSSL, as the proxy terminates inner TLS using a certificate signed by a CA you control. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [actionable] Upload `data/ca.crt` (or paste its contents) in the Console to flip the tunnel status to **Active**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [fact] The proxy config and compose file must be written before starting the deployment. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [actionable] Run `docker compose up` to start the containers, expecting one `route configured` line for `echo` and four `Registered tunnel connection` lines. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [actionable] Create a session in **Managed Agents > Sessions**, choose **Create new agent**, and add the MCP server with Subdomain `echo` and Path `mcp`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [actionable] Ask the agent to use the hello tool by saying: Use the hello tool to greet tunnel. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [idea] To swap in your own MCP server, add it to `docker-compose.yaml` or run it on the same Docker network. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [actionable] Add a route for your custom server in `config/mcp-proxy.yaml` and restart the proxy using `docker compose restart mcp-proxy`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart
- [fact] Production deployments can be done with Docker Compose for hardened single-host deployment or Helm for Kubernetes with automatic credential management. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/quickstart

- [definition] How tool use works — Tools differ primarily by where the code executes. **Client tools** (including user-defined tools and tools with Anthropic-defined schemas, such as `bash` and `text_editor`) run in your application. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#how-tool-use-works
- [definition] When Claude uses tools — With the default `tool_choice` of `{"type": "auto"}`, Claude determines on each turn whether to call a tool or respond directly. It calls a tool when the request maps to that tool's described capability and the answer isn't already in context. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#when-claude-uses-tools
- [definition] Choose a tool — For `type` strings, versions, and beta headers, see [Tool reference](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-reference). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#choose-a-tool
- [definition] Your own tools — For tools you define, you write the schema and your application executes each call. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#your-own-tools
- [definition] Anthropic-schema client tools — Anthropic publishes the schema and trains Claude on it. Your application still executes each call and returns the `tool_result`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#anthropic-schema-client-tools
- [definition] Server tools — Server tools run on Anthropic's infrastructure, with no handler code in your application. See [Server tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools) for the mechanics they share. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#server-tools

- [definition] Quick start — The advisor tool is in beta. Include the beta header `advisor-tool-2026-03-01` in your requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#quick-start
- [definition] How it works — When you add the advisor tool to your `tools` array, the executor model determines when to call it, like any other tool. When the executor calls the advisor: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#how-it-works
- [definition] Successful advisor call — When the advisor is called, a `server_tool_use` block is followed by an `advisor_tool_result` block in the assistant's content. The following example shows the plaintext `advisor_result` variant returned by a Claude Opus 4.8 advisor. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#successful-advisor-call
- [definition] Result variants — The `advisor_tool_result.content` field is a discriminated union. For successful calls, the variant depends on the advisor model: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#result-variants
- [definition] Error results — If the advisor call fails, the result carries an error: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#error-results
- [definition] Multi-turn conversations — Pass the full assistant content, including `advisor_tool_result` blocks, back to the API on subsequent turns. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#multi-turn-conversations
- [definition] Resuming a paused turn — A response can end with `stop_reason: "pause_turn"` while an advisor call is still pending. When that occurs, the response contains the advisor's `server_tool_use` block with no `advisor_tool_result` for it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#resuming-a-paused-turn
- [definition] Mid-conversation nudge for under-calling executors — If a Haiku executor has not called the advisor in its first assistant turn, append a short reminder as an additional user message before the second assistant turn. In Anthropic's internal behavioral evaluation this raised task pass rates by roughly 7 percentage points on Haiku executors. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#mid-conversation-nudge-for-under-calling-executors
- [definition] Streaming — The advisor sub-inference does not stream. The executor's stream pauses while the advisor runs; then the full result arrives in a single event. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#streaming
- [definition] Usage and billing — Advisor calls run as a separate sub-inference billed at the advisor model's rates. Usage is reported in the `usage.iterations[]` array: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#usage-and-billing
- [definition] Advisor prompt caching — There are two independent caching layers. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-prompt-caching
- [definition] Executor-side caching — The `advisor_tool_result` block is cacheable like any other content block. A `cache_control` breakpoint placed after it on a subsequent turn hits. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#executor-side-caching
- [definition] Advisor-side caching — Set `caching` on the tool definition to enable prompt caching for the advisor's own transcript across calls within the same conversation: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-side-caching
- [definition] Combining with other tools — The advisor tool composes with other server-side and client-side tools. Add them all to the same `tools` array: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#combining-with-other-tools
- [definition] Prompting for coding and agent tasks — The advisor tool ships with a built-in description that nudges the executor to call it near the start of complex tasks and when it hits difficulty. For research tasks, no additional prompting is typically needed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#prompting-for-coding-and-agent-tasks
- [definition] Capping advisor output — Set `max_tokens` on the tool definition to cap the advisor's total output (thinking plus text) per call: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#capping-advisor-output
- [definition] Pairing with effort settings — For coding tasks, pairing a Sonnet executor at medium [effort](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort) with an Opus advisor achieves intelligence comparable to Sonnet at default effort, at lower cost. For maximum intelligence, keep the executor at default effort. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#pairing-with-effort-settings
- [definition] Model compatibility — The executor model (the top-level `model` field) and the advisor model (the `model` field inside the tool definition) must form a valid pair. The advisor must be Claude Sonnet 4.6 or a more capable model, and it must be at least as capable as the executor. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#model-compatibility
- [definition] Platform availability — The advisor tool is available in beta on the Claude API and on [Claude Platform on AWS](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws). It is not currently available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Foundry. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#platform-availability
- [definition] Advisor on Claude Managed Agents — [Claude Managed Agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview) sessions support an advisor as well, configured as part of the agent rather than as a tool definition: add a `{"type": "advisor", "model": ...}` entry to the agent's multiagent roster, and the session's primary… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-on-claude-managed-agents
- [concept] The advisor tool enables a faster executor model to consult a higher-intelligence advisor model mid-generation for strategic guidance. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool
- [concept] The advisor reads the full conversation and produces a plan or course correction, after which the executor continues the task. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool
- [idea] This pattern is designed for long-horizon agentic workloads like coding agents, computer use, and multistep research pipelines where most turns are mechanical but planning is crucial. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool
- [fact] The pattern delivers close to advisor-solo quality while the bulk of token generation occurs at executor-model rates. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool
- [concept] The benefit of this pattern shrinks as the executor's own capability approaches the advisor's capability. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool
- [fact] Measured results regarding cost and intelligence optimization are available in the Optimizing for cost and intelligence documentation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool
- [fact] Zero data retention (ZDR) applies to this feature, with specific details found in the API and data retention documentation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool
- [concept] The advisor tool composes with other server-side and client-side tools. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#combining-with-other-tools
- [actionable] Add all composed tools to the same `tools` array. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#combining-with-other-tools
- [fact] The executor can search the web, call the advisor, and use custom tools in the same turn. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#combining-with-other-tools
- [concept] The advisor's plan can inform which tools the executor reaches for next. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#combining-with-other-tools
- [concept] Advisor on Claude Managed Agents is configured as part of the agent rather than as a tool definition. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-on-claude-managed-agents
- [fact] The roster entry for an advisor takes no `max_uses`, `max_tokens`, or `caching` options. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-on-claude-managed-agents
- [concept] Advice from an advisor is delivered as thread events on the session's event stream rather than as `advisor_tool_result` blocks in the response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-on-claude-managed-agents
- [actionable] Add a `{"type": "advisor", "model": ...}` entry to the agent's multiagent roster to configure an advisor. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-on-claude-managed-agents
- [fact] The session's primary thread can consult the advisor model mid-turn. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-on-claude-managed-agents
- [concept] The Memory tool allows storing and retrieving information across conversations using a client-side memory directory. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#next-steps
- [concept] Server tools enable working with Anthropic-executed tools, including server_tool_use blocks, pause_turn continuation, and domain filtering. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#next-steps
- [fact] The Tool reference provides a directory of Anthropic-provided tools and serves as a reference for optional tool definition properties. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#next-steps
- [concept] Effort is a parameter used to control how many tokens Claude uses when responding, allowing a trade-off between response thoroughness and token efficiency. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#next-steps

## Components
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts>

- [snippet] Connection model: sequenceDiagram — `sequenceDiagram` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#connection-model
- [parameter] **Tunnel stack**: Definition=The two containers you run inside your network to attach to a tunnel: the proxy and cloudflared. One stack serves one tunnel and can be replicated across hosts for availability. With programmatic access, the setup component runs alongside the stack to provision credentials.; Also appears as=the stack, the MCP tunnel stack, the tunnel deployment, your deployment — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components
- [parameter] **Proxy**: Definition=Anthropic's routing component. Terminates inner TLS, validates that upstream IPs fall within an allowed range, and routes each request to an upstream MCP server based on hostname.; Also appears as=`mcp-proxy` (image name, Compose service name, and Helm container name), `mcp-gateway` (container-internal config path `/etc/mcp-gateway/config.yaml` and Helm `gateway.config.*`… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components
- [parameter] **cloudflared**: Definition=Cloudflare's open-source tunnel connector. Initiates the outbound-only connections from your network to the tunnel edge and carries encrypted traffic between the edge and the proxy. Not related to a Managed Agent.; Also appears as=the outbound connector, the tunnel connector — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components
- [parameter] **Setup component**: Definition=The `setup` binary, shipped inside the `mcp-proxy` image. With programmatic access it authenticates over Workload Identity Federation, fetches the tunnel token, generates a CA and server certificate, and registers the CA with Anthropic. Also provides `renew-cert`.; Also appears as=setup Job (the Helm pre-install hook), `setup` service (the Compose profile), setup… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components
- [parameter] **Tunnel edge**: Definition=The Cloudflare edge servers that cloudflared dials out to (IP ranges `198.41.192.0/19` and `2606:4700:a0::/44`, port 7844 TCP and UDP). The tunnel that runs over them is provisioned and controlled by Anthropic; Cloudflare operates the underlying network.; Also appears as=the edge, the Anthropic-operated tunnel edge — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components
- [parameter] **Inner TLS**: Definition=A second TLS handshake carried inside the tunnel's plaintext WebSocket stream, between Anthropic's backend and your proxy. The proxy presents a server certificate signed by a CA you registered on the tunnel. Because only you hold the private key, the transport provider cannot read request or response payloads.; Also appears as=the inner TLS handshake — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components
- [parameter] **Upstream MCP server**: Definition=An MCP server running in your private network that the proxy routes to. Each upstream is exposed as one subdomain under your tunnel domain.; Also appears as=upstream, routed MCP server, tunneled MCP server — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#components
- [parameter] **Programmatic access**: How credentials reach the stack=The setup component authenticates to the Tunnels API through [Workload Identity Federation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation), fetches the tunnel token, generates a CA and server certificate locally, and registers the CA. No long-lived secret is copied by hand. Requires a federation rule with… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#credential-provisioning
- [parameter] **Manual**: How credentials reach the stack=You copy the tunnel token from the Claude Console, generate a CA and server certificate yourself (for example with `openssl`), register the CA in the Console, and supply the token and certificate to the stack as secrets. No setup component runs.; Helm chart name=External mode (`setup.enabled: false`); Tab label=**Without programmatic access** — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#credential-provisioning
- [definition] Credential provisioning — The tunnel stack needs two credentials at runtime: the **tunnel token**, which authenticates cloudflared's outbound connection, and a **server certificate** signed by a CA registered on the tunnel, which the proxy presents during the inner TLS handshake. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#credential-provisioning
- [definition] Connection model — Two directions are at work in a tunnel, and they point opposite ways: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts#connection-model
- [concept] MCP tunnels are in research preview and require a request for access via a form. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts
- [concept] The tunnel stack requires two credentials at runtime: a tunnel token for authenticating cloudflared's outbound connection and a server certificate signed by a registered CA for the proxy to present during the inner TLS handshake. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts
- [concept] Credential provisioning is handled through two modes referred to as the programmatic flow and the manual flow. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts
- [fact] The tunnel connection direction is outbound, where cloudflared dials from your network to the tunnel edge on port 7844. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts
- [fact] No inbound ports are opened for MCP tunnels; firewalls only see egress traffic. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts
- [concept] MCP requests travel from Anthropic toward your network over the established tunnel connection through cloudflared to the proxy and then to the upstream MCP server. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts
- [fact] The phrase 'outbound-only' describes the connection mechanism, not the direction of the requests carried over it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts
- [fact] Inner TLS spans Anthropic's backend and your proxy, with cloudflared and the tunnel edge sitting between them on the wire. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts
- [fact] Cloudflared and the tunnel edge see only ciphertext; the proxy is the first location inside your network where MCP request payloads are readable. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/concepts

- [definition] Parameters — A bash tool definition has two required fields, `type` and `name`, and the `name` must be `bash`. The tool is schema-less: you don't provide an `input_schema`, because the schema is built into Claude's model and can't be modified. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#parameters
- [definition] Tool versions — `bash_20250124` is the current version of the tool, and it requires no beta header. Every model from Claude Sonnet 3.7 ([retired](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations)) onward accepts it, including all current Claude models. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#tool-versions
- [definition] Example: Multistep automation — Claude can chain commands across tool calls to complete a multistep task: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#example-multistep-automation
- [definition] Implement the bash tool — Claude determines which command to run. Your application owns everything else: the shell process, the timeout, and the safety checks. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#implement-the-bash-tool
- [definition] Create a persistent bash session — Start one long-lived bash process and run every command inside it. Because a pipe to a live process never reports end-of-file, the session prints a unique sentinel line after each command to mark where that command's output ends: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#implement-the-bash-tool
- [definition] Process Claude's tool calls — Extract and run commands from Claude's responses: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#implement-the-bash-tool
- [definition] Return the result to Claude — Send the `tool_result` back in a `user` message that continues the same conversation. Claude either requests another command in the same session or finishes its answer: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#implement-the-bash-tool
- [definition] Implement safety measures — Add validation and restrictions. Use an allowlist rather than a blocklist: a blocklist misses any command it didn't anticipate. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#implement-the-bash-tool
- [definition] Handle errors — When a command fails or the session breaks, tell Claude what happened. Return the message as the `tool_result` content and set `is_error` to `true`, which marks the tool call as failed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#handle-errors
- [definition] Security — Your application runs whatever command Claude requests. Run the session in an isolated environment, such as a container or a virtual machine, as the least-privileged user that can do the work. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#security
- [definition] Pricing — The bash tool definition adds the following input tokens to your request. This is in addition to the per-model [tool use system prompt](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#pricing) that applies whenever any tool is present. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#pricing
- [definition] Combining with other tools — The bash tool pairs well with the [Text editor tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/text-editor-tool): Claude edits a file with one tool and requests the command that runs it with the other. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool#combining-with-other-tools

- [parameter] `succeeded`: Request was successful. Includes the message result. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#retrieving-batch-results
- [parameter] `errored`: Request encountered an error and a message was not created. Possible errors include invalid requests and internal server errors. You will not be billed for these requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#retrieving-batch-results
- [parameter] `canceled`: User canceled the batch before this request could be sent to the model. You will not be billed for these requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#retrieving-batch-results
- [parameter] `expired`: Batch reached its 24-hour expiration before this request could be sent to the model. You will not be billed for these requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#retrieving-batch-results
- [definition] Message Batches API — The Message Batches API is a powerful, cost-effective way to asynchronously process large volumes of [Messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages/create) requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#message-batches-api
- [definition] How the Message Batches API works — When you send a request to the Message Batches API: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [definition] Supported models — All [active models](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview) support the Message Batches API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#supported-models
- [definition] What can be batched — Almost any request you can make to the Messages API can be included in a batch. This includes: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#what-can-be-batched
- [definition] Pricing — The Batches API offers significant cost savings. All usage is charged at 50% of the standard API prices. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#pricing
- [definition] Prepare and create your batch — A Message Batch is composed of a list of requests to create a Message. The shape of an individual request comprises: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#prepare-and-create-your-batch
- [definition] Tracking your batch — The Message Batch's `processing_status` field indicates the stage of processing the batch is in. It starts as `in_progress`, then updates to `ended` once all the requests in the batch have finished processing, and results are ready. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#tracking-your-batch
- [definition] Listing all Message Batches — You can list all Message Batches in your Workspace using the [list endpoint](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/listing-message-batches). The API supports pagination, automatically fetching additional pages as needed: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#listing-all-message-batches
- [definition] Retrieving batch results — Once batch processing has ended, each Messages request in the batch has a result. There are four result types: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#retrieving-batch-results
- [definition] Canceling a Message Batch — You can cancel a Message Batch that is currently processing using the [cancel endpoint](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/canceling-message-batches). Immediately after cancellation, a batch's `processing_status` will be `canceling`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#canceling-a-message-batch
- [definition] Using prompt caching with Message Batches — The Message Batches API supports prompt caching, allowing you to potentially reduce costs and processing time for batch requests. The pricing discounts from prompt caching and Message Batches can stack, providing even greater cost savings when both features are used together. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#using-prompt-caching-with-message-batches
- [definition] Server tools and the agentic loop — All [server tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools) (web search, web fetch, code execution, MCP connectors, advisor, and tool search) work in batch requests. The batch worker runs the same server-side agentic loop as the synchronous Messages API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#server-tools-and-the-agentic-loop
- [definition] Extended output (beta) — The `output-300k-2026-03-24` beta header raises the `max_tokens` cap to 300,000 for batch requests using Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5, or Claude Sonnet 4.6. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#extended-output-beta
- [definition] Data retention — Batch processing stores request and response data for up to 29 days after batch creation. You can delete a message batch at any time after processing using the `DELETE /v1/messages/batches/{batch_id}` endpoint. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#data-retention
- [concept] Batch processing allows submitting multiple requests together for asynchronous processing instead of handling them one at a time. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing
- [fact] The Message Batches API is Anthropic's first implementation of the batch processing pattern. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing
- [fact] Most batches finish in less than 1 hour while reducing costs by 50% and increasing throughput. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing
- [problem] This approach is not suitable for tasks that require immediate responses. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing
- [idea] Use batch processing when you need to optimize for cost efficiency or run large-scale evaluations and analyses. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing
- [concept] The Message Batches API is designed for tasks where immediate responses are not required. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing
- [concept] The Message Batches API creates a new batch from provided requests and processes them asynchronously, allowing independent handling of each request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [actionable] Poll for the status of a batch to retrieve results once processing has ended for all requests within it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [idea] Use the Message Batches API for bulk operations that do not require immediate results, such as large-scale evaluations or content moderation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [fact] A Message Batch is limited to either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB in size, whichever limit is reached first. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [fact] Most batches complete within 1 hour, but results are accessible only when all messages finish or after 24 hours, whichever comes first. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [problem] Batches expire if processing does not complete within 24 hours. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [fact] Batch results are available for download for 29 days after creation; after this period, the batch remains viewable but results cannot be downloaded. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [fact] Batches are scoped to a Workspace, meaning you can only view batches and results created within the Workspace where the request runs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [problem] Processing may be slowed by high demand or volume, potentially causing more requests to expire after 24 hours than usual. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [fact] Due to high throughput and concurrent processing, batches may slightly exceed a Workspace's configured spend limit. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [problem] Setting `max_tokens` to 0 is not supported inside a batch because ephemeral cache entries written during processing likely expire before follow-up requests run. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [fact] All active models support the Message Batches API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [concept] Almost any request supported by the Messages API, including Vision and Tool use (e.g., web search, code execution), can be included in a batch. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [idea] Consider using the 1-hour cache duration with prompt caching for batches with shared context to improve cache hit rates, as processing can take longer than 5 minutes. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works
- [fact] All usage of the Batches API is charged at 50% of the standard API prices. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#pricing
- [concept] Batches are isolated within the Workspace they are created in. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#batch-storage-and-privacy
- [fact] Batch results are available for 29 days after the batch is created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#batch-storage-and-privacy
- [actionable] Access batches only via API requests in the same Workspace or by users with permission to view Workspace batches in the Console. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#batch-storage-and-privacy
- [fact] Batches may take up to 24 hours for processing, but many finish sooner. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [problem] It is possible for a batch to expire and not complete within the 24-hour window. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [concept] The Message Batches API supports nearly all features available in the Messages API, including most beta features. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [problem] Parameters `stream`, `speed`, `store`, `previous_thread_event_id`, `cache_hint`, `context_hint`, `max_tokens: 0`, and `research_preview_2026_02` are not supported in batch requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [fact] The Message Batches API offers a 50% discount on all usage compared to standard API prices. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [problem] Once a batch has been submitted, it cannot be modified or updated. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [actionable] To make changes to a batch, cancel the current batch and submit a new one. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [problem] Batch cancellation may not take immediate effect after being requested. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [fact] The Message Batches API has HTTP requests-based rate limits in addition to limits on the number of requests in need of processing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [fact] Usage of the Batches API does not affect rate limits in the Messages API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [concept] When retrieving batch results, each request has a `result` field indicating whether it `succeeded`, `errored`, was `canceled`, or `expired`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [concept] For `errored` results, additional error information is provided in the response object. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [fact] Batches and their results are isolated within the Workspace in which they were created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [fact] Each request within a batch is processed independently, with no data leakage between requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [fact] Batch results are only available for a limited time of 29 days. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [actionable] Downloading batch results in the Console can be disabled on the organization-level or on a per-workspace basis. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [concept] Prompt caching is supported in the Message Batches API, but cache hits are provided on a best-effort basis due to concurrent and unordered processing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq
- [concept] Natural citations can be enabled for RAG applications by providing search results with source attribution. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#next-steps
- [idea] Use prompt caching to reduce cost and latency by caching prompt prefixes shared across requests in a batch. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#next-steps

- [definition] Quick start — The browser use tool is available on the Claude API and [Google Cloud](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-vertex-ai): add one entry of type `browser_toolset_20260801`, with no `name`, to the `tools` array of a [Messages… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#quick-start
- [definition] How browser use works — Browser use runs as an agent loop: Claude returns member tool calls, your executor runs them against the browser, and you return the results until Claude answers in text. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#how-browser-use-works
- [definition] Batch actions — A turn with several member calls is a batch action: run the calls in the order they appear, stop at the first failure, and answer every later call with `is_error: true` and the exact text `Not executed: an earlier action in this turn failed.` A batch uses the same response shape as [parallel tool… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#batch-actions
- [definition] Targets and coordinates — Member tools that act on a location take a `target` object, which is either a viewport-pixel coordinate or a reference to an element that `read_page` or `find` returned. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#targets-and-coordinates
- [definition] Security considerations — Browser use carries risks that standard API features don't, because Claude reads and acts on content from the open web, where any page can contain text written to manipulate it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#security-considerations
- [definition] Member tools — The `browser_toolset_20260801` entry declares 31 member tools; each call's `input` is exactly the parameters listed here, and `tab_id`, where optional, defaults to the active tab. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#member-tools
- [definition] Configure the toolset — Besides `type`, the toolset entry accepts `configs`, `cache_control`, and `allowed_callers`; the rules these fields share with the computer use toolset are listed under [Client toolsets](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-reference#client-toolsets), and this section… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#configure-the-toolset
- [definition] Enable or disable member tools — List only the members you want to change in `configs`; every member you omit keeps its default. - [definition] Combine with other tools — Declare the browser use tool alongside your own tools and other Anthropic-provided tools in the same `tools` array. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#combine-with-other-tools
- [definition] Enable optional members — Four member tools are disabled by default: `javascript_exec` and `file_upload` because they widen what a manipulated page could make Claude do, and `read_console` and `read_network` because not every browser automation stack can supply those logs and they widen what page-controlled content reaches… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#enable-optional-members
- [definition] Upload files — `file_upload` sets the files on an `<input type="file">` element directly, which is more reliable than driving a native file chooser. Its `target` is a reference only, because the call needs the element's identity, and it takes `paths`, `document_ids`, or both: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#upload-files
- [definition] Run JavaScript in the page — `javascript_exec` runs the expression Claude writes in the page's context and returns the value of the last expression as text; Claude writes an expression, not a `return` statement. The code runs with the page's full privileges, including its cookies, storage, and same-origin requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#run-javascript-in-the-page
- [definition] Read console and network activity — `read_console` returns the tab's console entries and `read_network` returns its network requests, each as text with one line per entry accumulated since the previous read of that tab. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#read-console-and-network-activity
- [definition] Track tabs with `browser_state` — Claude addresses tabs by `tab_id`, your application is the source of truth for which tabs exist, and you report that state in a `browser_state` content block that Claude never sees directly: the API renders the text Claude reads from it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#track-tabs-with-browser-state
- [definition] Tab management results — For `new_tab`, `switch_tab`, `close_tab`, and `list_tabs`, a successful result's `content` is exactly one `browser_state` block with no text or image, and the API writes the text Claude sees. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#tab-management-results
- [definition] Tab context on other results — On every other member the block is optional: send it when the set of open tabs, the active tab, or a tab's title or URL changed, or when there are `state_changes` to report, and always include the full `tabs` inventory. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#tab-context-on-other-results
- [definition] Report downloads — When a click or navigation starts a file download, report it in `state_changes` on the result of the call during which it happened, correlated across results by a `download_id` you assign. Downloads run asynchronously and can span several results, so there are three event types: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#report-downloads
- [definition] Handle errors — Report a failed call to Claude as an ordinary error result: `is_error: true`, text content that says what went wrong, `toolset_name` echoed, and no `browser_state` block. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#handle-errors
- [definition] Return errors from your executor — Make error text specific, because Claude reads it and adapts: `Error: Navigation to https://example.com/status timed out after 30 seconds. The page may be unavailable.` gives Claude something to act on where a bare `Error: navigation failed` doesn't. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#return-errors-from-your-executor
- [definition] Request errors — The API validates the toolset entry and every member `tool_use` and `tool_result` block in the conversation. When one is malformed, the API returns an `invalid_request_error` before Claude runs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#request-errors

- [actionable] Build page reads from the accessibility tree or visible text rather than raw DOM source to prevent hidden text from reaching Claude. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool#security-considerations
