- [definition] Set up the loop — The example is a single file. The constants control the effort level, the fan-out shape, and how often the mode refresher is re-sent. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#set-up-the-loop
- [definition] Define the mode reminders — The reminders are short on purpose. They flip the mode and point at the tool description, where the heavyweight instructions live. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#define-the-mode-reminders
- [definition] Grant standing consent in the tool description — The Workflow tool carries the real behavioral contract: the opt-in rule, the standing consent that applies while the mode is on, granularity guidance for sizing the fan-out, and the quality patterns the model can reach for (a verification wave, a completeness critic, multiphase sequencing). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#grant-standing-consent-in-the-tool-description
- [definition] Run the bash tool locally — The bash handler runs the requested command with a timeout, captures combined stdout and stderr, and truncates the result so a runaway command can't flood the context window. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#run-the-bash-tool-locally
- [definition] Run one subagent — Each workflow subtask becomes its own small agent loop with the bash tool, running at the same effort as the main loop. A per-request timeout bounds each API call so a dropped connection degrades one subagent instead of stalling the whole run. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#run-one-subagent
- [definition] Journal results so reruns resume — A fan-out that spawns dozens of subagents is expensive to restart from scratch. A small content-addressed journal makes it idempotent: before dispatching a subagent, look up the SHA-256 of its prompt in a local JSON file, and return the recorded result if one exists. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#journal-results-so-reruns-resume
- [definition] Fan out, then verify — The fan-out accepts up to `MAX_TOTAL_SUBTASKS` prompts, runs them through the journal with at most `MAX_CONCURRENT` in flight (sequential in the PHP port), and isolates failures so one broken subagent degrades to an error string instead of ending the run. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#fan-out-then-verify
- [definition] Toggle the mode with mid-conversation system messages — The agent appends the user's message first, then any system messages that are due: the exit notice, the full mode text on entry, or the periodic refresher. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#toggle-the-mode-with-mid-conversation-system-messages
- [definition] Run it — The bash tool in this example runs model-written commands directly on your machine with no sandbox, and the fan-out runs several of those agents in parallel. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#run-it
- [definition] Toward a production harness — This example is deliberately small. A harness meant for real workloads would typically add: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example#toward-a-production-harness
- [concept] An orchestration mode is a session-level switch that enables maximum thoroughness and parallel subagent fan-out for substantive requests when active. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] The orchestration mode is not an API parameter but is built entirely from documented pieces like effort levels and system messages. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [concept] When the mode is off, the orchestration tool reverts to per-request opt-in behavior. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] The example sets the effort level at the top of each request using a value like `xhigh` without requiring a beta header. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [concept] Mode reminders use mid-conversation system messages to tell the model the mode is active, providing a one-line refresher every several turns. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] The top-level `system` field never changes in this example to ensure the cached prefix stays intact. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [concept] Standing consent is granted by including a tool description stating the model should author and run workflows for every substantive task without asking first while the mode is on. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [problem] The fan-out mechanism multiplies token usage significantly as a single request can spawn many subagent conversations. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] `MAX_CONCURRENT` caps the number of subagents running simultaneously, while `MAX_TOTAL_SUBTASKS` caps the queue size for a single Workflow call. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] The PHP port of this example is sequential and ignores the `MAX_CONCURRENT` constant. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [actionable] Set the `DOC_TEST_MODE` environment variable to cap loops to a single turn for automated docs harness validation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [concept] The Workflow tool description defines the behavioral contract including opt-in rules, standing consent, and quality patterns like verification waves. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] Subagents use a `report_findings` tool to return results as structured JSON instead of prose. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] The example uses the Anthropic-defined `bash_20250124` tool run locally. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [problem] The bash handler runs commands with no sandbox, executing them with the permissions of the process that launched the example. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] Commands run in the directory from which the example is launched, and `DOC_TEST_MODE` uses a throwaway fixture directory removed on exit. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [idea] A production agent should back the bash tool with a long-lived shell to ensure working directory, environment, and restart actions behave as documented. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [concept] The journaling mechanism uses content-addressed storage (SHA-256 of the prompt) to make fan-out runs idempotent and allow resumption after interruption. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] The journal deduplicates across runs but not within a single fan-out wave; deleting the journal file starts fresh. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [concept] The verification wave reuses the same subagent path to refute results, defaulting to refuted when uncertain. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [fact] System messages must be placed after the user turn to keep cached bytes untouched and satisfy placement rules. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [problem] Trivial or conversational requests stay solo, but the model may scout with bash commands before deciding to dispatch the Workflow tool unprompted. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [idea] Add sandboxing before adapting this example for anything beyond local experimentation due to the lack of security isolation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [idea] A production harness should use durable journaling with a store that survives process restarts and handles concurrent writers across machines. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [idea] Implement budget enforcement to track total subagents launched across the whole session and refuse to exceed a hard cap. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example

- [snippet] Response format: { — `{` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#response-format
- [parameter] field absent: The request did not include `diagnostics`, or the beta header was missing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#response-format
- [parameter] `null`: Either `previous_message_id` was `null` (first turn, nothing to compare), or a comparison ran and found no divergence. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#response-format
- [parameter] `{"cache_miss_reason": null}`: The comparison was still running when the response was serialized. This can happen when the response starts very quickly. Treat it as inconclusive and check the next turn. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#response-format
- [parameter] `{"cache_miss_reason": {...}}`: A `cache_miss_reason` is attached. For `*_changed` types this identifies the first divergence point; `previous_message_not_found` and `unavailable` are cases where no comparison was produced. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#response-format
- [parameter] `model_changed`: What it means=The `model` differs from the previous request (for example, a router, A/B test, or fallback selected a different model). The cache is per-model.; What to change=Hold the model constant within a cached conversation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#cache-miss-reason-types
- [parameter] `system_changed`: What it means=The `system` parameter differs. Typically a timestamp, request ID, or other per-request value was interpolated into the system prompt.; What to change=Make the system prompt a byte-stable constant and move dynamic data into the first `user` message after your cache breakpoint. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#cache-miss-reason-types
- [parameter] `tools_changed`: What it means=The `tools` array differs: tools were added, removed, or reordered between turns, or tool `input_schema` JSON was serialized non-deterministically.; What to change=Send the same tool list on every turn in a fixed order with deterministically serialized schemas (for example, sort keys). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#cache-miss-reason-types
- [parameter] `messages_changed`: What it means=The model, system, and tools all match, but an earlier entry in `messages` was altered, reordered, or removed rather than appended to. Typically conversation history was truncated or edited, or assistant turns and `tool_result` blocks were re-serialized differently on resend.; What to change=Treat the history as append-only; echo assistant `content` and tool… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#cache-miss-reason-types
- [parameter] `previous_message_not_found`: What it means=No stored fingerprint exists for the supplied `previous_message_id`. This is not evidence that your request changed. Typically the previous request did not carry the beta header, it came from a different workspace, or too much time has passed since it was sent.; What to change=Send the beta header on every turn and keep consecutive turns close together… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#cache-miss-reason-types
- [parameter] `unavailable`: What it means=Diagnostic information was not available for this request. This includes the case where `model`, `system`, and `tools` match but another prompt-affecting request parameter (`tool_choice`, `thinking`, `context_management`, `output_config`, `output_format`, or the set of active `anthropic-beta` headers) differs, and very long conversations where the divergence is… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#cache-miss-reason-types
- [parameter] `null`: Cache read tokens=high; Interpretation=Working as expected. Your prefix is stable and the cache hit. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#reading-diagnostics-alongside-usage
- [parameter] `null`: Cache read tokens=low or zero; Interpretation=Your requests match but the cache entry was no longer available. Consider shortening gaps between turns or using the [1-hour cache TTL](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#1-hour-cache-duration). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#reading-diagnostics-alongside-usage
- [parameter] `cache_miss_reason` is a `*_changed` type: Cache read tokens=low or zero; Interpretation=Your bug. The request changed; fix the cause indicated by `type`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#reading-diagnostics-alongside-usage
- [parameter] `cache_miss_reason` is a `*_changed` type: Cache read tokens=high; Interpretation=Rare. A change occurred late in the prompt but an earlier `cache_control` breakpoint still hit. Worth fixing, but low impact. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#reading-diagnostics-alongside-usage
- [definition] How cache diagnostics works — When the beta header is present, the API stores a lightweight fingerprint of each request, keyed by the response `id`. On your next request, include that `id` as `diagnostics.previous_message_id`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#how-cache-diagnostics-works
- [definition] Basic usage — Send the beta header on every turn. On the first turn, pass `"previous_message_id": null` to opt in without a prior message to compare against. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#basic-usage
- [definition] Streaming — In streaming responses, `diagnostics` appears on the `message_start` event. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#streaming
- [definition] Threading diagnostics through a conversation loop — In a multi-turn conversation, carry the latest response `id` forward as `previous_message_id` on every turn. The first iteration passes `null` to opt in; each subsequent iteration passes the `id` from the previous response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#threading-diagnostics-through-a-conversation-loop
- [definition] Response format — The `diagnostics` field on the response `Message` has four possible states: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#response-format
- [definition] Cache miss reason types — `cache_miss_reason` is a discriminated union on `type`. The response reports the earliest divergence only, so fix it first; later ones may be hidden behind it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#cache-miss-reason-types
- [definition] Reading diagnostics alongside usage — `diagnostics` answers "did my request change?" while `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` answers "did the cache hit?". Combining them tells you where to look. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#reading-diagnostics-alongside-usage
- [definition] Data retention — Cache diagnostics is ZDR eligible (qualified). Anthropic does not store the raw text of your prompts or Claude's outputs for this feature. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#data-retention

- [definition] How citations work — Integrate citations with Claude in these steps: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations#how-citations-work
- [definition] Feature compatibility — Citations work in conjunction with other API features including [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching), [token counting](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting), and [batch… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations#feature-compatibility
- [definition] Choosing a document type — Three document types are supported for citations. Documents can be provided directly in the message (base64, text, or URL) or uploaded through the [Files API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files) and referenced by `file_id`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations#choosing-a-document-type
- [definition] Plain text documents — Plain text documents are automatically chunked into sentences. You can provide them inline or by reference with their `file_id`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations#plain-text-documents
- [definition] PDF documents — PDF documents can be provided as base64-encoded data, a URL, or by `file_id`. PDF text is extracted and chunked into sentences. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations#pdf-documents
- [definition] Custom content documents — Custom content documents give you control over citation granularity. No additional chunking is done and chunks are provided to the model according to the content blocks provided. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations#custom-content-documents
- [definition] Response structure — When citations are enabled, responses include multiple text blocks with citations: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations#response-structure
- [definition] Streaming support — For streaming responses, citations arrive as a `citations_delta` delta type inside `content_block_delta` events. Each delta contains a single citation to add to the `citations` list on the current `text` content block. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations#streaming-support

- [definition] Authentication — Claude in Amazon Bedrock supports three authentication paths. Choose the one that best fits your security requirements. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#authentication
- [definition] Bedrock service role (recommended) — Use a Bedrock service role with AWS-managed keys for the most secure, long-lived access: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#bedrock-service-role-recommended
- [definition] Admin: provision the service role — An AWS administrator provisions a Bedrock service role and grants developers `iam:PassRole` permission on the service role ARN. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#bedrock-service-role-recommended
- [definition] Developer: pass the role — When calling the API, Bedrock assumes the service role on your behalf. See the [Amazon Bedrock documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/bedrock-mantle.html) for how to associate the role with your requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#bedrock-service-role-recommended
- [definition] IAM assumed roles — For identity-federated access with a 12-hour maximum session: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#iam-assumed-roles
- [definition] Admin: configure the IAM role — Create an IAM role scoped to your Claude models. The trust policy names your identity provider (SAML, OIDC, or AWS Identity Center). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#iam-assumed-roles
- [definition] Developer: authenticate and assume — Authenticate through your corporate identity provider, then assume the IAM role. AWS STS issues temporary credentials that the SDK or CLI uses to sign requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#iam-assumed-roles
- [definition] Bearer tokens — For short-term access without IAM roles (12-hour maximum, least preferred): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#bearer-tokens
- [definition] Admin: restrict token types — Block long-term keys by attaching a policy that denies `bedrock:CallWithBearerToken` unless the `bedrock:BearerTokenType` condition matches a short-term token. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#bearer-tokens
- [definition] Developer: mint a token — Use the `aws-bedrock-token-generator` CLI to mint a bearer token. Pass it in the `x-api-key` header on each request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#bearer-tokens

- [problem] Server-side fallback is not supported; users must implement the client-side fallback pattern instead. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock
- [fact] The endpoint follows the pattern `https://bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws/anthropic/v1/messages`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock
- [concept] Credentials and region are resolved using standard AWS precedence: constructor arguments, environment variables, then the AWS config file and credential chain. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock

- [definition] Hosting options — Claude models in Microsoft Foundry are available in two hosting options. You choose the hosting option when you configure the deployment. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#hosting-options
- [definition] Install an SDK — Anthropic's [client SDKs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/overview) support Foundry through a platform-specific package or client class. The examples on this page also show requests with cURL and the ant CLI. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#install-an-sdk
- [definition] Provisioning — Foundry uses a two-level hierarchy: **resources** contain your security and billing configuration, while **deployments** are the model instances you call through the API. You'll first create a Foundry resource, then create one or more Claude deployments within it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#provisioning
- [definition] Provisioning Foundry resources — Create a Foundry resource, which is required to use and manage services in Azure. You can follow these instructions to create a [Foundry resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/multi-service-resource?pivots=azportal#create-a-new-azure-ai-foundry-resource). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#provisioning-foundry-resources
- [definition] Creating Foundry deployments — After creating your resource, deploy a Claude model to make it available for API calls. These steps describe the new Foundry portal (the **New Foundry** toggle is on): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#creating-foundry-deployments
- [definition] Authentication — Claude in Microsoft Foundry supports two authentication methods: API keys and Entra ID tokens. Both methods use Azure-hosted endpoints in the format `https://{resource}.services.ai.azure.com/anthropic/v1/*`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#authentication
- [definition] API key authentication — After provisioning your Foundry Claude resource, you can obtain an API key from the Foundry portal: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-key-authentication
- [definition] Microsoft Entra authentication — Entra ID authentication lets you manage access with Azure RBAC, integrate with your organization's identity management, and avoid handling API keys manually. To use Entra ID tokens: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#microsoft-entra-authentication
- [definition] Correlation request IDs — Foundry includes request identifiers in HTTP response headers for debugging and tracing. When contacting support, provide both the `request-id` and `apim-request-id` (Azure API Management) values to help teams quickly locate and investigate your request across both Anthropic and Azure systems. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#correlation-request-ids
- [definition] Feature support — Claude in Microsoft Foundry supports most Claude features. You can find all the features currently supported in [Features overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#feature-support
- [definition] Context window — Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 have a [1M-token context window](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows) on Microsoft Foundry. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#context-window
- [definition] Additional features not supported when hosted on Azure — The following features are available for deployments hosted on Anthropic but are not supported for deployments hosted on Azure: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#additional-features-not-supported-when-hosted-on-azure
- [definition] API responses — API responses from Claude in Microsoft Foundry follow the standard [Claude API response format](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages/create). This includes the `usage` object in response bodies, which provides detailed token consumption information for your requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-responses
- [definition] API model IDs and deployments — Lifecycle terms (Deprecated, Retired) are defined in [Model deprecations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations). Microsoft Foundry follows the Claude API lifecycle schedule. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-model-ids-and-deployments
- [definition] Billing — Claude in Microsoft Foundry bills through the [Azure Marketplace](https://azuremarketplace.microsoft.com/). Usage is denominated in Claude Consumption Units (CCUs), metered hourly, and invoiced monthly in arrears on your Azure bill. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#billing
- [definition] Migrating between hosting options — To move an existing deployment from one hosting option to the other: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#migrating-between-hosting-options

- [problem] Web search and web fetch tool versions later than `web_search_20250305` and `web_fetch_20250910` are not supported on Azure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#feature-support
- [fact] Deployments hosted on Azure support only basic web search and web fetch versions, meaning dynamic filtering, response inclusion, and cache bypass are unavailable. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#feature-support
- [problem] Agent Skills are not supported for deployments hosted on Azure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#feature-support
- [problem] Programmatic tool calling is not supported for deployments hosted on Azure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#feature-support
- [problem] The Files API is not supported for deployments hosted on Azure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#feature-support
- [fact] Requests using unsupported features against an Azure-hosted deployment return a `400 Bad Request` error by design. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#feature-support
- [idea] Claude Code automatically detects deployments hosted on Azure and adapts its feature set accordingly. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#feature-support
- [concept] API responses from Claude in Microsoft Foundry follow the standard Claude API response format. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-responses
- [fact] The `usage` object is included in response bodies to provide detailed token consumption information. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-responses
- [fact] The `usage` object behavior is consistent across all platforms including Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, AWS, Foundry, and Google Cloud. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-responses
- [concept] Foundry-specific response headers are documented under Correlation request IDs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-responses
- [concept] Microsoft Foundry follows the Claude API lifecycle schedule, including terms like Deprecated and Retired. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-model-ids-and-deployments
- [fact] By default, deployment names match the model IDs shown in the documentation table. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-model-ids-and-deployments
- [concept] Users can create custom deployments with different names in the Foundry portal to manage configurations, versions, or rate limits. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-model-ids-and-deployments
- [fact] API requests should use the deployment name rather than necessarily the model ID. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-model-ids-and-deployments
- [concept] Claude Mythos Preview is a research preview available to invited customers on Microsoft Foundry. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-model-ids-and-deployments
- [actionable] To upgrade to a newer Claude model, run `/claude-api migrate` in Claude Code. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-model-ids-and-deployments
- [concept] The `/claude-api migrate` command applies model ID swaps and breaking parameter changes across the codebase. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-model-ids-and-deployments
- [fact] The migration skill detects which cloud platform your code targets to adjust model ID formats and feature changes. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#api-model-ids-and-deployments
- [fact] Claude in Microsoft Foundry bills through the Azure Marketplace. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#billing
- [concept] Usage is denominated in Claude Consumption Units (CCUs) and metered hourly. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#billing
- [fact] Invoicing occurs monthly in arrears on your Azure bill. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#billing
- [problem] CCUs are not prepaid credits. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#billing
- [fact] There is no CCU balance or commitment required. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#billing
- [concept] Migrating between hosting options involves creating a new deployment of the model's other hosting version. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#migrating-between-hosting-options
- [actionable] Create a new deployment of the model's other hosting version (Hosted on Azure or Hosted on Anthropic). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#migrating-between-hosting-options
- [fact] The new deployment can be created in the same Foundry resource or a new one. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#migrating-between-hosting-options
- [actionable] Update your application to pass the new deployment name in the `model` parameter. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#migrating-between-hosting-options
- [actionable] Delete the old deployment once traffic has moved. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#migrating-between-hosting-options
- [concept] If the new deployment is in the same Foundry resource, your endpoint URL and authentication remain unchanged. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#migrating-between-hosting-options
- [actionable] If you created a new resource, update your application's endpoint and credentials to point to it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#migrating-between-hosting-options
- [concept] Azure provides monitoring and logging for Claude usage through standard Azure patterns including Azure Monitor, Azure Log Analytics, and Cost Management. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#monitoring-and-logging
- [fact] Azure Monitor tracks API usage, latency, and error rates for Claude usage. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#monitoring-and-logging
- [concept] Azure Log Analytics allows users to query and analyze request/response logs for Claude. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#monitoring-and-logging
- [fact] Cost Management is used to monitor and forecast costs associated with Claude usage. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#monitoring-and-logging
- [idea] Anthropic recommends logging activity on at least a 30-day rolling basis to understand usage patterns and investigate potential issues. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#monitoring-and-logging
- [fact] Azure's logging services are configured within the user's Azure subscription. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#monitoring-and-logging
- [concept] Enabling logging does not provide Microsoft or Anthropic access to user content beyond what is necessary for billing and service operation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#monitoring-and-logging
- [concept] The Foundry model catalog allows users to browse Anthropic models. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#additional-resources
- [fact] Microsoft provides pricing details for Azure AI Foundry via the Azure AI Foundry pricing page. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#additional-resources
- [fact] Anthropic provides per-model pricing details on its own Model pricing page. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#additional-resources
- [concept] The Azure portal is used to manage Azure resources. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry#additional-resources

- [definition] Bearer token authentication — You can authenticate with Bedrock using bearer tokens instead of AWS credentials. This is useful in corporate environments where teams need access to Bedrock without managing AWS credentials, IAM roles, or account-level permissions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#bearer-token-authentication
- [definition] Activity logging — Bedrock provides an [invocation logging service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-invocation-logging.html) that allows you to log the prompts and completions associated with your usage. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#activity-logging
- [definition] Feature support — For the full feature list with Amazon Bedrock availability, see [Features overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [definition] PDF support on Bedrock — PDF support is available on Bedrock through both the Converse API and InvokeModel API. For detailed information about PDF processing capabilities and limitations, see [Amazon Bedrock PDF support](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support#amazon-bedrock-pdf-support). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#pdf-support-on-bedrock
- [definition] Mid-conversation system messages on Bedrock — [Mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages) are available through the InvokeModel API for Claude Fable 5 and Claude Opus 4.8. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#mid-conversation-system-messages-on-bedrock
- [definition] Context window — Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 have a [1M-token context window](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows) on Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#context-window
- [definition] Global versus regional endpoints — Starting with **Claude Sonnet 4.5 and all future models**, Bedrock offers two endpoint types: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [concept] This page covers the legacy Amazon Bedrock integration using InvokeModel and Converse APIs with ARN-versioned model identifiers. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy
- [fact] The legacy integration uses AWS event-stream encoding for data transmission. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy
- [concept] Models available on the Messages-API Bedrock endpoint use the Messages API at /anthropic/v1/messages with SSE streaming. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy
- [fact] The legacy integration applies to Claude models Opus 4.6 and earlier. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy

- [fact] The AWS CLI version must be at or newer than version 2.13.23. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#install-and-configure-the-aws-cli

- [concept] Credentials can be verified after installation and configuration to ensure they are working. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#install-and-configure-the-aws-cli
- [concept] Anthropic's client SDKs support accessing Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#install-an-sdk-for-accessing-bedrock
- [concept] Users can access Amazon Bedrock directly using an AWS SDK like boto3. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#install-an-sdk-for-accessing-bedrock
- [fact] The documentation provides installation instructions for Python, TypeScript, C#, Go, Java, PHP, and Ruby SDKs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#install-an-sdk-for-accessing-bedrock
- [actionable] Install the appropriate client SDK for your programming language to access Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#install-an-sdk-for-accessing-bedrock
- [actionable] Use boto3 directly as an alternative method to access Bedrock in Python. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#install-an-sdk-for-accessing-bedrock
- [actionable] Go to the AWS Console > Bedrock > Model Access and request access to Anthropic models. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [fact] Anthropic model availability varies by region. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [concept] Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Opus 4.7 are reachable through InvokeModel on bedrock-runtime. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [problem] Models like Claude Opus 5 do not have ARN-versioned model IDs and are omitted from the model table. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [fact] Lifecycle terms Deprecated and Retired are defined in Model deprecations documentation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [problem] A request that passes the base model ID for newer models via cross-region inference fails with an HTTP 400 error. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [actionable] To invoke newer models, pass an inference profile instead of the base model ID. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [fact] The inference profile ID is the base model ID with a prefix from a column marked Yes in the supported regions table. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [actionable] You can pass the full inference profile ARN in the form arn:aws:bedrock:{region}:{account-id}:inference-profile/{inference-profile-id}. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [fact] The ant CLI does not support Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [problem] Calling the InvokeModel API with AWS credentials requires SigV4 request signing, which SDKs handle automatically but cURL does not. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [fact] You can authenticate with Bedrock using bearer tokens instead of AWS credentials. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [idea] Using bearer tokens is useful in corporate environments where teams need access to Bedrock without managing AWS credentials or IAM roles. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [actionable] Set the AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK environment variable to authenticate with Bedrock using a bearer token. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#accessing-bedrock
- [concept] The page lists supported features for Claude on Amazon Bedrock, including Messages API, Prompt caching, Thinking, Tool use, Citations, and Structured outputs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [fact] Input sources such as URL sources for images and documents, and the Files API are not supported on Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [fact] Server-side tools including code execution, web search, web fetch, and advisor are not available on Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [fact] Agent infrastructure features like Agent Skills, MCP connector, and programmatic tool calling are not supported on Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [problem] The Message Batches, Models, Admin, Compliance, Usage and Cost API endpoints are not available on Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [problem] Claude Managed Agents are not supported on Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [problem] Server-side fallback via the `fallbacks` parameter is not supported; users must implement the client-side fallback pattern instead. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [problem] Automatic prompt caching using the top-level `cache_control` field is not supported; explicit cache breakpoints must be used instead. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [problem] The `computer_toolset_20260801` and `browser_toolset_20260801` toolsets are not currently available on Amazon Bedrock, though beta versions remain. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [fact] PDF support is available on Bedrock through both the Converse API and InvokeModel API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [idea] Visual PDF analysis for charts, images, and layouts requires citations to be enabled; without them, only basic text extraction is available. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [idea] For full control over PDF processing without forced citations, users should use the InvokeModel API instead of the Converse API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [fact] Mid-conversation system messages are available through the InvokeModel API for Claude Fable 5 and Claude Opus 4.8. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [problem] Mid-conversation system messages are not available on Claude Sonnet 5; users must use the top-level `system` field instead. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [problem] Mid-conversation system messages are not available for ARN-versioned models listed in the model table. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [fact] The Converse API accepts system instructions through its top-level `system` parameter. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [fact] Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 have a 1M-token context window on Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [fact] Other Claude models, including Sonnet 4.5 and Sonnet 4 (deprecated), have a 200k-token context window on Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [problem] Bedrock limits request payloads to 20 MB, which may be reached before the token limit when sending large documents or many images. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support
- [concept] Bedrock offers two endpoint types: global endpoints for dynamic routing and regional endpoints for guaranteed data routing through specific geographic regions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [fact] Starting with Claude Sonnet 4.5 and all future models, Bedrock offers both global and regional endpoint types. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [fact] Regional endpoints include a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints for infrastructure costs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [fact] The regional endpoint pricing premium applies only to Claude Sonnet 4.5 and future models, not older models. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [fact] Older models like Claude Sonnet 4 (deprecated) and earlier maintain their existing pricing structures without the regional premium. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [idea] Use global endpoints for applications where data residency is flexible, as they provide maximum availability and uptime. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [concept] Global endpoints dynamically route requests to regions with available capacity to ensure high availability. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [idea] Use regional endpoints (CRIS) when data residency or compliance requirements mandate traffic through specific geographic regions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [fact] Regional endpoints are available in the US, EU, Japan, and Asia-Pacific regions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [concept] For Claude Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, and Sonnet 4.5, global endpoints are the default implementation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [fact] Model IDs for Claude Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, and Sonnet 4.5 already include the `global.` prefix. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [problem] The `ant` CLI does not support Amazon Bedrock; users must use SDK examples instead. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [fact] Calling the `InvokeModel` API with AWS credentials requires SigV4 request signing, which SDKs handle automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [problem] Self-contained cURL commands for Bedrock endpoints require manual handling of SigV4 request signing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints
- [idea] To use regional endpoints, replace the `global.` prefix in the model ID with a regional prefix such as `us.`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#global-versus-regional-endpoints

- [definition] How the platform integration works — Claude models run on Anthropic-managed infrastructure. This is a commercial integration for billing and access through AWS. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#how-the-platform-integration-works
- [definition] Claude Platform on AWS versus Amazon Bedrock — Both offerings let you use Claude through AWS, but they differ in architecture, API surface, and feature availability. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#claude-platform-on-aws-versus-amazon-bedrock
- [definition] Set up your account — Setting up Claude Platform on AWS happens in four phases: sign up on the AWS Console service page, complete your Anthropic organization setup, note your workspace ID, and sign in to the Claude Console. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#set-up-your-account
- [definition] Sign up in the AWS Console — 1. Open the [AWS Console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/) and navigate to the **Claude Platform on AWS** service page. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#set-up-your-account
- [definition] Set up your Anthropic organization — After sign-up completes, you're redirected to `platform.claude.com/partner-signup`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#set-up-your-account
- [definition] Create your workspace and note its ID — After you complete setup, the AWS Console prompts you to create a workspace. See [Workspaces](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#workspaces) for details on region binding, IAM resource scoping, and creating additional workspaces. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#set-up-your-account
- [definition] Sign in to the Claude Console — Access to the Claude Console is federated through AWS IAM: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#set-up-your-account
- [definition] Moving from an existing Anthropic organization — Signing up for Claude Platform on AWS always provisions a new Anthropic organization tied to your AWS account. There is no in-place conversion: an existing organization, such as a first-party Claude API organization, can't become a Claude Platform on AWS organization. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#moving-from-an-existing-anthropic-organization
- [definition] Enable outbound web identity federation — The Claude Platform on AWS gateway calls `sts:GetWebIdentityToken` server-side to mint a JWT it forwards to Anthropic. This STS capability is **disabled by default** on every AWS account. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#enable-outbound-web-identity-federation
- [definition] Obtain your workspace ID — You create a workspace from the AWS Console after completing account setup (see [Set up your account](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#set-up-your-account)). Workspaces are bound to a single AWS region. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#obtain-your-workspace-id
- [definition] Authentication — Claude Platform on AWS supports two authentication methods: AWS IAM with Signature Version 4 (SigV4) request signing (primary) and API key authentication. Both use the same base URL and request format. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#authentication
- [definition] SigV4 authentication — SigV4 is the enterprise-native path and integrates with your existing AWS IAM policies, roles, and auditing. Configure AWS credentials using any method supported by the [AWS default credential provider chain](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdkref/latest/guide/standardized-credentials.html): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#sigv4-authentication
- [definition] API key authentication — For simpler integration paths (local development and scripts), you can authenticate with an API key instead of SigV4. Set the `ANTHROPIC_AWS_API_KEY` environment variable or pass `apiKey` to the SDK constructor. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#api-key-authentication
- [definition] Credential precedence — The platform-specific client resolves authentication in the following order. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#credential-precedence
- [definition] Region resolution — The client reads `AWS_REGION` from the environment if `aws_region`/`awsRegion` is not passed to the constructor, falling back to `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` for compatibility with the standard AWS SDKs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#region-resolution
- [definition] Install an SDK — Anthropic's [client SDKs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/overview) support Claude Platform on AWS. Each SDK provides a platform-specific client class that handles SigV4 signing, region-based base URL construction, and the `anthropic-workspace-id` header. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#install-an-sdk
- [definition] Available models — The following models are available on Claude Platform on AWS: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#available-models
- [definition] Making requests — Claude Platform on AWS uses the same API endpoints as the first-party Claude API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#making-requests
- [definition] Context window — Context-window sizes on Claude Platform on AWS are identical to the first-party Claude API. See [Context windows](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows) for per-model limits. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#context-window
- [definition] Feature support — Claude Platform on AWS uses Claude API endpoints directly, which means you get full feature parity with the first-party Claude API (except where noted in the [feature limitations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#features-not-supported)): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#feature-support
- [definition] Claude Managed Agents — [Claude Managed Agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview) is available on Claude Platform on AWS, including [agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup), [environments](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/environments)… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#claude-managed-agents

- [definition] Workspaces — Inference and resource requests on Claude Platform on AWS target a workspace. You pass the workspace's ID in the `anthropic-workspace-id` header on these API calls. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#workspaces
- [definition] Workspace scoping — Workspaces are bound to a single AWS region. A workspace created in `us-west-2` can only be accessed through the `us-west-2` endpoint. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#workspace-scoping

- [definition] Using the Claude Console — Claude Platform on AWS uses the standard Claude Console at [platform.claude.com](https://platform.claude.com). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#using-the-claude-console
- [definition] Signing in — Access to the Claude Console is federated through AWS IAM. - [definition] Available pages — The **Through AWS gateway** column indicates whether the page reads and writes data through the AWS gateway (and is therefore governed by [IAM actions](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-platform-on-aws-iam-actions)). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#available-pages
- [definition] Switching organizations — The Claude Console does not support organization switching for Claude Platform on AWS. - [definition] Rate limits and quotas — Organizations on Claude Platform on AWS are placed on the Start tier. Anthropic manages rate limits directly, not through AWS quota systems. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#rate-limits-and-quotas
- [definition] Billing — Claude Platform on AWS bills through [AWS Marketplace](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace). Usage is denominated in Claude Consumption Units (CCUs), metered hourly, and invoiced monthly in arrears on your AWS bill. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#billing
- [definition] Spend limits — The Start, Build, and Scale usage tiers each carry a monthly spend cap; see the [per-tier spend caps](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#spend-limits) for current values. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#spend-limits
- [definition] Monitoring and logging — AWS CloudTrail can capture all requests to Claude Platform on AWS. Workspace, external key, compliance, vault, and webhook operations are logged as Management events by default. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#monitoring-and-logging
- [definition] Request IDs — Each response includes two request IDs in the response headers: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#request-ids
- [definition] Migrating from Amazon Bedrock — If you currently use Claude on Bedrock, migrating to Claude Platform on AWS requires changes throughout your integration. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#migrating-from-amazon-bedrock
- [definition] What changes — The migration delta depends on which Bedrock integration you're coming from. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#what-changes
- [definition] IAM policies — Claude Platform on AWS integrates with AWS IAM for access control. You grant or deny access to specific API actions on specific workspaces using standard IAM policy syntax. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#iam-policies
- [definition] Example: deny batch inference — The following policy allows real-time inference while blocking batch processing: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#example-deny-batch-inference
- [definition] Managed policies — AWS provides five managed policies (`AnthropicFullAccess`, `AnthropicReadOnlyAccess`, `AnthropicInferenceAccess`, `AnthropicLimitedAccess`, and `AnthropicSelfHostedEnvironmentAccess`) for common access patterns. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#managed-policies
- [concept] Claude Platform on AWS provides the full Anthropic platform experience including Messages API, Agent Skills, code execution, and beta features. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws
- [fact] Anthropic operates the inference stack for Claude Platform on AWS, whereas AWS operates the stack for Amazon Bedrock. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws
- [concept] AWS provides the authentication layer via SigV4 or API keys, IAM-based access control, and billing integration through AWS Marketplace. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws
- [fact] The Anthropic SDKs support Claude Platform on AWS. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws
- [concept] Anthropic acts as the data processor for inference inputs and outputs when using Claude through AWS. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#how-the-platform-integration-works
- [fact] AWS processes billing and identity metadata under the marketplace model. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#how-the-platform-integration-works
- [problem] Data might not reside in AWS, and inference might route to Anthropic's primary cloud. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#how-the-platform-integration-works
- [problem] Subservices might change without notice. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#how-the-platform-integration-works
- [actionable] Set the `inference_geo` parameter per request to pin inference to a specific geography. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#how-the-platform-integration-works
- [fact] Claude Platform on AWS follows the same data retention policy as the first-party Claude API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws#how-the-platform-integration-works

- [definition] Tool definition — The code execution tool requires no additional parameters: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#tool-definition
- [definition] Response format — The code execution tool can return two types of results depending on the operation: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#response-format
- [definition] Results — Bash command results (`bash_code_execution_result`) include: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#results
- [definition] Errors — Each tool type can return specific errors: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#errors
- [definition] `pause_turn` stop reason — The response might include a `pause_turn` stop reason, which indicates that the API paused a long-running turn. You may provide the response back as-is in a subsequent request to let Claude continue its turn, or modify the content if you want to interrupt the conversation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#pause-turn-stop-reason
- [definition] Containers — The code execution tool runs in a secure, containerized environment designed specifically for code execution, with a higher focus on Python. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#containers
- [definition] Pre-installed libraries — The sandboxed Python environment includes these commonly used libraries: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#pre-installed-libraries
- [definition] Container reuse — You can reuse an existing container across multiple API requests by providing the container ID from a previous response. This allows you to maintain created files between requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#container-reuse
- [definition] Using code execution with other execution tools — When you provide code execution alongside client-provided tools that also run code (such as a [Bash tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool) or custom REPL), Claude is operating in a multicomputer environment. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#using-code-execution-with-other-execution-tools
- [definition] Streaming — With [streaming](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming) enabled (`"stream": true`), you'll receive code execution events as they occur. The sub-tool input streams as `input_json_delta` events, and each result block arrives whole in a single `content_block_start` event: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#streaming
- [definition] Batch requests — You can include the code execution tool in the [Messages Batches API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing). Code execution tool calls through the Messages Batches API are priced the same as those in regular Messages API requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#batch-requests
- [definition] Upgrade to latest tool version — The latest tool version is `code_execution_20260521`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#upgrade-to-latest-tool-version
- [definition] Upgrade steps — To upgrade, update the tool type in your API requests: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#upgrade-steps
- [definition] Data retention — Code execution runs in server-side sandbox containers. Container data, including execution artifacts, uploaded files, and outputs, is retained for up to 30 days. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#data-retention

- [parameter] `type`: Type=string; Default=Required; Description=Must be `"compact_20260112"` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#parameters
- [parameter] `trigger`: Type=object; Default=`{"type": "input_tokens", "value": 150000}`; Description=When to trigger compaction. `input_tokens` is the only supported trigger type. `value` must be at least 50,000 tokens. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#parameters
- [parameter] `pause_after_compaction`: Type=boolean; Default=`false`; Description=Whether to pause after generating the compaction summary — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#parameters
- [parameter] `instructions`: Type=string; Default=`null`; Description=Custom summarization prompt. Completely replaces the default prompt when provided. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#parameters
- [definition] How compaction works — When compaction is enabled, Claude automatically summarizes your conversation when it reaches the configured token threshold. The API: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#how-compaction-works
- [definition] Basic usage — Enable compaction by adding the `compact_20260112` strategy to `context_management.edits` in your Messages API request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#basic-usage
- [definition] Trigger configuration — Configure when compaction triggers using the `trigger` parameter: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#trigger-configuration
- [definition] Custom summarization instructions — The default summarization prompt varies by model. Each default instructs Claude to write a summary inside `<summary></summary>` tags with the information needed to continue the task in a future context window. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#custom-summarization-instructions
- [definition] Pausing after compaction — Use `pause_after_compaction` to pause the API after generating the compaction summary. This allows you to add additional content blocks (such as preserving recent messages or specific instruction-oriented messages) before the API continues with the response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#pausing-after-compaction
- [definition] Working with compaction blocks — When compaction is triggered, the API returns a `compaction` block at the start of the assistant response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#working-with-compaction-blocks
- [definition] Passing compaction blocks back — You must pass the `compaction` block back to the API on subsequent requests to continue the conversation with the shortened prompt. The simplest approach is to append the entire response content to your messages: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#passing-compaction-blocks-back
- [definition] Streaming — The compaction block streams differently from text blocks. You receive a `content_block_start` event, followed by a single `content_block_delta` with the complete summary content (no intermediate streaming), and then a `content_block_stop` event. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#streaming
- [definition] Prompt caching — Compaction works well with [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching). You can add a `cache_control` breakpoint on compaction blocks to cache the summarized content. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#prompt-caching
- [definition] Understanding usage — Compaction requires an additional sampling step, which contributes to rate limits and billing. The API returns detailed usage information in the response: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#understanding-usage
- [definition] Server tools — When using server tools (such as web search), the compaction trigger is checked at the start of each sampling iteration. Compaction might occur multiple times within a single request depending on your trigger threshold and the amount of output generated. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#server-tools
- [definition] Token counting — The token counting endpoint (`/v1/messages/count_tokens`) applies existing `compaction` blocks in your prompt but does not trigger new compactions. Use it to check your effective token count after previous compactions: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#token-counting
- [definition] Examples — Here's a complete example of a long-running conversation with compaction: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#examples

- [definition] Combining with thinking — For combining computer use with thinking, see [Thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#combining-with-thinking
- [definition] Augmenting computer use with other tools — To add other tools alongside computer use, include them in the same `tools` array. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#augmenting-computer-use-with-other-tools
- [definition] Build a custom computer use environment — The [reference implementation](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-quickstarts/tree/main/computer-use-demo) is meant to help you get started with computer use. It includes all of the components needed to have Claude use a computer. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#build-a-custom-computer-use-environment
- [definition] Implement the computer use tool — The computer use tool is implemented as a schema-less tool. When using this tool, you don't need to provide an input schema as with other tools; the schema is built into Claude's model and can't be modified. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#implement-the-computer-use-tool
- [definition] Set up your computing environment — Create a virtual display or connect to an existing display that Claude will interact with. This typically involves setting up Xvfb (X Virtual Framebuffer) or similar technology. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#implement-the-computer-use-tool
- [definition] Implement action handlers — Create functions to handle each action type that Claude might request: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#implement-the-computer-use-tool
- [definition] Process Claude's tool calls — Extract and run tool calls from Claude's responses: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#implement-the-computer-use-tool
- [definition] Implement the agent loop — Wrap the two previous steps in a loop that sends the results back and repeats until Claude returns no member tool calls; [Understand the agent loop](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#understanding-the-agentic-loop) shows this loop in each language. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#implement-the-computer-use-tool
- [definition] Handle errors — Report a failed action to Claude as a `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and a short description, and include `"toolset_name": "computer"` as on any other member result. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#handle-errors
- [definition] Size screenshots to fit image limits — Screenshots and zoom images that you return to the computer use toolset must already fit within your model's [image size limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision#evaluate-image-size): the toolset takes no display dimensions and the API doesn't downscale for you, so an… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#size-screenshots-to-fit-image-limits
- [definition] Manage screenshot history — Long agent loops accumulate screenshots quickly (roughly 1,000–1,800 input tokens each). The API's [request limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision#request-limits) also apply. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#manage-screenshot-history
- [definition] Diagnose click issues — If clicks miss their targets, the cause is usually one of the following: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#diagnose-click-issues
- [definition] Migrate from `computer_20251124` — Upgrading from `computer_20251124` to the toolset is optional: the models listed for `computer_20251124` under [Earlier tool versions](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#earlier-tool-versions) keep accepting it with its beta header, so an existing… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#migrate-from-computer-20251124
- [definition] Earlier tool versions — Two earlier versions of the computer use tool remain available in beta for existing integrations, for models that don't support the toolset, and on platforms where the toolset isn't currently available. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#earlier-tool-versions
- [definition] Limitations — 1. **Latency:** The current computer use latency for human-AI interactions might be too slow compared to regular human-directed computer actions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#limitations
- [definition] Data retention — Computer use is a client-side tool. All screenshots, mouse actions, keyboard inputs, and any files involved in a session are captured and stored in your environment, not by Anthropic. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#data-retention
- [definition] Pricing — Computer use follows the standard [tool use pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview#pricing). When using the computer use tool: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#pricing
