- [definition] Cache hits drop after changing thinking settings — `cache_read_input_tokens` falls to zero on requests that previously hit the cache. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-troubleshooting#cache-hits-drop-after-changing-thinking-settings
- [definition] Setting effort does not change thinking — You change `effort` but thinking frequency or depth stays the same. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-troubleshooting#setting-effort-does-not-change-thinking

## Claude calls the wrong tool
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use>

- [parameter] Claude calls tool A when you wanted tool B: Likely cause=Description ambiguity; Fix=Sharpen descriptions. Differentiate tools by WHEN to use them, not only WHAT they do. See [Define tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/define-tools). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#claude-calls-the-wrong-tool
- [parameter] Claude never calls your tool: Likely cause=Tool name collision or overly-generic schema; Fix=Check for duplicate names across your tool list. Add `input_examples` to make the intended use concrete. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#claude-calls-the-wrong-tool
- [parameter] Claude calls with wrong parameter types: Likely cause=Model guessing at ambiguous schema; Fix=Add `strict: true` (if your schema is in the supported subset) or add `input_examples`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#claude-calls-the-wrong-tool
- [parameter] Parameter that doesn't exist in your schema: Likely cause=Model over-generation without strict mode; Fix=Add `strict: true` if your schema is in the [supported subset](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/strict-tool-use). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#claude-invents-tool-parameters
- [parameter] Parameter values outside your enum: Likely cause=Missing strict mode or too-large enum; Fix=Shrink the enum or add `input_examples` showing valid choices. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#claude-invents-tool-parameters
- [parameter] Claude calls tools sequentially when parallel would be better: Likely cause=Message history formatting; Fix=Send multiple `tool_result` blocks in ONE user message, not one per turn. See [Parallel tool use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/parallel-tool-use). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#parallel-tool-calls-dont-work
- [parameter] `disable_parallel_tool_use` seems ignored: Likely cause=Set too late in the conversation; Fix=Must be set on the request that returns `tool_use`. Setting it on a later request has no effect on earlier tool calls. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#parallel-tool-calls-dont-work
- [parameter] Every request is a cache miss: Likely cause=`tool_choice`, the thinking configuration, or `output_config.effort` varying between requests; Fix=Keep `tool_choice` stable or place the `cache_control` breakpoint before the variation point; hold the thinking configuration and effort level constant for the life of a cached conversation. See [Tool use with prompt… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#cache-keeps-invalidating
- [parameter] Adding a tool mid-conversation breaks cache: Likely cause=Tool prepended to the tools array; Fix=Use `defer_loading: true` with tool search to append the tool inline instead of modifying the array head. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#cache-keeps-invalidating
- [parameter] `tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after`: Cause=Missing `tool_result` for some `tool_use` ids, or `tool_result` is not the first content block in the user message; Fix=Return one `tool_result` for every `tool_use` block in the assistant response. Put `tool_result` blocks before any text. See [Handle tool… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#errors-at-request-time
- [parameter] `was found without a corresponding <name>_tool_result block`: Cause=The previous assistant turn has a `server_tool_use` block with no result block (most often, Claude called it alongside a client tool), and either your next user message ended that turn (for example, with text after the `tool_result` blocks) or the resume request no longer defines that server tool (the message then ends with `but… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#errors-at-request-time
- [parameter] `Unsupported regex feature in pattern field: ...`: Cause=A `pattern` in a strict tool's `input_schema` uses a regex feature that strict mode can't compile, such as a backreference, a lookaround, a word boundary, or a large `{n,m}` range; Fix=Simplify the pattern. Anchored patterns with basic quantifiers, character classes, and groups are supported; see [JSON Schema… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#errors-at-request-time
- [parameter] `All tools have defer_loading: true`: Cause=No tools visible to the model; Fix=At least one tool must be immediately loaded. The tool search tool itself must never have `defer_loading: true`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#errors-at-request-time
- [parameter] Claude refuses to act on a tool result, or asks the user to confirm instructions that came from it: Likely cause=Your own instructions are being delivered inside the `tool_result` content; Fix=Claude is trained to treat instructions inside tool results as potentially untrusted third-party content. Move your instructions out of the tool result: send them in a `user` turn after the `tool_result`… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#claude-flags-tool-results-as-prompt-injection
- [parameter] String comparison on tool inputs fails with newer models: Cause=Unicode and forward-slash escaping differs between model versions; Fix=Parse with `json.loads()` or `JSON.parse()`. Never do raw string matching on serialized input. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#json-escaping-differences-opus-46
- [definition] Error: thinking blocks cannot be modified — If a request fails with a 400 `invalid_request_error` whose message contains `` `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified `` when continuing a conversation after a tool call, your application is altering the assistant's thinking blocks before… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/troubleshooting-tool-use#error-thinking-blocks-cannot-be-modified

- [definition] Ring 1: Single tool, single turn — The smallest possible tool-using program: one tool, one user message, one tool call, one result. The code is heavily commented so you can map each line to the [tool use lifecycle](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/how-tool-use-works). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/build-a-tool-using-agent#ring-1-single-tool-single-turn
- [definition] Ring 2: The agentic loop — Ring 1 assumed Claude would call the tool exactly once. Real tasks often need several calls: Claude might create an event, read the confirmation, then create another. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/build-a-tool-using-agent#ring-2-the-agentic-loop
- [definition] Ring 3: Multiple tools, parallel calls — Agents rarely have just one capability. Add a second tool, `list_calendar_events`, so Claude can check the existing schedule before creating something new. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/build-a-tool-using-agent#ring-3-multiple-tools-parallel-calls
- [definition] Ring 4: Error handling — Tools fail. A calendar API might reject an event with too many attendees, or a date might be malformed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/build-a-tool-using-agent#ring-4-error-handling
- [definition] Ring 5: The Tool Runner SDK abstraction — Rings 2 through 4 wrote the same loop by hand: call the API, check `stop_reason`, run tools, append results, repeat. The Tool Runner does this for you. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/build-a-tool-using-agent#ring-5-the-tool-runner-sdk-abstraction
- [definition] What you built — You started with a single hardcoded tool call and ended with a production-shaped agent that handles multiple tools, parallel calls, and errors, then collapsed all of that into the Tool Runner. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/build-a-tool-using-agent#what-you-built

- [parameter] **Skill IDs**: Anthropic Skills=Short names: `pptx`, `xlsx`, `docx`, `pdf`; Custom Skills=Generated: `skill_01AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUv` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#using-skills
- [parameter] **Version format**: Anthropic Skills=Date-based: `20251013` or `latest`; Custom Skills=Version ID: `skver_01AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUv` or `latest` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#using-skills
- [parameter] **Management**: Anthropic Skills=Pre-built and maintained by Anthropic; Custom Skills=Upload and manage through the [Skills API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/skills/create) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#using-skills
- [parameter] **Availability**: Anthropic Skills=Available to all users; Custom Skills=Private to your workspace — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#using-skills
- [parameter] Skill label: With `skills-2025-10-02`=`display_title` (up to 64 characters, unique per workspace); Without the header=`display_name` (up to 255 characters, not unique); derived from the `SKILL.md` `name` when omitted — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] Newest version pointer: With `skills-2025-10-02`=`latest_version`, an epoch-microsecond string such as `"1759178010641129"`; Without the header=`latest_version_id`, a version ID such as `"skver_01AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUv"`; `GET /v1/skills/{skill_id}/versions/latest` resolves it in one call — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] Version identifier in URLs: With `skills-2025-10-02`=Epoch-microsecond string; Without the header=Version ID (`skver_...`). IDs captured under the beta with the `skill_version_` prefix are accepted as input. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] Version object: With `skills-2025-10-02`=Includes `directory` (always equal to the Skill `name`); Without the header=No `directory` field — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] `source`: With `skills-2025-10-02`=A string, `"custom"` or `"anthropic"`; Without the header=An object, for example `{"type": "custom"}`; the example catalog value is `"anthropic_example"` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] List responses: With `skills-2025-10-02`=`{ data, has_more, next_page }`; Without the header=`{ data, next_page }`; `limit` from 1 to 1,000 (default 20) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] Versions list order: With `skills-2025-10-02`=Oldest first; Without the header=Newest first, default `limit` 20. Page cursors from one shape are not valid on the other. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] Deleting a Skill: With `skills-2025-10-02`=Returns a 400 error while any version exists; Without the header=Deletes the Skill and all of its versions — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] Deleting a Skill's only version: With `skills-2025-10-02`=Allowed, leaving a Skill with no versions; Without the header=Returns a 400 error; upload a replacement version first, or delete the Skill — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] Upload layout: With `skills-2025-10-02`=Files must sit inside a top-level directory whose name matches the Skill `name`; Without the header=`SKILL.md` may sit at the root of the upload; stored paths are the same either way — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [parameter] Response types: With `skills-2025-10-02`=`CreateSkillResponse`, `GetSkillResponse`, and one type per operation; Without the header=`Skill`, `SkillVersion`, `DeletedSkill`, `DeletedSkillVersion` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [definition] Overview — For a detailed look at the architecture and real-world applications of Agent Skills, read the engineering blog post: [Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#overview
- [definition] Using Skills — Skills integrate identically in the Messages API regardless of source. You specify Skills in the `container` parameter with a `skill_id`, `type`, and optional `version`, and they run in the code execution environment. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#using-skills
- [definition] Container parameter — Skills are specified using the `container` parameter in the Messages API. You can include up to 20 Skills for each request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#container-parameter
- [definition] Downloading generated files — When Skills create documents (Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, Word), they return `file_id` attributes in the response. You must use the Files API to download these files. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#downloading-generated-files
- [definition] Multi-turn conversations — The response's `container` object carries the container's `id` and `expires_at` timestamp (see [Container reuse](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#container-reuse) for lifetime details). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#multi-turn-conversations
- [definition] Long-running operations — Skills may perform operations that require multiple turns. Handle `pause_turn` stop reasons: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#long-running-operations
- [definition] Using multiple Skills — Combine multiple Skills in a single request to handle complex workflows: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#using-multiple-skills
- [definition] Creating a Skill — A Skill bundle is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file at the top level with `name` and `description` YAML frontmatter, plus any supporting scripts or resources. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#creating-a-skill
- [definition] Listing Skills — Retrieve all Skills available to your workspace, including both Anthropic pre-built Skills and your custom Skills. Use the `source` parameter to filter by skill type: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#listing-skills
- [definition] Deleting a Skill — Deleting a Skill also removes all of its versions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#deleting-a-skill
- [definition] Versioning — Skills support versioning to manage updates safely: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#versioning
- [definition] Use cases — Skills fit both organizational and personal work. Organizations use them to apply brand formatting to documents, structure notes and reports around company templates, and run company-specific analytical procedures. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#use-cases
- [definition] Example: financial modeling — Combine Excel and custom DCF analysis Skills: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#example-financial-modeling
- [definition] Environment constraints — Skills run in the code execution container with these limitations: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#environment-constraints
- [definition] When to use multiple Skills — Combine Skills when tasks involve multiple document types or domains: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#when-to-use-multiple-skills
- [definition] Version management strategy — The SDK tabs in this section show the `container` value to include in a Messages request. The cURL and CLI tabs show the full request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#version-management-strategy
- [definition] Prompt caching considerations — If you use [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching), changing the Skills list in your container breaks the cache. Skills render into the system prompt in a fixed order, so the same list produces the same cacheable prefix: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#prompt-caching-considerations
- [definition] Migrate from `skills-2025-10-02` — The Skills API is out of beta and needs no beta header. Migrating off `skills-2025-10-02` is optional: requests that still send it keep working and keep returning the beta response shapes, so an existing integration keeps working until you change it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#migrate-from-skills-2025-10-02
- [definition] SDK beta namespace — Starting with Python SDK 1.2.0, TypeScript SDK 0.122.0, Go SDK 1.68.0, Java SDK 2.59.0, Ruby SDK 1.67.0, and C# SDK 12.44.0, `client.beta.skills` no longer sends `skills-2025-10-02` and returns the same shapes as `client.skills`, with `Beta`-prefixed type names (`BetaSkill`, `BetaSkillVersion`… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#sdk-beta-namespace
- [definition] Data retention — Agent Skills are not covered by ZDR arrangements. Skill definitions and execution data are retained according to Anthropic's standard data retention policy. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#data-retention
- [definition] Audit logging — If your organization has the [Compliance API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api) enabled, its [Activity Feed](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed) records the creation and deletion of Skills and Skill versions made with a Claude… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#audit-logging

- [definition] Limitations — Although Claude's image understanding capabilities are cutting-edge, there are some limitations to be aware of: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision#limitations

- [definition] How web fetch works — Web fetch is a [server tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools): the API fetches the content during the request and inserts the results into the conversation. You don't run anything or return a `tool_result`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#how-web-fetch-works
- [definition] When Claude fetches — Claude fetches when the request points at a specific page or document: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#when-claude-fetches
- [definition] Dynamic filtering — Fetching full web pages and PDFs can quickly consume tokens, especially when only specific information is needed from large documents. With `web_fetch_20260209` or later, Claude can write and execute code to filter the fetched content before loading it into context. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#dynamic-filtering
- [definition] How to use web fetch — Provide the web fetch tool in your API request: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#how-to-use-web-fetch
- [definition] Tool definition — The web fetch tool supports the following parameters: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#tool-definition
- [definition] Max uses — The `max_uses` parameter limits the number of web fetches performed. Failed fetches count against the limit. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#max-uses
- [definition] Domain filtering — For domain filtering with `allowed_domains` and `blocked_domains`, see [Server tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools#domain-filtering). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#domain-filtering
- [definition] Content limits — The `max_content_tokens` parameter limits the amount of content included in the context. If the fetched content exceeds this limit, the tool truncates it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#content-limits
- [definition] Cache bypass — Requires `web_fetch_20260309` or later (including `web_fetch_20260318`). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#cache-bypass
- [definition] Citations — Unlike web search where citations are always enabled, citations are optional for web fetch and disabled by default. Set `"citations": {"enabled": true}` to enable Claude to cite specific passages from fetched documents. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#citations
- [definition] Errors — When the web fetch tool encounters an error, the Claude API returns a 200 (success) response with the error represented in the response body. Claude sees the error result and continues the turn. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#errors
- [definition] URL validation — For security reasons, the web fetch tool can only fetch URLs that have previously appeared in the conversation context. This includes: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#url-validation
- [definition] Combined search and fetch — When both the web search and web fetch tools are enabled, and the user names a specific page or document without providing a URL (for example, "read the README from the anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python repository"), Claude uses web search to locate it, then fetches the result. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#combined-search-and-fetch
- [definition] Prompt caching — For caching tool definitions across turns, see [Tool use with prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#prompt-caching
- [definition] Streaming — With streaming enabled, fetch events are part of the stream with a pause during content retrieval: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#streaming
- [definition] Batch requests — You can include the web fetch tool in the [Messages Batches API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing). Web fetch tool calls through the Messages Batches API are priced the same as those in regular Messages API requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#batch-requests
- [definition] Usage and pricing — Web fetch usage has **no additional charges** beyond standard token costs: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#usage-and-pricing

- [definition] How web search works — When you add the web search tool to your API request: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#how-web-search-works
- [definition] When Claude searches — Claude searches when the request depends on information that is current, changing, or outside its training data: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#when-claude-searches
- [definition] Dynamic filtering — With basic web search, every search result is loaded into Claude's context window, and much of that content can be irrelevant to the request. With `web_search_20260209` or later, Claude instead writes and runs code that filters the results first, so only relevant content reaches the context window. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#dynamic-filtering
- [definition] How to use web search — Web search is enabled for your organization unless an administrator has disabled it in the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/settings/privacy), where they can also restrict which domains it searches. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#how-to-use-web-search
- [definition] Tool definition — The web search tool supports the following parameters: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#tool-definition
- [definition] Max uses — The `max_uses` parameter limits the number of searches performed. If Claude attempts more searches than allowed, the `web_search_tool_result` is an error with the `max_uses_exceeded` error code. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#max-uses
- [definition] Domain filtering — Provide `allowed_domains` or `blocked_domains`, not both. If a request includes both, the API returns a 400 error. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#domain-filtering
- [definition] Localization — The `user_location` parameter allows you to localize search results based on a user's location. Provide at least one of `city`, `region`, `country`, or `timezone`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#localization
- [definition] Response inclusion — Requires `web_search_20260318` or later. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#response-inclusion
- [definition] Citations — Citations are always enabled for web search, and each `web_search_result_location` includes: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#citations
- [definition] Errors — When the web search tool encounters an error (such as hitting rate limits), the Claude API still returns a 200 (success) response. The error is represented within the response body using the following structure: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#errors
- [definition] `pause_turn` stop reason — The API can pause a long-running search turn and return `stop_reason: "pause_turn"`. To continue, send the paused assistant message back unchanged in a new request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#pause-turn-stop-reason
- [definition] Prompt caching — For caching tool definitions across turns, see [Tool use with prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#prompt-caching
- [definition] Streaming — With streaming enabled, you'll receive search events as part of the stream. There will be a pause while the search runs: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#streaming
- [definition] Batch requests — You can include the web search tool in the [Messages Batches API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing). Web search tool calls through the Messages Batches API are priced the same as those in regular Messages API requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#batch-requests
- [definition] Usage and pricing — Web search usage is charged in addition to token usage: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#usage-and-pricing

## Core concepts
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview>

- [parameter] **What it is**: Messages API=Direct model prompting access; Claude Managed Agents=Pre-built, configurable agent harness that runs in managed infrastructure — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview
- [parameter] **Best for**: Messages API=Custom agent loops and fine-grained control; Claude Managed Agents=Long-running tasks and asynchronous work — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview
- [parameter] **Agent**: The model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, and skills — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#core-concepts
- [parameter] **Environment**: Configuration for where sessions run: an Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox, or a self-hosted sandbox on your own infrastructure — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#core-concepts
- [parameter] **Session**: A running agent instance within an environment, performing a specific task and generating outputs — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#core-concepts
- [parameter] **Events**: Messages exchanged between your application and the agent (user turns, tool results, status updates) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#core-concepts
- [definition] Core concepts — Claude Managed Agents is built around four concepts: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#core-concepts
- [definition] Create an agent — Define the model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, and skills. Create the agent once and reference it by ID across sessions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#how-it-works
- [definition] Create an environment — Configure where the agent runs: a cloud sandbox, or a [self-hosted sandbox](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes) on your own infrastructure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#how-it-works
- [definition] Start a session — Launch a session that references your agent and environment configuration. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#how-it-works
- [definition] Send events and stream responses — Send user messages as events. Claude autonomously runs tools and streams back results through server-sent events (SSE). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#how-it-works
- [definition] Steer or interrupt — Send additional user events to guide the agent mid-execution, or interrupt it to change direction. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#how-it-works
- [definition] When to use Claude Managed Agents — Claude Managed Agents is best for workloads that need: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#when-to-use-claude-managed-agents
- [definition] Supported tools — Claude Managed Agents gives Claude access to a set of built-in tools: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#supported-tools
- [definition] Beta access — Claude Managed Agents is in beta. All Managed Agents endpoints require the `managed-agents-2026-04-01` beta header. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview#beta-access

- [parameter] Create credential: If you provide the object, any field you omit inside it defaults to `false`: `{"header": true}` creates a header-only credential. Omit the object entirely and both locations are enabled. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#add-a-credential
- [parameter] Update credential: Fields merge individually: `{"body": false}` disables body substitution and leaves `header` unchanged. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#add-a-credential
- [parameter] `vault.archived`: Vault archived. A `vault_credential.archived` event is also emitted for each underlying credential. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#credential-lifecycle
- [parameter] `vault.deleted`: Vault deleted. A `vault_credential.deleted` event is also emitted for each underlying credential. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#credential-lifecycle
- [parameter] `vault_credential.archived`: Credential archived, either directly or as a result of vault archival. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#credential-lifecycle
- [parameter] `vault_credential.deleted`: Credential deleted, either directly or as a result of vault deletion. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#credential-lifecycle
- [parameter] `vault_credential.refresh_failed`: An `mcp_oauth` credential cannot be refreshed (invalid refresh token, or irrecoverable error from the OAuth server). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#credential-lifecycle
- [definition] Create a vault — Vaults and credentials are workspace-scoped, meaning any API key with workspace access can reference them when creating a session. To revoke access, delete the vault or credential. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#create-a-vault
- [definition] Add a credential — Two credential categories are supported: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#add-a-credential
- [definition] Reference the vault at session creation — Pass `vault_ids` when creating a session: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#reference-the-vault-at-session-creation
- [definition] Rotate a credential — Secret values, `display_name`, and (on environment variable credentials) `injection_location` can be updated. `injection_location` updates merge per field, as described in the Environment variable tab of [Add a credential](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#add-a-credential). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#rotate-a-credential
- [definition] Credential lifecycle — Credentials are re-resolved periodically, both during a session and during the vault lifecycle. This ensures that credential rotation, archival, or deletion propagates to running sessions without a restart. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#credential-lifecycle
- [definition] Diagnose an OAuth refresh failure — To diagnose why a refresh failed, call `POST /v1/vaults/{vault_id}/credentials/{credential_id}/mcp_oauth_validate` (or `client.beta.vaults.credentials.mcp_oauth_validate(...)` in the SDK). This lets you decide how to handle the failure; the right action depends on the error type. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults#diagnose-an-oauth-refresh-failure

- [parameter] `limited`: Restricts sandbox network access to the hosts in `allowed_hosts`. Set `allow_package_managers` and `allow_mcp_servers` to `true` to allow additional access. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/environments#networking

- [definition] Packages — The `packages` field pre-installs packages into the sandbox before the agent starts. - [definition] Networking — The `networking` field controls the sandbox's outbound network access. It does not affect the `web_search` or `web_fetch` tools, which run on Anthropic's servers; to restrict the sites those tools can reach, set `allowed_domains` or `blocked_domains` on the tool's entry in the agent toolset. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/environments#networking
- [definition] Pre-installed runtimes — Cloud sandboxes include common language runtimes, databases, and command-line tools out of the box. - [parameter] `satisfied`: Session transitions to `idle`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#outcome-evaluation-end
- [parameter] `needs_revision`: Agent starts a new iteration cycle. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#outcome-evaluation-end
- [parameter] `max_iterations_reached`: One final acknowledgment turn follows before the session transitions to `idle`. No further evaluation runs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#outcome-evaluation-end
- [parameter] `failed`: Session transitions to `idle`. Returned when the rubric does not apply to the deliverables, for example if the description and rubric contradict each other. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#outcome-evaluation-end
- [parameter] `interrupted`: Emitted when the session is interrupted while an outcome is active, even if evaluation hadn't started yet. If no `outcome_evaluation_start` fired before the interrupt, `outcome_evaluation_start_id` is an empty string. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#outcome-evaluation-end
- [definition] Create a rubric — A rubric is a markdown document describing per-criterion scoring. The rubric is required. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#create-a-rubric
- [definition] Create a session with an outcome — The following examples create a [session](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions) for an existing [agent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup) and [environment](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/environments) (both created… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#create-a-session-with-an-outcome
- [definition] Outcome events — Progress on an outcome-oriented session is surfaced on the events [stream](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#outcome-events
- [definition] Define outcome user event — Only one outcome is supported at a time, but you may chain outcomes in sequence. To do this, send a new `user.define_outcome` event after the terminal `span.outcome_evaluation_end` event of the previous outcome. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#define-outcome-user-event
- [definition] Outcome evaluation start — Emitted once the grader starts an evaluation over one iteration loop. The `iteration` field is a 0-indexed revision counter: `0` is the first evaluation, `1` is the re-evaluation after the first revision, and so on. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#outcome-evaluation-start
- [definition] Outcome evaluation ongoing — Heartbeat emitted while the grader runs. The grader's internal reasoning is opaque: you see that it's working, not what it's thinking. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#outcome-evaluation-ongoing
- [definition] Outcome evaluation end — Emitted when an outcome evaluation cycle ends: after the grader finishes evaluating one iteration, or when the session is interrupted while an outcome is active. The `result` field indicates what happens next. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#outcome-evaluation-end
- [definition] Check outcome status — You can either listen on the [event stream](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming) for `span.outcome_evaluation_end`, or poll `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}` and read `outcome_evaluations[].result`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#check-outcome-status
- [definition] Retrieve deliverables — The agent writes output files to `/mnt/session/outputs/` inside the sandbox. To retrieve them, list files through the [Files API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files) with the session ID as the `scope_id`, then download them by ID. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes#retrieve-deliverables

- [parameter] `name`: Required. A human-readable name for the agent. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-configuration-fields
- [parameter] `model`: Required. The Claude [model](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview) that powers the agent. Accepts a model ID string or an object, for example `{"id": "claude-opus-5"}`. Claude 4.5 and later models are supported. The object form also accepts `speed`, `effort`, and `inference_geo` fields; see the tips under [Create an… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-configuration-fields
- [parameter] `system`: A [system prompt](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#give-claude-a-role) that defines the agent's behavior and persona. The system prompt is distinct from [user messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types), which should describe the work to be done. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-configuration-fields
- [parameter] `tools`: The tools available to the agent. Combines [pre-built agent tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools), [MCP tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector), and [custom tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#custom-tools). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-configuration-fields
- [parameter] `mcp_servers`: [MCP servers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector) that provide standardized third-party capabilities. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-configuration-fields
- [parameter] `skills`: [Skills](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/skills) that supply domain-specific context with progressive disclosure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-configuration-fields
- [parameter] `multiagent`: A coordinator declaration listing the agents this agent can delegate to. See [Multiagent orchestration](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-configuration-fields
- [parameter] `description`: A description of what the agent does. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-configuration-fields
- [parameter] `metadata`: Arbitrary key-value pairs for your own tracking. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-configuration-fields
- [parameter] **Update**: Generates a new agent version when the configuration changes. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-lifecycle
- [parameter] **List versions**: Returns the full version history so you can track changes over time. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-lifecycle
- [parameter] **Archive**: Makes the agent read-only. New sessions cannot reference it, but existing sessions continue to run. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#agent-lifecycle
- [definition] Create an agent — The following example defines a coding agent that uses Claude Opus 5 with access to the pre-built agent toolset. The toolset lets the agent write code, read files, search the web, and more. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#create-an-agent
- [definition] Pin the inference geo — Like `speed` and `effort`, `inference_geo` is set through the object form of `model`: pass `model` as an object and set `inference_geo` alongside `id`. The field accepts `"us"` or `"global"`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#pin-the-inference-geo
- [definition] Update an agent — Updating an agent generates a new version when the configuration changes. The `version` field is optional: supply it for optimistic concurrency (a mismatch returns a 409), or omit it to apply the update unconditionally (last write wins). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#update-an-agent
- [definition] List versions — Fetch the full version history to track how an agent has changed over time. Results are paginated, and the SDK examples fetch every page automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#list-versions
- [definition] Archive an agent — Archiving makes the agent read-only and cannot be undone. Existing sessions continue to run, but new sessions cannot reference the agent. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#archive-an-agent

- [parameter] `pending`: Dream successfully created and queued. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#lifecycle
- [parameter] `running`: The pipeline is processing. `usage` updates as work progresses. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#lifecycle
- [parameter] `completed`: Finished successfully. The `outputs[]` value is the new memory store. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#lifecycle
- [parameter] `failed`: Dreaming run ended with an error. The output memory store is left as-is with whatever was written before failure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#lifecycle
- [parameter] `canceled`: Dreaming run canceled. The output memory store is left as-is. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#lifecycle
- [parameter] `timeout`: The pipeline exceeded its runtime budget. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#errors
- [parameter] `internal_error`: Unclassified pipeline failure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#errors
- [parameter] `memory_store_org_limit_exceeded`: Your organization hit its memory-store cap while the pipeline was provisioning working storage. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#errors
- [parameter] `input_memory_store_too_large`: The input memory store exceeds the pipeline's size limit. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#errors
- [parameter] `input_memory_store_unavailable`: The input memory store was archived or deleted after the dream was created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#errors
- [parameter] `input_session_unavailable`: An input session was deleted after the dream was created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#errors
- [parameter] Sessions per dream: 100 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#limits
- [parameter] `instructions` length: 4,096 characters — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#limits
- [parameter] Supported models: `claude-opus-5`, `claude-fable-5`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#limits
- [definition] How it works — A **dream** is an asynchronous job that takes: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#how-it-works
- [definition] Steer with instructions — The optional `instructions` field steers what the dreaming pipeline synthesizes. It is applied throughout the pipeline: what to read closely, what to merge or drop, and how to structure the output store. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#steer-with-instructions
- [definition] Track progress — Dreams run asynchronously and typically take minutes to a few hours, driven by the number of input transcripts. Poll the dream by ID to check status: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#track-progress
- [definition] Watch the pipeline run — Once a dream is `running`, its `session_id` field points at the underlying [session](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions) running the pipeline. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#watch-the-pipeline-run
- [definition] Use the output — When `status` reaches `completed`, the `memory_store` entry in `outputs[]` references a fully populated store. It's an ordinary memory store in your workspace. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#use-the-output
- [definition] Cancel a dream — Cancel moves a `pending` or `running` dream to `canceled` immediately. Canceling an already-`canceled` dream is an idempotent no-op; canceling a `completed` or `failed` dream returns 400. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#cancel-a-dream
- [definition] Archive a dream — Archive sets `archived_at` on a dream that has reached a terminal state (`completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`); `status` is left unchanged. Archived dreams are excluded from default list responses but remain readable by ID. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#archive-a-dream
- [definition] List dreams — Returns all non-archived dreams in the workspace, newest first. Use `limit` (default 20, max 100) and the `page` cursor to paginate. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#list-dreams
- [definition] Errors — A non-exhaustive list of possible dreaming errors follows. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#errors
- [definition] Billing — Dreams are billed at standard API token rates for the model you select; `usage` on the resource reports the exact totals. Cost scales roughly linearly with the number and length of input sessions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams#billing

- [parameter] `type`: Required. Must be `"url"`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#mcp-servers-field-reference
- [parameter] `name`: Required. A unique name for this server within the agent (1–255 characters). Used as the `mcp_server_name` in the `tools` array and surfaced on MCP tool events in the [session event stream](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#mcp-servers-field-reference
- [parameter] `url`: Required. The endpoint of the remote MCP server (up to 2,048 characters). See [Supported MCP server types](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#supported-mcp-server-types) for transport requirements. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#mcp-servers-field-reference
- [parameter] `mcp_connection_failed_error`: The MCP server could not be reached (network error, timeout, or non-authentication HTTP failure). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#handle-connection-and-authentication-failures
- [parameter] `mcp_authentication_failed_error`: Authentication with the MCP server failed: the server rejected the credential from the attached vault, required authentication when no matching credential was configured, or an OAuth token refresh failed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#handle-connection-and-authentication-failures
- [definition] Declare MCP servers on the agent — Specify MCP servers in the `mcp_servers` array when creating an agent. Each server needs a `type`, a unique `name`, and a `url`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#declare-mcp-servers-on-the-agent
- [definition] `mcp_servers` field reference — Each entry in the `mcp_servers` array defines one connection. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#mcp-servers-field-reference
- [definition] Configure which MCP tools are available — The `mcp_toolset` entry supports a `default_config` object and a `configs` array, applied to the tools the MCP server exposes. Each `configs` entry accepts only `name`, `enabled`, and `permission_policy`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#configure-which-mcp-tools-are-available
- [definition] MCP tool output handling — When an MCP tool output exceeds 100,000 characters (about 25,000 tokens), it is automatically written to a file in the sandbox. The model receives a truncated preview with the file path and can read the full content from there. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#mcp-tool-output-handling
- [definition] Provide authentication at session creation — When starting a session, pass `vault_ids` to provide credentials for your MCP servers. Vaults are collections of credentials that you register once and reference by ID. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#provide-authentication-at-session-creation
- [definition] Handle connection and authentication failures — Session creation does not validate MCP connectivity or credentials. If an MCP server is unreachable or rejects the supplied credential, the session still starts and interaction remains possible. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector#handle-connection-and-authentication-failures

- [parameter] You provision your own sandbox for running agent-generated code.: The session sandbox handles code execution, file operations, and bash. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#what-you-stop-managing

- [parameter] Built-in tools run in your process against your filesystem: `{"type": "agent_toolset_20260401"}` runs the same tools inside the session sandbox against `/workspace`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#what-changes
- [parameter] `cwd`, `add_dirs` point at local paths: Upload or mount [files](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/files) as session resources. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#what-changes
- [parameter] `system_prompt` and the `CLAUDE.md` hierarchy: A single `system` string on the Agent. Each update that changes the agent produces a new server-side version; pin sessions to a specific version to promote or roll back without a deploy. - [parameter] `mcp_servers` configured and authenticated in one place: Declare servers on the Agent; provide credentials through a [Vault](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults) on the Session. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#what-changes
- [parameter] `permission_mode`, `can_use_tool`: Per-tool [`permission_policy`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies); send `user.tool_confirmation` events for `always_ask` tools. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#what-changes
- [parameter] Plan mode: Run a planning-only session first, then a second session to run the plan. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#features-that-move-to-your-client
- [parameter] Output styles, slash commands: Apply in your client before sending `user.message` or after receiving `agent.message`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#features-that-move-to-your-client
- [parameter] `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` hooks: Your client already sees every `agent.custom_tool_use` event before responding; put the logic there. For built-in tools, use `permission_policy: always_ask`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#features-that-move-to-your-client
- [parameter] `max_turns`: Count turns client-side. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#features-that-move-to-your-client
- [definition] From a Messages API agent loop — If you built an agent by calling `messages.create` in a `while` loop, running tool calls yourself, and appending results to the conversation history, most of that code goes away. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#from-a-messages-api-agent-loop
- [definition] From the Claude Agent SDK — If you built with the [Claude Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview), you're already working with agents, tools, and sessions as concepts. The difference is where they run: the SDK runs in a process you operate, while Managed Agents runs in Anthropic's infrastructure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#from-the-claude-agent-sdk
- [definition] Features that move to your client — The tradeoff for Anthropic running the agent loop is that a few things the SDK handled automatically become your client's responsibility. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#features-that-move-to-your-client
- [definition] Migration checklist — 1. [Create an environment](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/environments) with the networking and runtimes your agent needs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#migration-checklist
- [definition] Migrating between model versions — When a new Claude model is released, migrating a Claude Managed Agents integration is typically a one-field change: update `model` on your [agent definition](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup) and the change takes effect on the next session you create. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/migration#migrating-between-model-versions

- [parameter] `session.thread_created`: A thread was created. Includes `session_thread_id` and `agent_name`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#primary-thread-events
- [parameter] `session.thread_status_running`: A thread started activity. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#primary-thread-events
- [parameter] `session.thread_status_idle`: The agent associated with the thread is awaiting input. Includes a `stop_reason` indicating why the agent stopped. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#primary-thread-events
- [parameter] `session.thread_status_terminated`: A thread was archived or encountered a terminal error. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#primary-thread-events
- [parameter] `agent.thread_message_received`: On the primary thread, an agent sent a report or question to the coordinator. Includes `from_session_thread_id`, `from_agent_name`, and `content`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#primary-thread-events
- [parameter] `agent.thread_message_sent`: On the primary thread, the coordinator sent a task or follow-up message to another agent. Includes `to_session_thread_id`, `to_agent_name`, and `content`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#primary-thread-events
- [definition] How it works — All agents share the same sandbox, filesystem, and [vault credentials](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults), but each agent runs in its own **session thread**, a context-isolated event stream with its own conversation history. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#how-it-works
- [definition] What to delegate — Multiagent coordination is best suited for complex tasks that either require work across a variety of surfaces, or where multiple well-scoped tasks contribute to an overall goal. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#what-to-delegate
- [definition] Configure the coordinator — When [defining your agent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup), set `multiagent` to declare the roster of agents the coordinator can delegate to: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#configure-the-coordinator
- [definition] Give the session an advisor — An advisor entry in `multiagent.agents` gives the session's primary thread an **advisor**: a model it can consult mid-turn for strategic guidance, such as planning an approach, getting unstuck, or reviewing work before finishing. The entry has exactly two fields, `type` and `model`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#give-the-session-an-advisor
- [definition] Create the session — Create a session referencing the coordinator. The coordinator delegates to the agents in its roster as needed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#create-the-session
- [definition] Connect agents to MCP servers — MCP servers are agent-scoped (each agent definition declares its own servers and tools), while vault credentials are session-scoped (`vault_ids` passed at session creation apply to every thread). Two implications for your integration: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#connect-agents-to-mcp-servers
- [definition] Threads — The **session-level event stream** (`/v1/sessions/{session_id}/events/stream`) is considered the **primary thread**, containing a condensed view of all activity across all threads. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#threads
- [definition] Primary thread events — These events surface multiagent activity on the primary thread at `/v1/sessions/{session_id}/events/stream`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#primary-thread-events
- [definition] Session thread events — Critical events are proxied to the primary thread. However, you might still want to investigate a specific agent's reasoning and tool calls. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#session-thread-events
- [definition] Tool permissions and custom tools — If a subagent needs something from your client, such as [permission](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#tool-confirmation) to run an `always_ask` tool, or the [result of a custom… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#tool-permissions-and-custom-tools

- [parameter] `always_allow`: The tool executes automatically with no confirmation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies#permission-policy-types
- [parameter] `always_ask`: The session pauses and waits for your approval before executing. See [Respond to confirmation requests](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies#respond-to-confirmation-requests) for the event flow. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies#permission-policy-types
- [definition] Set a policy for a toolset — You set permission policies in the agent's `tools` configuration when you create the agent, and you can change them later by [updating the agent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#update-an-agent). Running sessions keep the toolset configuration they were created with. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies#set-a-policy-for-a-toolset
- [definition] Agent toolset permissions — When creating an agent, you can apply a policy to every tool in `agent_toolset_20260401` using `default_config.permission_policy`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies#agent-toolset-permissions
- [definition] MCP toolset permissions — MCP toolsets default to `always_ask`. This ensures that new tools added to an MCP server do not execute in your application without approval. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies#mcp-toolset-permissions
- [definition] Override an individual tool policy — Use the `configs` array to override the default for individual tools. The `name` values for the agent toolset are listed in [Available tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#available-tools). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies#override-an-individual-tool-policy
- [definition] Respond to confirmation requests — When the agent invokes a tool with an `always_ask` policy: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies#respond-to-confirmation-requests
- [definition] Custom tools — Permission policies do not apply to custom tools. When the agent invokes a custom tool, your application receives an `agent.custom_tool_use` event and is responsible for deciding whether to execute it before sending back a `user.custom_tool_result`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies#custom-tools

## Event types
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference>

- [parameter] `user.message`: A user message with text, image, or document content. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `user.interrupt`: Stop the agent mid-execution. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `user.custom_tool_result`: Response to a custom tool call from the agent. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `user.tool_confirmation`: Approve or deny an agent or MCP tool call when a permission policy requires confirmation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `user.define_outcome`: Define an [outcome](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes) for the agent to work toward. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `user.tool_result`: For sessions with `self_hosted` [environments](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes) only, your integration is responsible for providing `agent_toolset` results. The SDK helpers and CLI do this automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.message`: Agent response content blocks. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.thinking`: Signals the agent is making forward progress through extended thinking. This is a progress signal only and does not carry the thinking content. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.tool_use`: Agent invokes a pre-built agent tool (bash, file operations, and so on). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.tool_result`: Result of a pre-built agent tool execution. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.mcp_tool_use`: Agent invokes an MCP server tool. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.mcp_tool_result`: Result of an MCP tool execution. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.custom_tool_use`: Agent invokes one of your custom tools. Respond with a `user.custom_tool_result` event. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.thread_context_compacted`: Conversation history was compacted to fit the context window. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.thread_message_received`: In a [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) session, a message from another thread arrived on the thread whose stream carries this event; on the primary thread, an agent sent a report or question to the coordinator. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `agent.thread_message_sent`: In a [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) session, the thread whose stream carries this event sent a message to another thread; on the primary thread, the coordinator sent a task or follow-up message to another agent. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.status_running`: Agent is actively processing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.status_idle`: Agent finished its current task and is waiting for input. Includes a `stop_reason` indicating why the agent stopped. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.status_rescheduled`: A transient error occurred and the session is retrying automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.status_terminated`: Session ended, either because of an unrecoverable error or because it was archived. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.deleted`: Session was deleted. Terminates any active event stream; no further events are emitted for this session. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.updated`: Session update request changed at least one field. Includes only the fields that changed. Updates apply on the next turn. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.error`: An error occurred during processing. Includes a typed `error` object with a `retry_status`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.usage`: Snapshot of the session's cumulative usage and tracked list cost. Carries the session's usage totals and an echo of the session's [budget](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets), or `null` when the session has none. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.thread_created`: A [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) thread was created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.thread_status_running`: A session thread began executing. Every session emits this for its primary thread; in [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) sessions, child-thread transitions are also cross-posted to the primary stream. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.thread_status_idle`: A session thread finished its turn and is awaiting input. Includes `stop_reason`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.thread_status_rescheduled`: A session thread hit a transient error and is retrying automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `session.thread_status_terminated`: A session thread was archived or reached a terminal error. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `span.model_request_start`: A model inference call has started. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `span.model_request_end`: A model inference call has completed. Includes `model_usage` with token counts. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `span.outcome_evaluation_start`: [Outcome](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes) evaluation has started. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `span.outcome_evaluation_ongoing`: Heartbeat during an ongoing [outcome](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes) evaluation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `span.outcome_evaluation_end`: An [outcome](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes) evaluation cycle has completed. A `needs_revision` result means another cycle follows; `satisfied`, `max_iterations_reached`, `failed`, and `interrupted` are terminal. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `system.message`: Append privileged system-level context that applies to the accompanying turn and all subsequent turns. Supported on Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, and Claude Opus 5; on an unsupported primary model the event is rejected with `model_does_not_support_mid_conversation_system`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `event_start`: A previewed event has started generating. Carries the upcoming event's `type` and `id`. Stream-only and never persisted. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `event_delta`: Incremental content for a previewed event, identified by `event_id`. Stream-only and never persisted. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [parameter] `--environment-id`: The environment to poll for work. Also reads from `ANTHROPIC_ENVIRONMENT_ID`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#self-hosted-worker
- [parameter] `--environment-key`: Authenticates the worker with this environment. Also reads from `ANTHROPIC_ENVIRONMENT_KEY`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#self-hosted-worker
- [parameter] `--workdir`: Directory where skills are downloaded and tools read and write files. Defaults to `.` (the current directory); the system default working directory is `/workspace`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#self-hosted-worker
- [parameter] `--on-work`: Script to call for each claimed work item instead of running tools in-process. Receives session details as environment variables. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#self-hosted-worker
- [parameter] `--unrestricted-paths`: Allow the file tools to read and write paths outside `--workdir`. The workdir check is a guardrail for the file tools only, not a sandbox; it does not constrain bash. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#self-hosted-worker
- [parameter] `--max-idle`: How long to wait after the session goes idle with an `end_turn` [stop reason](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/handling-stop-reasons) before shutting down. Defaults to `60s`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#self-hosted-worker
- [parameter] `--log-format`: Log output format. Use `json` for structured log ingestion. Defaults to `text`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#self-hosted-worker
- [parameter] Create endpoints (such as agents, sessions, and environments): 300 requests per minute — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#rate-limits
- [parameter] Read endpoints (such as retrieve, list, and stream): 1,200 requests per minute — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#rate-limits
- [definition] Event types — Persisted event type strings follow a `{domain}.{action}` naming convention; the stream-only event deltas (see the Event deltas tab) are the exception. See [Session event stream](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming) for sending, streaming, and listing events. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types
- [definition] Self-hosted worker — These are the `ant beta:worker` CLI flags for the pre-built worker that drives a `self_hosted` environment. See [Self-hosted sandboxes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes) for setting up the environment, running a worker, and the SDK helper options. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#self-hosted-worker
- [definition] Supported MCP server types — Claude Managed Agents connects to [remote MCP servers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/remote-mcp-servers) that expose an HTTP endpoint, or to private MCP servers through [MCP tunnels](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#supported-mcp-server-types
- [definition] Rate limits — Managed Agents endpoints are rate-limited per organization: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#rate-limits
- [definition] Branding guidelines — For partners integrating Claude Managed Agents, use of Claude branding is optional. When referencing Claude in your product: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#branding-guidelines

- [definition] Create a scheduled deployment — When creating a deployment, you pass the [session configurations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions) required for execution, in addition to a `schedule`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#create-a-scheduled-deployment
- [definition] Set a budget on each run — Pass the optional `budget` object when you create or update the deployment. It takes the same shape as a [session budget](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#set-a-budget-on-each-run
- [definition] Deployment runs — Deployments can fail to trigger for a variety of reasons: for example, if the `environment` resource has been archived, or if session creation is rate-limited. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#deployment-runs
- [definition] Managing deployment lifecycle — Each lifecycle change emits a [webhook event](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types), so you can react to a paused, unpaused, or archived deployment without polling; see the Deployment events tab. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#managing-deployment-lifecycle
- [definition] Failure behavior — Session creation rate-limit responses are recorded immediately as a `session_rate_limited_error` run without retry; the schedule attempts again at the next scheduled occurrence. Rate limits on underlying API calls within a session are handled by the session itself. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#failure-behavior
- [definition] Trigger a manual run — To run a deployment outside its schedule, call the [`run` endpoint](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/deployments/run). This creates a session immediately and writes a deployment run with `trigger_context.type: "manual"`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#trigger-a-manual-run

- [definition] Subscribe to session webhooks — In the [Console](https://platform.claude.com/settings/workspaces/default/webhooks), define a webhook endpoint that listens for `session.status_run_started` events.
