- [definition] Export the webhook signing key — In addition to the environment ID and key from [Before you begin](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#before-you-begin), export the webhook signing key on your handler host so the handler can verify incoming payloads. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#run-a-worker
- [definition] Implement the webhook handler — `EnvironmentWorker` claims the work item, downloads skills, executes tool calls in the working directory, posts results back, and exits. Invoke it when `session.status_run_started` fires. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#run-a-worker
- [definition] SDK helpers — The SDK provides three helpers at different levels of control. `EnvironmentWorker` covers most use cases; drop to the lower-level helpers when you need to launch your own per-session process or run tools against an already-claimed session. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#sdk-helpers
- [definition] Verify the worker is connected — From a separate shell, with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set to your Claude API key (not the environment key), confirm `workers_polling` is at least 1: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#verify-the-worker-is-connected
- [definition] Start a session — Once your worker is running, create a session that targets the environment. Set `AGENT_ID` to the agent ID you noted in [Before you begin](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#before-you-begin). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#start-a-session
- [definition] Use memory stores — Sessions on a self-hosted environment attach [memory stores](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory) exactly as sessions on cloud environments do: list them in `resources` when you create the session, as shown in [Attach a memory store to a… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#use-memory-stores
- [definition] How the worker handles memory — When the worker claims a work item whose session has memory stores attached, it: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#how-the-worker-handles-memory
- [definition] Prepare the host — Memory stores on self-hosted sandboxes need a POSIX filesystem on the worker host (the Linux host from [Before you begin](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#before-you-begin)); Windows hosts are not supported, because the worker requires `O_NOFOLLOW` when it… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#prepare-the-host
- [definition] Run one sandbox per session — The sandbox-per-session pattern in [Run a worker](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#run-a-worker) gives each session a fresh filesystem, which is what [Prepare the… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#run-one-sandbox-per-session
- [definition] Configure sync — Two `EnvironmentWorker` options control memory behavior: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#configure-sync
- [definition] Read-only stores and conflicts — For a store attached with `access: "read_only"`, the `write` and `edit` tools refuse to change files inside its directory, and the worker never uploads anything from it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#read-only-stores-and-conflicts
- [definition] Troubleshoot memory mounts — The worker logs mount and background sync failures rather than reporting them to the session; only read-only refusals reach the agent, as tool errors (see [Read-only stores and conflicts](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#read-only-stores-and-conflicts)). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#troubleshoot-memory-mounts
- [definition] Serve custom tools from your sandbox — [Custom tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#custom-tools) are tools your own code executes: the agent emits an `agent.custom_tool_use` event and waits for a matching `user.custom_tool_result`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#serve-custom-tools-from-your-sandbox
- [definition] Declare the tool on the agent — Add a `custom` entry to the agent's `tools` whose `name` matches the tool your worker registers. See [Custom tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#custom-tools) for the full declaration shape. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#serve-custom-tools-from-your-sandbox
- [definition] Register the implementation with the worker — Pass the tool through the worker's `tools` factory (see [SDK helpers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#sdk-helpers)), alongside the built-in toolset: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#serve-custom-tools-from-your-sandbox
- [definition] Wrap an MCP server as custom tools — The [MCP connector](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector) connects to MCP servers from Anthropic's side, so a server must expose an HTTP endpoint that Anthropic can reach, directly or through an [MCP… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#wrap-an-mcp-server-as-custom-tools
- [definition] Declare the server's tools on the agent — List the MCP server's tools and declare each one as a `custom` tool; the MCP `name`, `description`, and `inputSchema` map one to one onto the custom tool's fields. If the server paginates its tool list, declare every page; the worker must list the same pages. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#wrap-an-mcp-server-as-custom-tools
- [definition] Serve the tools from the worker — Connect to the same MCP server at startup, convert its tools with the MCP helpers, and register them alongside the built-in toolset. Keep one MCP session open for the life of the worker. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#wrap-an-mcp-server-as-custom-tools
- [definition] Monitoring and operations — These calls run from your monitoring or operations tooling, authenticated with your Claude API key, to observe and manage the worker fleet. The claim and keep-alive loop is handled inside the worker helpers, so you don't call those endpoints directly. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#monitoring-and-operations
- [definition] Read queue depth — `work.stats` returns the queue state for an environment: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#read-queue-depth
- [definition] Stop a session gracefully — Use `work.stop` to ask the worker handling a specific session to shut it down. By default the work item moves to `stopping`: the worker notices on its next lease heartbeat, cancels the session's in-flight tool call, and confirms the shutdown, at which point the work item becomes `stopped`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#stop-a-session-gracefully

- [parameter] A work-starting event (for example, `user.message`) is sent while the session is at or over its budget; the error names the [accepted settle events](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#events-accepted-at-the-cap): 400 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#error-reference
- [parameter] The budget is set to a value at or below the session's consumed list cost: 400 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#error-reference
- [parameter] A budget is added to a session created without one, or re-added after removal: 400 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#error-reference
- [parameter] `amount` is not a whole number of cents (for example, `"25.00"`), is zero or negative, or `currency` is not `USD`: 400 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#error-reference
- [parameter] A budgeted create references a model with [no public list price](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#models-without-a-list-price): 400 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#error-reference
- [definition] Set a budget at session creation — Pass the optional `budget` field when you create the session: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#set-a-budget-at-session-creation
- [definition] How list cost is measured — The platform prices what the session consumes, continuously, at public list rates: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#how-list-cost-is-measured
- [definition] When a session reaches its budget — The cap is enforced between model requests, not mid-request. Before each model request, the platform checks the session's consumed list cost, and once that total reaches the cap every thread pauses before its next request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#when-a-session-reaches-its-budget
- [definition] Events accepted at the cap — While the session is at or over its budget, it accepts only events that settle work already in progress: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#events-accepted-at-the-cap
- [definition] Resume a session at its budget — Change or remove the budget with a session update. An accepted update resumes the session's paused work automatically; no further client action is needed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#resume-a-session-at-its-budget
- [definition] Change the budget — Update the session with a new `max_list_cost`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#change-the-budget
- [definition] Remove the budget — Set `budget` to `null` to remove the cap entirely. The session's paused work resumes, and the resulting `session.updated` event carries `budget` set to `null`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#remove-the-budget
- [definition] Monitor spend — The session object carries its `budget` and a `usage` object with the tracked spend: `usage.list_cost` is the session's consumed list cost, and `usage.active_seconds` is the running time its runtime cost is priced on. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#monitor-spend
- [definition] Budgets in multiagent sessions — A [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) session has a single budget shared across all of its threads; there are no per-thread caps. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#budgets-in-multiagent-sessions
- [definition] Budgets on deployments — A [deployment](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments) accepts the same `budget` object when you create or update it: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#budgets-on-deployments
- [definition] Models without a list price — A budget can only track consumption the platform can price. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#models-without-a-list-price
- [definition] Error reference — Budget-related requests are rejected in the following cases: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets#error-reference

- [snippet] Tracking usage: { — `{` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#tracking-usage
- [parameter] A stream with buffered events but no `event_start` or `event_delta`: The connection you're reading didn't opt in (`event_deltas[]` applies per connection, not per session), or the turn never touched the thread you're streaming. Previews are thread-scoped, so list the session's threads (`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/threads`) to find which one ran. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#troubleshoot-previews
- [parameter] A 404 on the stream URL: The path or an ID is wrong, or the request carries no managed-agents beta header at all. The thread endpoints are beta-gated, so without the header they don't exist. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#troubleshoot-previews
- [parameter] A 400 naming `event_deltas`: Only `agent.message` and `agent.thinking` are accepted. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#troubleshoot-previews
- [definition] Event deltas — By default, the agent's response text reaches the stream as buffered `agent.message` events, each emitted only after the model request that produced it finishes. Event deltas let you render that text incrementally, as a live preview, while the model is still generating it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#event-deltas
- [definition] Opt in to previews — Previews are opt-in per stream connection. Add the `event_deltas[]` query parameter to the stream you're reading, repeating it once for each event type you want previewed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#opt-in-to-previews
- [definition] Accumulate and reconcile — Every SDK that supports event deltas includes an accumulator helper that handles the `index` bookkeeping for you. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#accumulate-and-reconcile
- [definition] Preview session thread events — In a [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) session, every session thread has its own event stream at `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/threads/{thread_id}/stream`, and it takes the same `event_deltas[]` parameter with the same values. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#preview-session-thread-events
- [definition] Limitations — Previews are tuned for responsiveness. Build against these constraints: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#limitations
- [definition] Troubleshoot previews — If the stream doesn't behave as you expect: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#troubleshoot-previews
- [definition] Handling custom tool calls — When the agent invokes a [custom tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#custom-tools): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#handling-custom-tool-calls
- [definition] Tool confirmation — When a [permission policy](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/permission-policies) requires confirmation before a tool executes: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#tool-confirmation
- [definition] Resuming an idle session — Sessions persist between interactions. Conversation history is preserved unless the session is explicitly deleted. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#resuming-an-idle-session
- [definition] Reaching a session budget — A session created with a [budget](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets) pauses instead of overspending. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#reaching-a-session-budget
- [definition] Sending system messages — `system.message` is currently supported by Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, and Claude Opus 5. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#sending-system-messages
- [definition] Tracking usage — The session object includes a `usage` field with the session's cumulative usage: token counts, server tool use, active time, and the tracked list cost. Fetch the session after it goes idle to read the latest totals. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#tracking-usage
- [definition] Console observability — The Claude Console includes a session viewer for inspecting what an agent did without writing any code. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#console-observability

- [parameter] `idle`: Agent is waiting for input, including user messages or tool confirmations. Sessions created without `initial_events` start in `idle`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#session-statuses
- [parameter] `running`: Agent is actively executing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#session-statuses
- [parameter] `rescheduling`: Transient error occurred, retrying automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#session-statuses
- [parameter] `terminated`: Session has ended, either because of an unrecoverable error or because it was archived. A session that finishes its work goes `idle`, not `terminated`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#session-statuses
- [definition] Session statuses — Sessions progress through these statuses. See [Start a session](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions) for the session lifecycle. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#session-statuses
- [definition] Updating the agent configuration — You can update a session's `agent.tools` and `agent.mcp_servers`, including permission policies and per-tool web settings such as [domain filters](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#restrict-web-search-and-web-fetch-domains), mid-session without creating a new agent version. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#updating-the-agent-configuration
- [definition] Updating the session budget — A session [created with a budget](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#set-a-session-budget) accepts two kinds of budget update: replacing the cap with a new `max_list_cost`, and removing it by setting `budget` to `null`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#updating-the-session-budget
- [definition] Listing sessions — Results from `GET /v1/sessions` are paginated. Use the `limit` query parameter to control the page size. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#listing-sessions
- [definition] Archiving a session — Archive a session to prevent new events from being sent while preserving its history. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#archiving-a-session
- [definition] Deleting a session — Delete a session to permanently remove its record, events, and associated sandbox. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations#deleting-a-session

- [parameter] More than one `user.define_outcome` event: 400 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#seed-the-session-with-initial-events
- [parameter] A `user.define_outcome` event without a `rubric`: 400 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#seed-the-session-with-initial-events
- [parameter] More than 100 file-sourced [`document` content blocks](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files#document-blocks) across the whole list: 400 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#seed-the-session-with-initial-events
- [parameter] A request body over 32 MB: 413 — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#seed-the-session-with-initial-events
- [definition] Creating a session — A session requires an `agent` ID and an `environment` ID. Agents are versioned resources; passing in the `agent` ID as a string creates the session with the latest agent version. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#creating-a-session
- [definition] Seed the session with initial events — You can create a session and start its work in one call. `initial_events` is an optional array of initial [events](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference#event-types) to send to the session at creation, processed in order. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#seed-the-session-with-initial-events
- [definition] Override agent configuration for a session — You can pass `agent` in three forms: an agent ID string, a pinned-version object (`type: "agent"`), or an overrides object. The overrides form changes parts of the agent's configuration for a single session. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#override-agent-configuration-for-a-session
- [definition] Set a session budget — To cap what a session can spend, pass the optional `budget` object when you create it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#set-a-session-budget
- [definition] MCP authentication through vaults — If your agent uses MCP tools that require authentication, pass `vault_ids` at session creation to reference a vault containing stored OAuth credentials. Anthropic manages token refresh on your behalf. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#mcp-authentication-through-vaults
- [definition] Starting the session — Creating a session without `initial_events` registers the session but does not start any work; the environment's sandbox begins provisioning as soon as the session is created, so the first tool call does not wait on it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#starting-the-session

- [parameter] `session.status_run_started`: Agent execution started. This triggers at every session status transition to `running`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.status_idled`: Agent awaiting input, for example, a tool permission approval or a new user message. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.budget_reached`: The session reached its [budget](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets) and paused. Fires at most once for each budget value you set; changing the budget arms it again. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.status_rescheduled`: A transient error occurred and the session is retrying automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.status_terminated`: The session terminated, either because of an unrecoverable error or because it was archived. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.thread_created`: New [multiagent thread](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) opened: an additional agent called by the coordinator is starting work, or the session's [advisor](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#give-the-session-an-advisor) is being consulted. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.thread_idled`: An agent in a [multiagent interaction](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) is waiting for input. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.thread_terminated`: A [multiagent thread](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) terminated, either because the thread was archived or because it exhausted its retries. A coordinator-spawned child that finishes its work goes `idle`, not `terminated` (an advisor thread terminates once its consultation completes). Fires for child threads only; the… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.outcome_evaluation_ended`: [Outcome evaluation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes) for a single iteration completed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.updated`: Session properties changed (for example, its name or configuration was updated). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `session.deleted`: Session permanently deleted. There is no object left to fetch, so treat the event itself as final. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `vault.created`: Vault created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `vault.archived`: Vault archived. A `vault_credential.archived` event is also emitted for each underlying credential. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `vault.deleted`: Vault deleted. A `vault_credential.deleted` event is also emitted for each underlying credential. There is no object left to fetch, so treat the event itself as final. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `vault_credential.created`: Credential created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `vault_credential.archived`: Credential archived, either directly or as a result of vault archival. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `vault_credential.deleted`: Credential deleted, either directly or as a result of vault deletion. There is no object left to fetch, so treat the event itself as final. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `vault_credential.refresh_failed`: An `mcp_oauth` credential cannot be refreshed (invalid refresh token, or irrecoverable error from the OAuth server). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `agent.created`: Agent created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `agent.updated`: A [new version of the agent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/agent-setup#update-an-agent) was published. Updates that do not create a new version do not trigger this event. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `agent.archived`: Agent archived. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `agent.deleted`: Agent permanently deleted. There is no object left to fetch, so treat the event itself as final. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `deployment.created`: [Scheduled deployment](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments) created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `deployment.updated`: Deployment properties changed (for example, its schedule was updated). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `deployment.paused`: Deployment paused, either by request or automatically when a scheduled run fails with an unrecoverable error, such as an archived subagent or an archived environment. Recoverable failures, including rate limits, don't pause the deployment. See [Failure behavior](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#failure-behavior). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `deployment.unpaused`: Deployment unpaused, resuming its schedule. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `deployment.archived`: Deployment archived, either directly or because its agent was archived. If the agent is deleted instead, a scheduled deployment is archived at its next scheduled run; a deployment without a schedule is not archived automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `deployment.deleted`: Deployment permanently deleted. There is no object left to fetch, so treat the event itself as final. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `deployment_run.started`: A scheduled run started. Only scheduled runs emit `deployment_run` events; [manual runs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#trigger-a-manual-run) do not. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `deployment_run.succeeded`: A scheduled run created its session. The event carries the same `data.id` (the run ID) as the run's `deployment_run.started` event. To follow the session's work, subscribe to its session events (the Session events tab), or fetch the [deployment run](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#deployment-runs) for its `session_id`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `deployment_run.failed`: A scheduled run did not create a session. The event carries the same `data.id` as the run's `deployment_run.started` event. Fetch the [deployment run](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/scheduled-deployments#deployment-runs) for the error details. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `environment.created`: Environment created. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `environment.updated`: Environment updated with at least one changed field. A no-op update emits nothing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `environment.archived`: Environment archived. Re-archiving an already-archived environment emits nothing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `environment.deleted`: Environment deleted, including delete of an already-archived environment. There is no object left to fetch, so treat the event itself as final. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `memory_store.created`: Memory store created, either by you or by an Anthropic-operated process that clones one of your existing stores. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `memory_store.archived`: Memory store archived. Re-archiving an already-archived store emits nothing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [parameter] `memory_store.deleted`: Memory store deleted, including delete of an already-archived store. Deleting a store cascades to its memories and memory versions without emitting per-memory events; the single `memory_store.deleted` event is the signal. There is no object left to fetch, so treat the event itself as final. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types
- [definition] Register an endpoint — Visit **Manage > Webhooks** in the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/settings/workspaces/default/webhooks). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#register-an-endpoint
- [definition] Verify the signature — Every delivery carries the `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` headers. Use the SDK's `unwrap()` helper to verify the signature and parse the event in one step. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#verify-the-signature
- [definition] Handle an event — Parse the body, switch on `data.type`, and fetch the resource by ID. Return any `2xx` to acknowledge. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#handle-an-event

- [parameter] Grep: Name=`grep`; Description=Text search using regex patterns — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#available-tools
- [parameter] Web fetch: Name=`web_fetch`; Description=Fetch content from a URL — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#available-tools
- [parameter] Web search: Name=`web_search`; Description=Search the web for information — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#available-tools
- [parameter] `allowed_domains`: Applies to=`web_search`, `web_fetch`; Description=The only hosts the tool can reach. Cannot be combined with `blocked_domains` on the same entry. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#restrict-web-search-and-web-fetch-domains
- [parameter] `blocked_domains`: Applies to=`web_search`, `web_fetch`; Description=Hosts the tool cannot reach. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#restrict-web-search-and-web-fetch-domains
- [parameter] `max_content_tokens`: Applies to=`web_fetch`; Description=Caps the amount of fetched page content included in the context. Must be a positive integer. See [content limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#content-limits). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#restrict-web-search-and-web-fetch-domains
- [parameter] `user_location`: Applies to=`web_search`; Description=Localizes search results. An object with the same fields as the Messages API [`user_location`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#localization) parameter. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#restrict-web-search-and-web-fetch-domains
- [definition] Available tools — The agent toolset includes the following tools. All are enabled by default when you include the toolset in your agent configuration. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#available-tools
- [definition] Configuring the toolset — Enable the full toolset with `agent_toolset_20260401` when creating an agent. Use the `configs` array to disable specific tools or override their settings. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#configuring-the-toolset
- [definition] Disabling specific tools — To disable a tool, set `enabled: false` in its config entry in the toolset object of your agent's `tools` array: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#disabling-specific-tools
- [definition] Enabling only specific tools — The `default_config` object sets the baseline for every tool in the set, and per-tool `configs` entries override it. To start with everything off and enable only what you need, set `default_config.enabled` to `false`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#enabling-only-specific-tools
- [definition] Restrict web search and web fetch domains — To control which sites the agent's web tools can reach, set `allowed_domains` (the tool can reach only these hosts) or `blocked_domains` (the tool can never reach these hosts) on the `web_search` and `web_fetch` entries of the toolset's `configs` array. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#restrict-web-search-and-web-fetch-domains
- [definition] Custom tools — In addition to built-in tools, you can define custom tools. Custom tools are analogous to [user-defined client tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/how-tool-use-works#user-defined-tools-client-executed) in the Messages API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#custom-tools

- [definition] Overview — A **memory store** is a workspace-scoped collection of text documents optimized for Claude. When you attach a store to a session, it is mounted as a directory inside the session's sandbox. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#overview
- [definition] Create a memory store — Give the store a `name` and a `description`. The description is passed to the agent, telling it what the store contains. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#create-a-memory-store
- [definition] Seed it with content (optional) — Pre-load a store with reference material before any agent runs: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#seed-it-with-content-optional
- [definition] Attach a memory store to a session — Memory stores are attached in the session's `resources[]` array when the [session is created](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#creating-a-session). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#attach-a-memory-store-to-a-session
- [definition] How the agent accesses memory — Each attached store is mounted inside the session's sandbox as a directory under `/mnt/memory/`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#how-the-agent-accesses-memory
- [definition] View and edit memories — Memory stores can be managed directly through the API. Use this for building review workflows, correcting bad memories, or seeding stores before any session runs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#view-and-edit-memories
- [definition] List memories — List the memories in a store. Results are returned in a stable, server-defined order. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#list-memories
- [definition] Read a memory — Fetching an individual memory returns the full content. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#read-a-memory
- [definition] Create a memory — `memories.create` creates a memory at a given `path`. Create does not overwrite; to change an existing memory, use [`memories.update`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#update-a-memory). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#create-a-memory
- [definition] Update a memory — `memories.update` modifies an existing memory by ID. You can change `content`, `path` (a rename), or both. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#update-a-memory
- [definition] Audit memory changes — Every mutation to a memory creates an immutable **memory version** (`memver_...`). Use the version endpoints to audit who changed what and when, to inspect or restore a prior snapshot, and to scrub sensitive content out of history with redact. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#audit-memory-changes
- [definition] List versions — List version history for a store, newest first. The example filters to a single memory's history: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#list-versions
- [definition] Retrieve a version — Fetching an individual version returns the same fields as the list response plus the full `content` body. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#retrieve-a-version
- [definition] Redact a version — Redact scrubs content out of a historical version while preserving the audit trail (who did what, when). Use it for compliance workflows such as removing leaked secrets, PII, or user deletion requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#redact-a-version
- [definition] Manage memory stores — In addition to [`create`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/memory_stores/create), memory stores support [`retrieve`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/memory_stores/retrieve), [`update`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/memory_stores/update)… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#manage-memory-stores
- [definition] List stores — List stores in the workspace. Archived stores are excluded by default; pass `include_archived: true` to include them. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#list-stores
- [definition] Archive a store — Archiving makes a store read-only and prevents it from being attached to new sessions. Archiving is one-way; there is no unarchive. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#archive-a-store
- [definition] Best practices for memory management — When a store reaches its 10,000-memory limit, writes to new memories fail: both direct `memories.create` calls and the agent's file writes to unmapped paths. Existing memories remain readable and editable. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#best-practices-for-memory-management

- [snippet] CMEK content preservation: { — `{` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#cmek-content-preservation
- [parameter] `id`: Type=string; Description=Unique identifier for this activity — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `accessed_at`: Type=RFC 3339 string; Description=When the access occurred. Might be earlier than when the activity becomes visible in your feed — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `created_at`: Type=RFC 3339 string; Description=When the activity became visible in your feed — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `actor`: Type=object; Description=Always `{ "type": "anthropic_actor", "email_address": null }`. Individual employee identity is not disclosed — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `accessor_department`: Type=string; Description=The Anthropic team that performed the access (for example, `Safeguards`) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `reason_code`: Type=enum; Description=See [Reason codes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#reason-codes) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `resource_details.type`: Type=enum; Description=A resource type, currently only `message`. Extensible for future resource types — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `resource_details.id`: Type=string or null; Description=Identifier of the content accessed — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `resource_details.parent`: Type=string or null; Description=Identifier of the content's parent, for example the conversation ID containing a message. Currently `null` or omitted until resources with parents are supported — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `organization_id`: Type=string; Description=The organization the content belongs to. Tagged ID format (`org_...`) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `organization_uuid`: Type=string; Description=The organization the content belongs to. UUID format — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `workspace_id`: Type=string or null; Description=The workspace the content belongs to — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [parameter] `safety_review`: Content was viewed as part of a usage-policy or safety investigation — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#reason-codes
- [parameter] `incident_response`: Content was viewed while investigating an incident affecting your organization — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#reason-codes
- [parameter] `policy_violation_investigation`: Content was preserved during a Trust and Safety policy-violation investigation — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#reason-codes
- [parameter] `csae_report`: Content was preserved as evidence for a child safety (CSAE) report — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#reason-codes
- [parameter] Claude API (`api.anthropic.com`): Covered=Yes; Details=Prompts, completions, and data directly embedded in the API inputs — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [parameter] Claude Code (using an API key): Covered=Yes; Details=API traffic from Claude Code is covered as Claude API traffic — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [parameter] Claude Platform on AWS: Covered=Yes; Details=Claude Platform on AWS generates Access Transparency events within the Compliance API (not AWS CloudTrail) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [parameter] Claude API (`api.anthropic.com`) (Batch, Files): Covered=No; Details=The Claude API Batch and Files APIs are not covered, just like they are not covered by ZDR — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [parameter] Claude for Enterprise (claude.ai seats): Covered=No; Details=Not covered — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [parameter] Claude for Work: Covered=No; Details=Not covered — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [parameter] Claude Free, Pro, Max: Covered=No; Details=Consumer plans are not eligible — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [parameter] Playground (Claude Console): Covered=No; Details=Not covered — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [parameter] Microsoft Foundry: Covered=No; Details=Not available — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [parameter] Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud: Covered=No; Details=Partner-operated platforms; refer to those platforms' transparency controls — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [definition] How Access Transparency works — Anthropic personnel access customer content only under defined conditions. Access Transparency is designed to make such access visible to you. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#how-access-transparency-works
- [definition] Request Access Transparency — Contact your Anthropic account representative. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#getting-started
- [definition] Anthropic reviews eligibility — Anthropic confirms your organization meets the eligibility criteria and enables the capability at the organization level. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#getting-started
- [definition] Receive events through the Compliance API — `anthropic_access` activities appear in your existing Activity Feed under your existing Compliance Access Key; no new endpoint or credentials are required. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#getting-started
- [definition] Receiving Access Transparency events — Access Transparency events are delivered as the `anthropic_access` activity type on the Compliance API Activity Feed. Filter with `activity_types[]`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#receiving-access-transparency-events
- [definition] CMEK content preservation — In rare cases, Anthropic preserves specific content beyond the standard retention window (for example, when a safety review confirms severely harmful content that must be retained for an ongoing investigation). Preservation is itself a logged, customer-visible action: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#cmek-content-preservation
- [definition] Reason codes — The set of reason codes is closed. Anthropic will update this page in the event it introduces a new code. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#reason-codes
- [definition] Surface eligibility — The following table lists which surfaces are covered by Access Transparency. Coverage means human access to content from that surface generates `anthropic_access` events. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#surface-eligibility
- [definition] Coverage timing — Access Transparency applies from the time it is enabled for your organization. Content already in your retention window at enablement might also generate events when accessed, but Anthropic does not guarantee coverage for content written before enablement. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#coverage-timing
- [definition] Notification timing — `anthropic_access` and `cmek_preserve` events are delivered to your Compliance API feed within two business days of the access or preservation they record. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#notification-timing
- [definition] Automated processing does not generate access events — `anthropic_access` events record human access only. Anthropic's automated safety systems and classifiers continue to process your content as part of normal operation, and that processing does not generate `anthropic_access` events. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#automated-processing-does-not-generate-access-events
- [definition] Access Transparency does not change what Anthropic can access — Access Transparency records access; it does not grant or restrict it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#access-transparency-does-not-change-what-anthropic-can-access
- [definition] CMEK key-use logs are not a per-read record — For organizations that also enable CMEK, your cloud KMS audit log (CloudTrail, Cloud Audit Logs, or Azure Monitor) records Anthropic's use of your key. Because keys are cached for short periods during operation, an individual human read does not necessarily produce a distinct KMS decryption entry. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/access-transparency#cmek-key-use-logs-are-not-a-per-read-record

## Which API do you need?
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api>

- [snippet] Call the API: curl "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/usage_report/claude_code?starting_at=2025-09-08" \ — `curl "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/usage_report/claude_code?starting_at=2025-09-08" \` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#get-access-to-the-claude-code-analytics-api
- [parameter] **Claude Code Analytics API**: Key type=Admin API key (`sk-ant-admin01-...`); Created in=[Claude Console > Settings > Admin keys](https://platform.claude.com/settings/admin-keys); Who can create it=Organization admin; What it covers=Daily Claude Code metrics per user: sessions, lines of code, commits, pull requests, tool acceptance, and estimated cost by model — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#which-api-do-you-need
- [parameter] **Claude Enterprise Analytics API**: Key type=Analytics API key; Created in=[claude.ai > Organization settings > API](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/api-access); Who can create it=Primary owner; What it covers=Organization-wide engagement and adoption (user activity, active-user summaries, project, skill, and connector usage), plus cost and usage reports — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#which-api-do-you-need
- [definition] Get access to the Claude Code Analytics API — The Claude Code Analytics API is available to every organization with access to the [Admin API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api), and is free to use. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#get-access-to-the-claude-code-analytics-api
- [definition] Create an Admin API key — Follow the steps in [Create an Admin API key](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys#create-a-key-for-a-claude-console-organization). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#get-access-to-the-claude-code-analytics-api
- [definition] Get access to the Claude Enterprise Analytics API — The Claude Enterprise Analytics API is available to Claude Enterprise organizations. Engagement and adoption data is available on all Enterprise plans. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#get-access-to-the-claude-enterprise-analytics-api
- [definition] Sign in as the primary owner — Only the primary owner of the organization can enable API access and create Analytics API keys. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#get-access-to-the-claude-enterprise-analytics-api
- [definition] Enable API access and create a key — Go to [claude.ai > Organization settings > API](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/api-access) and enable public API access, then create an Analytics API key. Keys carry the `read:analytics` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#get-access-to-the-claude-enterprise-analytics-api
- [definition] Call the API — Pass the key in the `x-api-key` header. Endpoints live under `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/analytics/`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#get-access-to-the-claude-enterprise-analytics-api
- [definition] Data availability and freshness — Claude Enterprise Analytics API data is available for dates on or after January 1, 2026. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#data-availability-and-freshness
- [definition] Known limitations — If your organization uses Claude Code through Amazon Bedrock, the Claude Enterprise Analytics API does not return Claude Code activity for that usage. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api#known-limitations

- [definition] Zero data retention (ZDR) — Under a ZDR arrangement, Anthropic does not store customer prompts or responses at rest after the API response is returned. - [definition] HIPAA readiness — The Claude API supports HIPAA-ready integrations for organizations that handle protected health information (PHI). With a signed BAA and a HIPAA-enabled organization, you can use supported API features to process PHI while supporting your organization's HIPAA compliance. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#hipaa-readiness
- [definition] PHI handling guidelines — Protected health information (PHI) includes any individually identifiable health information. In the context of the Claude API, PHI typically appears in message content (prompts and Claude's responses), attached files (images, PDFs), and file names or metadata associated with message content. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#phi-handling-guidelines
- [definition] HIPAA error handling — Your signed BAA is the official source of truth for which features are covered. The API also enforces these restrictions automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#hipaa-error-handling
- [definition] Getting started with HIPAA readiness — There are two ways to set up HIPAA-ready API access. Most organizations can enable it directly in the Claude Console with Anthropic's standard BAA; organizations that require a negotiated BAA should work with their account team. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#getting-started-with-hipaa-readiness
- [definition] Open your organization's privacy settings — In [Claude Console > Settings > Privacy](https://platform.claude.com/settings/privacy), organization admins with the HIPAA management permission see a **HIPAA compliance** card. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#enable-in-the-console-standard-baa
- [definition] Review and execute the BAA — Download the Business Associate Agreement and the HIPAA Implementation Guide, then accept the agreement as an authorized legal representative of your organization. Each step becomes available after you download the prior document, and your enablement is bound to the exact BAA version you downloaded. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#enable-in-the-console-standard-baa
- [definition] Enablement takes effect immediately — HIPAA readiness controls are applied to your organization as soon as you accept. Once HIPAA readiness is enabled for your organization, the configuration is permanent and cannot be disabled by an administrator. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#enable-in-the-console-standard-baa
- [definition] Model-specific data retention requirements — Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 are designated Covered Models (see the [Covered Models support article](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15425695)) and require 30-day data retention; ZDR is therefore not available for either model. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#model-specific-data-retention-requirements
- [definition] Enable 30-day retention for a workspace — Organizations with a ZDR arrangement can make Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 available in a specific workspace by enabling 30-day retention for that workspace only. - [definition] Open the workspace's privacy controls — In [Claude Console > Settings > Workspaces](https://platform.claude.com/settings/workspaces), select the workspace and open its **Privacy controls** tab. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#enable-30-day-retention-for-a-workspace

- [definition] Verify — Requests to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 from this workspace now succeed. Workspaces without an override continue to follow the organization default. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#enable-30-day-retention-for-a-workspace

- [definition] Retention regardless of arrangement — Even with ZDR or HIPAA arrangements in place, Anthropic may retain data where required by law or where it has been flagged by Anthropic's automated trust and safety systems. As a result, if a chat or session is flagged, Anthropic may retain inputs and outputs for up to 2 years. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention#retention-regardless-of-arrangement

## How App Attest works
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/app-attest>

- [definition] How App Attest works — Each installation of your app uses Apple's [App Attest](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/establishing-your-app-s-integrity) service to prove that it is a genuine, unmodified build of the app you registered. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/app-attest#how-app-attest-works
- [definition] Set up App Attest — App Attest requires a physical device. The Simulator, and hardware without a Secure Enclave, cannot perform App Attest. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/app-attest#set-up-app-attest
- [definition] Revoke an app integration — To stop a compromised or retired app, revoke its integration: in your workspace's settings in the Claude Console, open **App integrations**, select the integration, and click **Revoke**, then confirm. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/app-attest#revoke-an-app-integration

- [definition] Create an RSA key in your vault — Azure Key Vault does not support symmetric key wrapping, so the key must be RSA (3072-bit or larger) with `wrapKey` and `unwrapKey` in its allowed operations. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek-azure-key-vault#encryption-key-setup
- [definition] Grant the Anthropic service principal access to your key — Assign the `Key Vault Crypto User` role to the service principal from the first step, scoped to the **individual key** rather than the whole vault. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek-azure-key-vault#encryption-key-setup
- [definition] Register the key with Anthropic — How you register the key depends on which product you use. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek-azure-key-vault#register-the-key-with-anthropic
- [definition] Register the key with Anthropic — Create an external key configuration through the Admin API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek-azure-key-vault#register-the-key-with-anthropic
- [definition] Validate the key — Trigger an encrypt and decrypt round-trip against your key. This confirms that Anthropic can authenticate to your tenant and perform wrap and unwrap operations. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek-azure-key-vault#register-the-key-with-anthropic
- [definition] Attach the key to a workspace — Once the key is validated, attach it to a new workspace before you send any requests to that workspace. For a workspace that already receives requests, the key can take [up to a day to take effect](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek#how-it-works). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek-azure-key-vault#register-the-key-with-anthropic
- [definition] Terraform — For infrastructure-as-code deployments, the same steps map to the `azurerm` and `azuread` providers. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek-azure-key-vault#terraform

## Before you begin
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration>

- [parameter] URL rejected: The URL failed a structural check. Use an `https://` URL on port 443. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [parameter] Private or internal IP: The host resolves to a private or internal address. Use a publicly routable host. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [parameter] Timeout: The AI security server did not return a verdict within the timeout. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [parameter] Transport error: DNS resolution, the TLS handshake, or the connection failed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [parameter] Non-200 status: The AI security server responded with a status other than 200. Verdicts must come back as HTTP 200; redirects are not followed and count as failures. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [parameter] Unparseable response: The AI security server responded, but the body is not a valid verdict. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Set up Inference hooks — There are three enforcement states: **off** (**Enforce verdicts** is off: your AI security server is never contacted and prompts are not inspected), **shadow** (**Enforce verdicts** is on with **Mode** set to **Shadow mode**: your AI security server receives prompts and returns verdicts, and… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Allow Inference hooks for your organization — Go to claude.ai > **Organization settings** > **Data and privacy** and find the **Inference hooks** section. Turn on **Allow for your organization**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Open the Inference hooks settings page — Still in **Data and privacy**, open the **Inference hooks** section to reach the Inference hooks settings page. It lives under Data and privacy rather than as its own entry in the settings nav, so its breadcrumb reads **Data and privacy / Inference hooks**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Configure your endpoint — Click **Configure** to open the **Configure endpoint** dialog and fill in: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Test the connection — Click **Test connection**. Claude sends a synthetic test prompt to the URL and headers currently in the form, not the saved values, so re-enter any stored header values before testing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Save and store your signing secret — Save the endpoint configuration. The first save generates your webhook signing secret and reveals it once. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Choose failure handling and timeout — Under **Failure handling**, set **Mode** to choose what happens while the AI security server is unreachable or verdicts time out: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Choose a rollout percentage — Under **Rollout**, set **Requests inspected (%)** to run inspection on a percentage of requests while you bring your AI security server up. The value ranges from 0 to 100: 100 inspects everything, and 0 turns inspection off. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Turn on Enforce verdicts — To evaluate verdicts against live traffic without blocking anyone at first, set **Mode** to **Shadow mode** (step 6) before turning on enforcement; see [Shadow mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#shadow-mode). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#set-up-inference-hooks
- [definition] Shadow mode — Shadow mode runs your hook against live traffic without blocking anything. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#shadow-mode
- [definition] Exclusions — Under **Exclusions**, select roles whose members are not covered by Inference hooks: their prompts are never sent to your AI security server. Only custom roles your organization created can be excluded; the built-in roles aren't offered. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#exclusions
- [definition] Custom blocked prompt message — Under **Custom blocked prompt message**, set custom text of up to 500 characters that is appended to the error an end user sees when your AI security server denies a request (typically who to contact or where to request an exception). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#custom-blocked-prompt-message
- [definition] Monitor your AI security server — The endpoint health area of the Inference hooks settings page shows: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#monitor-your-ai-security-server
- [definition] Circuit breaker — Sustained webhook failures attributable to your AI security server trip the circuit breaker, which stops enforcement: your server is no longer contacted, and your **Failure handling** choice applies to every inspected request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#circuit-breaker
- [definition] Rotate your signing secret — Click **Rotate secret** under **Request signing** to replace your signing secret. Rotation is an immediate cutover: the new secret is generated and revealed once, the old secret can no longer be retrieved, and no request is ever signed with both secrets, so there is no overlap period to rely on. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#rotate-your-signing-secret
- [definition] Audit trail — Inference hooks activity is recorded in your organization's [Activity Feed](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed): configuration changes, denials, circuit breaker trips, and requests that proceeded without inspection under your failure handling setting. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration#audit-trail

- [definition] How it works — Only Organization Admins (on Claude Platform; the Admin role on Claude Platform on AWS) or Owners and the Primary Owner (on Claude Enterprise) can configure CMEK. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek#how-it-works
- [definition] Availability and regions — Except on Claude Platform on AWS (covered at the end of this section), CMEK is currently available in US regions only, and all encryption operations are processed in US regions. For minimal latency, choose a region close to Anthropic's US infrastructure: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek#availability-and-regions
- [definition] What CMEK protects — What CMEK covers depends on which product you use. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek#what-cmek-protects

- [definition] Encrypted with Anthropic key — These features remain available, but their data is not encrypted under your key. You can disable any feature that is not appropriate for your use case in **Settings**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek#encrypted-with-anthropic-key
- [definition] Feature support — The following Claude Platform APIs and tools store data at rest under your key when CMEK is enabled: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek#feature-support
- [definition] Limited preservation outside your key — In three narrow cases, Anthropic may preserve specific records under Anthropic-managed encryption: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek#limited-preservation-outside-your-key
- [definition] Configure your provider — Follow the guide for the key management service you use. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/cmek#configure-your-provider

- [snippet] Output: { — `{` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#response
- [parameter] `"global"`: Default. Inference may run in any available geography for optimal performance and availability. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#inference-geo
- [parameter] `"us"`: Inference runs only in US-based infrastructure. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#inference-geo
- [parameter] Global routing opt-out (US only): `allowed_inference_geos: ["us"]`, `default_inference_geo: "us"` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#what-happened-to-your-workspace
- [definition] Inference geo — For how zero data retention (ZDR) applies to this feature, see [API and data retention](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#inference-geo
- [definition] Response — The response `usage` object includes an `inference_geo` field indicating where inference ran: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#response
- [definition] Model availability — The `inference_geo` parameter is supported on Claude 4.6 and later models. Requests with `inference_geo` on Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, or earlier models return a 400 error. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#model-availability
- [definition] Workspace-level restrictions — Workspace settings also support restricting which inference geos are available: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#workspace-level-restrictions
- [definition] Workspace geo — Workspace geo is set when you create a workspace and can't be changed afterward. Currently, `"us"` is the only available workspace geo. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#workspace-geo
- [definition] Pricing — Data residency pricing varies by model generation: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#pricing
- [definition] Batch API support — The `inference_geo` parameter is supported on the [Batch API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing). Each request in a batch can specify its own `inference_geo` value. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#batch-api-support
- [definition] Migration from legacy opt-outs — If your organization previously opted out of global routing to keep inference in the US, your workspace has been automatically configured with `allowed_inference_geos: ["us"]` and `default_inference_geo: "us"`. No code changes are required. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#migration-from-legacy-opt-outs
- [definition] What changed — The legacy opt-out was an organization-level setting that restricted all requests to US-based infrastructure. The new data residency controls replace this with two mechanisms: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#what-changed
- [definition] What happened to your workspace — Your workspace was migrated automatically: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#what-happened-to-your-workspace
- [definition] If you want to use global routing — If your data residency requirements have changed and you want to take advantage of global routing for better performance and availability, update your workspace's inference geo settings to include `"global"` in the allowed geos and set `default_inference_geo` to `"global"`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#if-you-want-to-use-global-routing
- [definition] Pricing impact — Legacy models are unaffected by this migration. For current pricing on newer models, see [Pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#pricing). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency#pricing-impact

## Choose a feed-consumption pattern
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns>

- [snippet] cURL: curl --fail-with-body -sS -G \ — `curl --fail-with-body -sS -G \` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#window-polling
- [snippet] cURL: first_id="activity_01XyDMpzjS89pFZXqSFUBDr6"  # first_id from a previous response — `first_id="activity_01XyDMpzjS89pFZXqSFUBDr6"  # first_id from a previous response` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#cursor-driven-incremental-reads
- [snippet] Cursor-driven incremental reads: cursor = stored_cursor — `cursor = stored_cursor` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#cursor-driven-incremental-reads
- [parameter] Window polling: Your pipeline runs on a fixed schedule, you prefer stateless workers, and you can tolerate replaying or overlapping windows — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#choose-a-feed-consumption-pattern
- [parameter] Cursor-driven incremental reads: You want the lowest latency between an activity occurring and your pipeline ingesting it, you want to avoid re-reading pages you already drained, and you have a durable place to persist a cursor between runs — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#choose-a-feed-consumption-pattern
- [parameter] `actor.user_id`: Your identity provider's stable user identifier — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#correlate-with-your-siem
- [parameter] `actor.email_address`: Directory email when a stable ID is unavailable — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#correlate-with-your-siem
- [parameter] `actor.ip_address`: Network, VPN, and endpoint logs — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#correlate-with-your-siem
- [parameter] `actor.user_agent`: Endpoint and device inventory, and the client app that made the request — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#correlate-with-your-siem
- [parameter] `created_at`: Time-window correlation across any source — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#correlate-with-your-siem
- [parameter] Activity Feed records: Retained for=6 years; Controlled by=Anthropic — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#plan-content-retention
- [parameter] Chat, file, and project content: Retained for=Your organization's claude.ai retention policy, unless a user deletes it sooner; Controlled by=Your organization — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#plan-content-retention
- [parameter] Local session transcripts (sessions on users' machines): Retained for=6 years by default, or your organization's custom conversation retention period when a finite one is set; Controlled by=Anthropic by default; your organization when it sets a custom period — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#plan-content-retention
- [parameter] Remote session transcripts (sessions in the cloud): Retained for=6 years; Controlled by=Anthropic — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#plan-content-retention
- [parameter] Content hard-deleted through the Compliance API: Retained for=Not retained; deletion is immediate and permanent; Controlled by=The caller of the `DELETE` endpoint — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#plan-content-retention
- [definition] Choose a feed-consumption pattern — The Activity Feed supports two consumption patterns: periodic window polling bounded by `created_at.gte` and `created_at.lt`, and cursor-driven incremental reads that persist a cursor from one response and pass it on the next request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#choose-a-feed-consumption-pattern
- [definition] Window polling — Set `created_at.lt` at least 1 minute in the past so that every activity in the window is already queryable. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#window-polling
- [definition] Correlate with your SIEM — Each `Activity` carries fields you can join against events already in your SIEM (Splunk, Datadog, Microsoft Sentinel, Cribl, or similar): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#correlate-with-your-siem
- [definition] Plan content retention — Five retention horizons govern what you can retrieve later: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#plan-content-retention
- [definition] Delivery guarantees and completeness — Treat the Activity Feed as **at-least-once**: a correctly paginated traversal returns every activity at least once, but a retry after a partial failure can re-deliver activities you already stored. Deduplicate on the activity `id` field. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-integration-patterns#delivery-guarantees-and-completeness
