- [parameter] `source`: Type=object; Description=The originating application: `application` (see [Source values](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#source-values)). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#the-prompt-frame
- [parameter] `messages`: Type=array; Description=The conversation transcript up to the point of inference. - [parameter] `session_id`: Type=string or null; Description=Opaque conversation identifier, when one exists. Don't parse it. For Claude Code it is a best-effort, client-asserted session identifier. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#the-prompt-frame
- [parameter] `model`: Type=string or null; Description=Public model identifier for this request, when available. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#the-prompt-frame
- [parameter] `metadata`: Type=object; Description=Reserved extension map of string keys to string values, sent empty today. - [parameter] `text`: `text`: the text content. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#content-blocks
- [parameter] `tool_use`: `id`: the identifier the matching tool result references. `tool_name`: the tool's name. `input`: the arguments the model passed to the tool. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#content-blocks
- [parameter] `tool_result`: `content`: the tool's output as text, with parts joined by newlines; binary parts such as images are replaced by placeholder markers, and raw bytes are never sent. `is_error`: whether the tool call failed. `tool_name`: the tool's name, so a policy can condition on tool identity without cross-referencing an earlier block. `tool_use_id`: the `id` of the matching `tool_use` block. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#content-blocks
- [parameter] `attachment`: `file_name`: the original file name or path. `media_type`: the attachment's media type. `size_bytes`: the size of the original file. `text`: the text content of the attachment when available, such as extracted document text, an audio transcript, or link metadata. Raw attachment bytes are never sent. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#content-blocks
- [parameter] `action`: Constraints=`"allow"` or `"deny"`; required; Semantics=`allow` lets inference proceed; `deny` rejects it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#return-a-verdict
- [parameter] `deny_reason`: Constraints=string or null; at most 500 characters, longer values truncated; Semantics=Shown to the end user when `action` is `deny`; ignored on `allow`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#return-a-verdict
- [parameter] `reference_id`: Constraints=string or null; at most 50 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`; Semantics=Your own identifier for this evaluation. It's recorded on the denial's `inference_hooks_request_denied` [compliance activity](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed) and never shown to the end user. Keep it opaque: no request content and no personal data. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#return-a-verdict
- [parameter] `webhook-id`: Unique identifier for this delivery. Equals the body's `request_id`. Use it as an idempotency key and as the first component of the signed payload. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#verify-the-signature
- [parameter] `webhook-timestamp`: Unix time in seconds, as a decimal string, when the request was signed. Reject a timestamp more than five minutes from your server's clock, in either direction. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#verify-the-signature
- [parameter] `webhook-signature`: One or more space-separated `v1,<base64>` values, each an HMAC-SHA256 over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body bytes}`. Accept the request if any value matches yours, using a constant-time comparison. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#verify-the-signature
- [definition] Get a first verdict round trip — The smallest working integration is a server that reads each request and allows it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#get-a-first-verdict-round-trip
- [definition] Receive a request — Anthropic sends an HTTPS `POST` to the URL your administrator configures. The whole configured URL is the endpoint: there is no fixed path suffix, so choose any path that suits your server. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#receive-a-request
- [definition] The prompt frame — The request body is a JSON object with these fields: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#the-prompt-frame
- [definition] Content blocks — Each entry in `messages` has a `role` of `user` or `assistant` (tool results appear under the `user` role, matching the public Messages API content model) and a `content` array of blocks discriminated by `type`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#content-blocks
- [definition] What the transcript contains — The transcript is the conversation as the end user sees it, up to the point of inference: transcript text, tool calls and their results, extracted attachment text, and prior turns. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#what-the-transcript-contains
- [definition] Source values — `source.application` is an open string, not a closed enum. Known values are `claude-ai` and `claude-code`; [connection tests](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-configuration) use `config-test`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#source-values
- [definition] Return a verdict — Respond with HTTP 200 and a JSON verdict body for both outcomes; the `action` field discriminates. To allow the request: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#return-a-verdict
- [definition] Verify the signature — Requests are signed per the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) specification, using three headers. Anthropic sends the header names in lowercase, and proxies are free to re-case them, so look them up case-insensitively. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#verify-the-signature
- [definition] Timeout and retry — Your administrator sets a verdict timeout between 1 and 10,000ms (5,000ms by default). The budget covers the entire exchange: connection, TLS handshake, request, and response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#timeout-and-retry
- [definition] Webhook failures — Timeouts, non-200 statuses (redirects included), unparseable or oversized response bodies, and unreachable endpoints are all webhook failures. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#webhook-failures
- [definition] Circuit breaker — Sustained webhook failures attributable to your AI security server trip a circuit breaker that stops enforcement: Anthropic stops contacting your server, and failure handling applies to every request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#circuit-breaker
- [definition] Latency — Enforcement adds your AI security server's round trip to the latency of every governed request in your organization. Keep the verdict fast, and load-test your server before rolling it out to a large organization. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#latency
- [definition] Source IP addresses — Requests to your AI security server originate from `160.79.106.0/24`, part of Anthropic's published [outbound IP ranges](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/ip-addresses). Allowlist that block, not the inbound ranges on the same page, which don't cover it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#source-ip-addresses
- [definition] Forward compatibility — The protocol grows without breaking correctly written servers. Your server must ignore: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#forward-compatibility
- [definition] Design your integration — A production AI security server makes a few design choices beyond the wire protocol. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks-endpoint#design-your-integration

- [definition] 404 Not Found — The endpoint resolved but the resource ID does not exist or has already been deleted. - [definition] 409 Conflict — The request is well-formed and authorized but conflicts with the resource's current state. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-errors#409-conflict
- [definition] 429 Too Many Requests — Requests to the Compliance API are limited to **600 requests per minute per [parent organization](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api#how-the-compliance-api-works)**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-errors#429-too-many-requests
- [definition] 500 Internal Server Error — A 500 from the Compliance API carries an `x-should-retry: false` response header when the failure is deterministic. Anthropic SDKs honor this header automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-errors#500-internal-server-error

- [parameter] `{"type": "discovery"}`: The provider serves `/.well-known/openid-configuration` at the issuer URL. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#federation-issuers
- [parameter] `{"type": "explicit_url", "url": "..."}`: Point at a JWKS endpoint directly. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#federation-issuers
- [parameter] `{"type": "inline", "keys": [...]}`: Upload the key set for providers that are not reachable from the public internet. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#federation-issuers
- [definition] Prerequisites — Every request on this page authenticates with an OAuth bearer token that carries the `org:admin` scope. The scope is granted only to organization members with the admin, owner, or primary owner role, and it grants access to the whole organization: any workspace binding is ignored. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#prerequisites
- [definition] Interactive (your terminal) — Log in with the [`ant` CLI](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/cli/quickstart) under a dedicated profile, requesting the `org:admin` scope (see [Admin access](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/cli/authentication#admin-access)), then export the bearer token. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#interactive-your-terminal
- [definition] Workload (CI and automation) — Create a federation rule with `oauth_scope: org:admin` that targets a service account whose `organization_role` is `admin`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#workload-ci-and-automation
- [definition] Bootstrap a workload to manage WIF — One Console-created rule is enough to put the rest of your federation configuration under infrastructure as code: grant a single trusted workload the `org:admin` scope, and let that workload manage federation issuers and every workspace-scoped federation rule through this API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#bootstrap-a-workload-to-manage-wif
- [definition] Create the org:admin rule in the Console — In the Claude Console, go to **Settings → Workload identity** and select **Connect workload** to create one federation rule for your automation workload, for example a GitHub Actions workflow in your infrastructure repository. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#bootstrap-a-workload-to-manage-wif
- [definition] Exchange the workload's identity token — A workload that uses one of the SDKs or the `ant` CLI does not perform the exchange itself. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#bootstrap-a-workload-to-manage-wif
- [definition] Manage issuers and workspace-scoped rules through the API — With the client configured (or, for curl, the minted token in `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`), the workload creates and manages your federation configuration using the endpoints on this page. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#bootstrap-a-workload-to-manage-wif
- [definition] Authentication — All endpoints live under `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/`. Every request to the federation and service-account endpoints needs the API version header and the bearer token: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#authentication
- [definition] Service accounts — A [service account](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#service-accounts) (`svac_...`) is the non-human identity that a federated token acts as. Set `organization_role` to `developer`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#service-accounts
- [definition] Federation issuers — A [federation issuer](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#federation-issuers) (`fdis_...`) registers an OIDC identity provider with your organization. The `jwks` field is a discriminated union that controls how Anthropic fetches the provider's signing keys: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#federation-issuers
- [definition] Federation rules — A [federation rule](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#federation-rules) (`fdrl_...`) binds an issuer to a service account: JWTs from the issuer that satisfy the rule's match conditions can mint tokens that act as the rule's target. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#federation-rules
- [definition] Pagination and archiving — The service-account, federation-issuer, and federation-rule list endpoints accept `limit` (1 to 100, default 20) and a `page` cursor taken from the previous response. Pass the response's `next_page` value as the `page` query parameter on the next request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#pagination-and-archiving

- [parameter] `user_actor`: When it appears=A signed-in claude.ai or Claude Console user took the action.; Key fields=`email_address`, `user_id`, `ip_address`, `user_agent` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed#understand-the-activity-object
- [parameter] `api_actor`: When it appears=A request called the Claude API or the Compliance API with a customer-issued API key. - [parameter] `admin_api_key_actor`: When it appears=An organization admin used an Admin API key to manage users, invites, workspaces, or API keys.; Key fields=`admin_api_key_id`, `ip_address`, `user_agent` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed#understand-the-activity-object
- [parameter] `unauthenticated_user_actor`: When it appears=An action occurred before sign-in completed, for example `sso_login_initiated`.; Key fields=`unauthenticated_email_address`, `ip_address`, `user_agent` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed#understand-the-activity-object
- [parameter] `anthropic_actor`: When it appears=Anthropic acted on the organization, for example through internal tooling.; Key fields=`email_address` (always `null`; present for shape consistency with `user_actor`, because Anthropic operators are not represented by individual email) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed#understand-the-activity-object
- [parameter] `scim_directory_sync_actor`: When it appears=An identity provider (such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or JumpCloud) pushed a change through SCIM directory sync.; Key fields=`workos_event_id`, `directory_id`, `idp_connection_type` (nullable; for example `OktaSCIMV2`, `AzureSCIMV2`) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed#understand-the-activity-object
- [definition] Filter activities — Filter by organization, actor, activity type, or a `created_at` time window using the dotted sub-parameters `created_at.gte`, `.gt`, `.lte`, and `.lt`. See the [API reference](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/compliance/activities/list) for each parameter's type and accepted values. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed#filter-activities
- [definition] Paginate results — Activities are returned newest first, with ties in `created_at` broken by activity ID, and capped at `limit` results in each response (default 100, max 5,000). See the [API reference](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/compliance/activities/list) for the full response schema. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed#paginate-results
- [definition] Understand the Activity object — Every entry in `data` is an Activity with this top-level shape: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-activity-feed#understand-the-activity-object

- [definition] Organization rate limits — The `/v1/organizations/rate_limits` endpoint returns the rate limits applied at the organization level for the Messages API and its supporting resources. Limits for other products, such as [Claude Managed Agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview), are not included. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/rate-limits-api#organization-rate-limits
- [definition] Look up the limits for a specific model — Pass any model ID or alias as the `model` query parameter to return only the entry that contains it: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/rate-limits-api#look-up-the-limits-for-a-specific-model
- [definition] Workspace rate limits — The `/v1/organizations/workspaces/{workspace_id}/rate_limits` endpoint returns the rate limit overrides configured for a single workspace. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/rate-limits-api#workspace-rate-limits
- [definition] Filtering by group type — Both endpoints accept an optional `group_type` query parameter that restricts the response to a single category: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/rate-limits-api#filtering-by-group-type
- [definition] Pagination — Both endpoints accept a `page` query parameter and return a `next_page` field. Responses are currently always a single page, so `next_page` is `null`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/rate-limits-api#pagination
- [definition] Which model strings appear in the `models` list? — Every model ID and alias that counts against the group, including dated IDs (such as `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`) and undated aliases (such as `claude-sonnet-4-5`). Look up any model string you pass to the Messages API and you'll find it in exactly one `model_group` entry. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/rate-limits-api#which-model-strings-appear-in-the-models-list
- [definition] What does it mean if a group is missing from the workspace response? — The workspace has no override for that group and inherits the organization-level limit. Query the organization endpoint to see the inherited values. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/rate-limits-api#what-does-it-mean-if-a-group-is-missing-from-the-workspace-response
- [definition] Can I update rate limits with this API? — No. To set workspace rate limits, open the workspace in the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/settings/workspaces) and use the **Rate limits** tab. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/rate-limits-api#can-i-update-rate-limits-with-this-api

- [parameter] **Spend limits**: Endpoints=`GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/effective` `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/{spend_limit_id}` `POST /v1/organizations/spend_limits` `DELETE /v1/organizations/spend_limits/{spend_limit_id}`; Use for=Read each member's effective spend limit and period-to-date spend; set or clear a per-user override. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#overview
- [parameter] **Spend limit increase requests**: Endpoints=`GET /v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests` `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/{id}` `POST /v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/{id}/approve` `POST /v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/{id}/deny`; Use for=List members' requests for a higher spend limit, with the context needed to decide; approve or… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#overview
- [parameter] `pending`: Awaiting admin action. The request normally carries a live `spend_summary` so you can see the member's current effective spend limit and period-to-date spend while deciding; `spend_summary` may be `null` if it could not be computed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#increase-request-lifecycle
- [parameter] `approved`: The request was resolved with approval: either an admin approved it explicitly, another admin action raised the member's spend limit, or Anthropic support raised a spend limit on the organization's behalf. `spend_summary` is `null`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#increase-request-lifecycle
- [parameter] `denied`: An admin declined. `spend_summary` is `null`. claude.ai hides that member's request button for 30 days from `resolved_at`; an admin can still raise the member's spend limit directly at any time. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#increase-request-lifecycle
- [definition] Overview — The API exposes eight endpoints across two resources: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#overview
- [definition] Quick start — List every member's effective monthly spend limit and period-to-date spend: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#quick-start
- [definition] The spend limit hierarchy — An **effective spend limit** applies to each member's spend, resolved from a hierarchy of scope levels. When a member has no per-user override, they inherit the spend limit configured for their group (if your organization uses group-based limits), their seat tier, or the organization-wide default. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#the-spend-limit-hierarchy
- [definition] Period — `period` is the recurring window over which the spend limit is enforced and spend resets. A spend limit is identified by its `(scope, period)` pair. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#period
- [definition] Amounts and currency — All monetary values are strings in **minor units of the organization's billing currency** (cents, for USD). For example, `"50000"` represents 500.00 USD. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#amounts-and-currency
- [definition] Increase request lifecycle — A **spend limit increase request** is created when a member clicks **Request more usage** in claude.ai. Requests are not created through this API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#increase-request-lifecycle
- [definition] Rate limiting — All eight endpoints share a single per-organization limit of **60 requests per minute**. Requests over the limit return **429 Too Many Requests**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#rate-limiting
- [definition] Pagination — `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/effective` and `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests` are paginated with an **opaque cursor**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#pagination
- [definition] Serializing list parameters — List parameters use bracket notation: repeat the parameter name with `[]` for each value. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#serializing-list-parameters
- [definition] Error responses — Error responses follow the standard shape documented in [Errors](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors). Quote the `request_id` from the response body when contacting support. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#error-responses
- [definition] List each member's effective spend limit — `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/effective` returns one row per current member, reflecting each member's effective spend limit, its `source` in the scope hierarchy, and their `period_to_date_spend`. Requires the `read:spend_limits` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#list-each-members-effective-spend-limit
- [definition] Get a single spend limit — `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/{spend_limit_id}` returns one configured spend limit by ID. Use it to inspect the row that a `spend_limit_id` field referenced. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#get-a-single-spend-limit
- [definition] Set a per-user override — `POST /v1/organizations/spend_limits` sets a per-user spend limit override. This is an upsert keyed on `(scope, period)`: setting a limit for a user and period that already has one overwrites it in place. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#set-a-per-user-override
- [definition] Remove a per-user override — `DELETE /v1/organizations/spend_limits/{spend_limit_id}` removes a per-user override, after which the member falls back to any inherited seat-tier, group, or organization default. Seat-tier, group, and organization-level rows cannot be deleted through this endpoint. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#remove-a-per-user-override
- [definition] List increase requests — `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests` lists requests, most recent first. Filter by `status[]` (`pending`, `approved`, `denied`) and `actor_ids[]`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#list-increase-requests
- [definition] Get a single increase request — `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/{id}` returns one request by ID. Requires the `read:spend_limits` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#get-a-single-increase-request
- [definition] Approve an increase request — `POST /v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/{id}/approve` approves a pending request: it writes a per-user spend limit at the admin-supplied `amount` for the requester and transitions the request to `approved`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#approve-an-increase-request
- [definition] Deny an increase request — `POST /v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/{id}/deny` denies a pending request. Idempotent on `denied`: denying an already-denied request returns 200 with the existing resource. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#deny-an-increase-request
- [definition] Example workflows — Some of these workflows combine the Spend Limits API with the [Analytics APIs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/analytics-api) cost endpoints. The Analytics cost endpoints are designed for organization-wide spend reporting across a date range. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#example-workflows
- [definition] Automate the increase-request review flow — Run a scheduled job that fetches pending requests, applies your organization's approval policy, and resolves each one. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#automate-the-increase-request-review-flow
- [definition] Identify members close to their spend limit — Find members approaching their cap so you can raise it before they're blocked. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#identify-members-close-to-their-spend-limit
- [definition] Find members with rapidly changing usage — Surface members whose spend has jumped week over week. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#find-members-with-rapidly-changing-usage
- [definition] Temporarily raise a member's spend limit during an incident — Give an incident responder room to work while an incident is open: raise their spend cap when the incident starts, and roll it back after the incident closes. Gate the raise on your incident management system, for example by requiring a live incident ID with the member assigned to it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#temporarily-raise-a-members-spend-limit-during-an-incident
- [definition] Does setting a spend limit directly resolve a member's pending increase request? — No. `POST /v1/organizations/spend_limits` writes the override but leaves the pending request untouched. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#does-setting-a-spend-limit-directly-resolve-a-members-pending-increase-request
- [definition] What happens when I delete a per-user override? — The member falls back to whatever they'd inherit from the hierarchy: their group, seat-tier, or organization default. If no default exists at any level, the member is unlimited. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#what-happens-when-i-delete-a-per-user-override
- [definition] Can I set a seat-tier or organization-wide default through this API? — No. Only per-user overrides can be written through this API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#can-i-set-a-seat-tier-or-organization-wide-default-through-this-api
- [definition] Why does `period_to_date_spend` sometimes read as `"0"` for an active member? — The spend reading can be temporarily unavailable, in which case the field reads `"0"` rather than erroring. Treat it as informational. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api#why-does-period-to-date-spend-sometimes-read-as-0-for-an-active-member

- [definition] How is the default workspace represented? — Usage and costs attributed to the default workspace have a `null` value for `workspace_id`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api#how-is-the-default-workspace-represented

- [definition] Use STS web identity tokens (recommended) — The AWS STS `GetWebIdentityToken` API returns an OIDC token signed by AWS that asserts the caller's IAM identity. Because it uses the workload's ambient AWS credentials, the same integration covers Lambda, EC2, ECS, and EKS. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#use-sts-web-identity-tokens-recommended
- [definition] Enable outbound web identity federation for the account — This is an account-level flag, off by default. In the AWS console, open **IAM**, choose **Account settings**, and enable **Outbound web identity federation**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#configure-aws
- [definition] Grant the workload's IAM role permission to call the API — Attach this policy to the IAM role that your Lambda function, EC2 instance, or ECS task runs as: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#configure-aws
- [definition] Find your account's STS issuer URL — After enabling outbound federation, the **IAM > Account settings** page shows a **Get Token Issuer URL** field with a value of the form `https://<uuid>.tokens.sts.global.api.aws`. This URL is unique to your AWS account; copy it for the next step. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#configure-aws
- [definition] Configure Anthropic — In the Claude Console, open **Settings → Workload identity**, click **Connect workload**, and select the **AWS** tile. The wizard walks you through registering the issuer, creating a service account, and creating a federation rule. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#configure-anthropic
- [definition] Acquire and use the token — Call `GetWebIdentityToken` with `https://api.anthropic.com` as the audience, then pass the result to the SDK's federation credentials. The token provider is a callable, so the SDK re-invokes STS on each refresh. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#acquire-and-use-the-token
- [definition] Verify the setup — From inside the workload, exchange an STS-issued token directly and inspect the response: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#verify-the-setup
- [definition] Use EKS projected service-account tokens — If your workload runs in an EKS pod, you can skip the STS call and read a Kubernetes-projected service-account token directly from disk. Kubernetes natively projects an OIDC-compatible token into the pod, and the SDK can read it from a file path, so no token-provider callable is required. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#use-eks-projected-service-account-tokens
- [definition] Find your cluster's OIDC issuer URL — Each EKS cluster has a unique OIDC issuer. Retrieve it with the AWS CLI: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#configure-your-eks-cluster
- [definition] Create the service account and project an Anthropic-audience token — The EKS pod identity webhook detects the `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` annotation and automatically projects a token with `aud: sts.amazonaws.com`, exposing its path as `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`. That token is for AWS role assumption. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#configure-your-eks-cluster
- [definition] Note the token's claim shape — The projected token is a JSON Web Token (JWT) signed by your cluster's OIDC issuer. Its `sub` claim follows the Kubernetes convention `system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<service-account-name>`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#configure-your-eks-cluster
- [definition] Configure Anthropic — In the Claude Console, open **Settings → Workload identity**, click **Connect workload**, and select the **AWS** tile. The wizard walks you through registering the issuer, creating a service account, and creating a federation rule. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#configure-anthropic
- [definition] Acquire and use the token — Inside the pod, the projected token is at `/var/run/secrets/anthropic.com/token` (exposed as `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` in the Pod spec). Pass that file to the SDK's federation credentials and the SDK handles the exchange and refresh. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#acquire-and-use-the-token
- [definition] Verify the setup — From inside the pod, exchange the projected token directly and inspect the response: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#verify-the-setup
- [definition] Scope your rule — A `subject_prefix` of `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/*` matches every IAM role in the account. Any principal that can assume any matching role can obtain a federated Anthropic token. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/aws#scope-your-rule

- [definition] Use a managed identity — Use this path when your workload runs on a VM, a VM Scale Set, App Service, Functions, or Container Apps. The workload requests an Entra-issued JWT for its assigned managed identity from the platform's local token endpoint, then exchanges that JWT with Anthropic. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#use-a-managed-identity
- [definition] Attach a managed identity — Enable a system-assigned or user-assigned managed identity on your Azure resource. In the Azure portal, open the resource, go to **Identity**, and turn on **System assigned** (or attach a user-assigned identity). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-the-managed-identity
- [definition] Find the platform's token endpoint — The platform exposes a local token endpoint once the identity is attached: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-the-managed-identity
- [definition] Decode a sample token — Request a token from the endpoint and decode its payload to confirm the claims your federation rule needs to match. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-the-managed-identity
- [definition] Configure Anthropic — In the Claude Console, open **Settings → Workload identity**, click **Connect workload**, and select the **Microsoft Entra** tile. The wizard walks you through registering the issuer, creating a service account, and creating a federation rule. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-anthropic
- [definition] Acquire and use the token — At runtime your workload fetches its Entra token, exchanges it at `POST /v1/oauth/token`, and uses the returned bearer token to call Claude. Each Anthropic SDK handles the exchange and refresh loop when you supply a token-provider callable, as shown in the following examples. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#acquire-and-use-the-token
- [definition] Verify the setup — From your Azure resource, run the cURL exchange shown in [Acquire and use the token](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#acquire-and-use-the-token) and confirm that `POST /v1/oauth/token` returns a `200` with an `access_token` beginning with `sk-ant-oat01-` and an… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#verify-the-setup
- [definition] Use Entra Workload Identity on AKS — Use this path when your workload runs in an AKS pod. Entra Workload Identity federates a Kubernetes service account with a user-assigned managed identity: Kubernetes projects a service account token (signed by the AKS cluster's OIDC issuer) into the pod at the path in `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#use-entra-workload-identity-on-aks
- [definition] Enable the OIDC issuer and workload identity on your cluster — Enabling workload identity installs the `azure-workload-identity` mutating webhook for you; deploy it manually only on non-AKS clusters. Capture the cluster's OIDC issuer URL for the federated credential you create in a later step. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-entra-workload-identity
- [definition] Create a user-assigned managed identity — Capture two values from the identity: the **Client ID** goes into the service account annotation (and is injected into the pod as `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`), and the **Object (principal) ID** appears as the `oid` claim that your Anthropic federation rule matches. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-entra-workload-identity
- [definition] Create the annotated Kubernetes service account — The `azure-workload-identity` webhook reads the `azure.workload.identity/client-id` annotation to inject `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` into the pod, which the samples in [Acquire and use the token](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#acquire-and-use-the-token-2) read from the… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-entra-workload-identity
- [definition] Create the federated credential on the managed identity — The federated credential trusts your cluster's OIDC issuer for that specific service account. The `--audience api://AzureADTokenExchange` value is Entra's fixed audience for incoming Kubernetes service account tokens; it is unrelated to the Claude API audience you registered earlier. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-entra-workload-identity
- [definition] Label the pod and set its service account — The pod must carry the `azure.workload.identity/use: "true"` label and run as the annotated service account. The webhook then injects `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, and `AZURE_TENANT_ID` into the pod. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-entra-workload-identity
- [definition] Decode a sample token — The token your Anthropic federation rule sees is not the projected file; it is the Entra-issued token returned by the `client_credentials` exchange. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-entra-workload-identity
- [definition] Configure Anthropic — In the Claude Console, open **Settings → Workload identity**, click **Connect workload**, and select the **Microsoft Entra** tile. The wizard walks you through registering the issuer, creating a service account, and creating a federation rule. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#configure-anthropic
- [definition] Acquire and use the token — At runtime the pod performs the two-hop exchange: it sends the Kubernetes-projected token (the file at `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`) to Entra's token endpoint as a federated `client_credentials` assertion, then exchanges the resulting Entra access token at `POST /v1/oauth/token`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#acquire-and-use-the-token
- [definition] Verify the setup — From inside a labeled pod, run the cURL exchange shown in [Acquire and use the token](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#acquire-and-use-the-token-2) and confirm that `POST /v1/oauth/token` returns a `200` with an `access_token` beginning with `sk-ant-oat01-` and… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#verify-the-setup
- [definition] If your tokens are v1.0 — This guide configures the audience app registration with `api.requestedAccessTokenVersion: 2`, so every token it shows is v2.0. If you reuse an existing registration that leaves `requestedAccessTokenVersion` unset, Entra issues v1.0 tokens instead. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#if-your-tokens-are-v10
- [definition] Scope your rule — A federation rule can match the token's subject with `subject_prefix` in addition to (or instead of) the `claims` map; see [Rule matching semantics](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#rule-matching-semantics) for how the fields combine. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/azure#scope-your-rule

- [definition] Configure SPIRE — The instructions in this section are SPIRE-specific. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/spiffe#configure-spire
- [definition] Verify the JWT issuer — Anthropic validates a JWT-SVID by matching its `iss` claim against a registered federation issuer and fetching the JWKS from that issuer's discovery document. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/spiffe#verify-the-jwt-issuer
- [definition] Register the workload — Each workload that calls the Claude API needs a SPIRE registration entry that maps its runtime selectors to a SPIFFE ID. If the workload is already registered, note its SPIFFE ID, which you use in the federation rule's `subject_prefix`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/spiffe#register-the-workload
- [definition] Run spiffe-helper — [spiffe-helper](https://github.com/spiffe/spiffe-helper) is a sidecar utility that connects to the SPIRE Agent socket, fetches a JWT-SVID for a given audience, writes it to a file, and re-fetches it before expiry. The helper runs in daemon mode by default. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/spiffe#run-spiffe-helper
- [definition] Configure Anthropic — In the Claude Console, open **Settings → Workload identity**, click **Connect workload**, and select **Custom OIDC**. - [definition] Acquire and use the token — The Anthropic SDKs can either read the JWT-SVID from the file that spiffe-helper maintains or call the SPIFFE Workload API directly through a token-provider callable. The file path is the simplest integration and works in every SDK language. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/spiffe#acquire-and-use-the-token
- [definition] Verify the setup — Before wiring the SDK in, fetch a JWT-SVID directly from SPIRE Agent and confirm the claims match what your federation rule expects. If you use a different SPIFFE implementation, fetch a JWT-SVID with its CLI or Workload API client and decode the payload the same way. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/spiffe#verify-the-setup
- [definition] Scope your rule — SPIFFE ID path conventions are operator-defined, so the federation rule's `subject_prefix` matcher should reflect the path scheme your registration entries use. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-providers/spiffe#scope-your-rule

- [parameter] `user`: A standard member. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#organization-roles
- [parameter] `managed`: A member whose permissions are granted through the custom roles attached to their groups. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#organization-roles
- [parameter] `owner`: An organization owner. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#organization-roles
- [parameter] `membership_admin`: A member who can manage the organization's members. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#organization-roles
- [parameter] `primary_owner`: The organization's primary owner. There is exactly one. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#organization-roles
- [definition] Which endpoints can your organization use? — The Admin API is a single set of endpoints under `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#which-endpoints-can-your-organization-use
- [definition] Quick start — List the organization's members, newest first: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#quick-start
- [definition] Organization roles — Every member has exactly one organization role. Reads return the member's role as one of five values: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#organization-roles
- [definition] Members and invites — A person becomes a member by accepting an invite (or through your organization's single sign-on, where configured). Creating an invite sends an invitation email; the invite then reads as `pending` until the recipient accepts (`accepted`) or its server-assigned `expires_at` passes (`expired`). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#members-and-invites
- [definition] Groups and roles — Groups connect members to custom roles (role-based access control, the `rbac` in the endpoint paths and scope names). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#groups-and-roles
- [definition] Rate limits — Admin API endpoints share a per-organization limit of **100 requests per minute**; invite creation has its own limit of **1,200 requests per hour** instead. Requests over a limit return **429 Too Many Requests**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#rate-limits
- [definition] Pagination — Member and invite lists use ID-based pagination: pass `limit` (default 20, max 1000) plus at most one of `before_id` or `after_id`, and page using the `first_id` and `last_id` fields of each response until `has_more` is `false`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#pagination
- [definition] Error responses — Error responses follow the standard shape documented in [Errors](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#error-responses
- [definition] List members — `GET /v1/organizations/users` returns the organization's members, most recently added first. Filter by `email` to look up a specific member; the match is case-insensitive and tolerates common variants of the same address (for example, `jane+hiring@example.com` matches `jane@example.com`). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#list-members
- [definition] Get a member — `GET /v1/organizations/users/{user_id}` returns one member by ID. Requires the `read:members` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#get-a-member
- [definition] Change a member's role — `POST /v1/organizations/users/{user_id}` sets the member's role to `user` or `managed`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#change-a-members-role
- [definition] Remove a member — `DELETE /v1/organizations/users/{user_id}` removes the member from the organization, returning any purchased seat they occupied to the organization's pool. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#remove-a-member
- [definition] Create an invite — `POST /v1/organizations/invites` sends an invitation email and returns the invite with a server-assigned `expires_at`. `role` must be `user` or `managed`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#create-an-invite
- [definition] List invites — `GET /v1/organizations/invites` returns the organization's invites, most recent first, across the `pending`, `accepted`, and `expired` states; there is no status filter. Requires the `read:members` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#list-invites
- [definition] Get an invite — `GET /v1/organizations/invites/{invite_id}` returns one invite by ID. Requires the `read:members` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#get-an-invite
- [definition] Withdraw an invite — `DELETE /v1/organizations/invites/{invite_id}` withdraws a `pending` invite, deactivating the link in the invitation email. Withdrawing an `accepted` invite returns 400 (remove the member instead); withdrawing an `expired` invite returns 400. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#withdraw-an-invite
- [definition] Groups — Groups your enterprise creates directly, in [claude.ai organization settings](https://claude.ai/admin-settings) or through this API (`source_type: "direct"`), support every endpoint in this section. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#groups
- [definition] List groups — `GET /v1/organizations/rbac_groups` returns your enterprise's groups, including identity-provider-managed (`scim`) groups. Requires the `read:rbac_groups` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#list-groups
- [definition] Get a group — `GET /v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{group_id}` returns one group by ID. Requires the `read:rbac_groups` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#get-a-group
- [definition] Create a group — `POST /v1/organizations/rbac_groups` creates a group with the given `name` (1–255 characters) and no roles or members. Requires the `write:rbac_groups` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#create-a-group
- [definition] Rename a group — `POST /v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{group_id}` updates the group. `name` is the only field this endpoint can change. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#rename-a-group
- [definition] Delete a group — `DELETE /v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{group_id}` deletes the group. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#delete-a-group
- [definition] List a group's members — `GET /v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{group_id}/members` returns the group's members (each with their `user_id` and email), oldest first. Only current members of your enterprise's organizations are returned, so a page might contain fewer than `limit` entries while `has_more` is `true`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#list-a-groups-members
- [definition] Add a member to a group — `POST /v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{group_id}/members` adds an organization member to the group by `user_id`. The user must already be a member of one of your enterprise's organizations (the request returns 404 otherwise), and adding someone who is already in the group returns 400. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#add-a-member-to-a-group
- [definition] Remove a member from a group — `DELETE /v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{group_id}/members/{user_id}` removes the member from the group; they remain a member of their organization. The request returns 404 if the user is not a member of the group, and 400 for `scim` groups, whose membership is managed in your identity provider. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#remove-a-member-from-a-group
- [definition] Custom roles — Custom roles are read-only through the API: these endpoints catalog your organization's custom roles (defined in [claude.ai organization settings](https://claude.ai/admin-settings) or provisioned by Anthropic) and the permissions each role grants. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#custom-roles
- [definition] List roles — `GET /v1/organizations/rbac_roles` returns your organization's custom roles. Requires the `read:members` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#list-roles
- [definition] Get a role — `GET /v1/organizations/rbac_roles/{role_id}` returns one role by ID. Requires the `read:members` scope. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#get-a-role
- [definition] List a role's permissions — `GET /v1/organizations/rbac_roles/{role_id}/permissions` returns the role's permissions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#list-a-roles-permissions
- [definition] Audit group membership — 1. List groups and record each group's `id`, `name`, and `roles`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#audit-group-membership
- [definition] Is this a different API from the Admin API? — No. The member and invite endpoints are the same `/v1/organizations/` endpoints that Claude Console organizations use; this page documents their Claude Enterprise behavior. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#is-this-a-different-api-from-the-admin-api
- [definition] Can I assign the owner or membership admin role through the API? — No. The API assigns only `user` and `managed`, on invite creation and role updates. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#can-i-assign-the-owner-or-membership-admin-role-through-the-api
- [definition] Can I create or modify groups through the API? — Yes, with the `write:rbac_groups` scope: create, rename, and delete groups, and add or remove their members. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#can-i-create-or-modify-groups-through-the-api
- [definition] Does an unaccepted invite consume a seat? — On plans with a finite seat pool, yes: a `pending` invite holds a seat. Withdrawing the invite or letting it expire frees the seat. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#does-an-unaccepted-invite-consume-a-seat
- [definition] My organization uses single sign-on. Which operations work? — If your identity provider provisions users automatically (JIT or SCIM), invite creation returns 400. If it manages roles (advanced SSO or advanced SCIM provisioning), role updates return 400. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#my-organization-uses-single-sign-on-which-operations-work
- [definition] What happens to an Admin API key when the person who created it leaves? — The key keeps working. Admin API keys are scoped to the organization, not to individual users, and a key created in claude.ai does not expire. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management#what-happens-to-an-admin-api-key-when-the-person-who-created-it-leaves

An OAuth `org:admin` token can only create or modify rules scoped to `workspace:developer` or `workspace:inference`, and cannot update an issuer that backs a rule with any other scope; see the… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#oauth-scopes
- [parameter] `workspace:developer`: Service account `organization_role`=`admin`; Effective permissions=Claude API access in the rule's workspace only. The scope caps the token below the role. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#permission-boundaries
- [parameter] `org:admin`: Service account `organization_role`=`admin`; Effective permissions=Full Admin API access (organization members, invites, workspaces, API keys, and the rest), minus the OAuth-caller carve-outs; see [constraints](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-admin-api#permissions-and-constraints). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#permission-boundaries
- [parameter] Issuer, rule, and service account `name`: Must match `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, length 1 to 255 characters. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#resource-fields
- [parameter] `workspace_id`: Required on create unless `applies_to_all_workspaces` is true. The workspace (`wrkspc_...`) whose quota, billing, and rate limits apply to tokens minted under this rule. Must be a workspace in the same organization, and the target service account must be a member of that workspace. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#resource-fields
- [parameter] `applies_to_all_workspaces`: Boolean. Set `true` to enable the rule in every workspace in the organization instead of naming one; either this or `workspace_id` is required on create. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#resource-fields
- [parameter] `token_lifetime_seconds`: Integer between `60` and `86400` (1 minute to 24 hours). Default `3600`. Values outside this range are rejected at request time. See [Token lifetime and refresh](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#token-lifetime-and-refresh). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#resource-fields
- [parameter] Scheme: Must be `https`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#url-fields
- [parameter] Port: Must be `443` (explicit or default). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#url-fields
- [parameter] Host: Must be a public DNS hostname for your OIDC provider. Must resolve to public IP addresses; IP literals are not accepted. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#url-fields
- [parameter] Maximum size: The `assertion` JWT must be at most 16 KiB. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwt-verification
- [parameter] Signing algorithm: Only asymmetric algorithms (RSA and ECDSA families: ES256, ES384, ES512, RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512) are accepted. HMAC (`HS256`, `HS384`, `HS512`) and `none` are rejected. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwt-verification
- [parameter] Key ID: The JWT header must carry a `kid` that matches a key in the issuer's JWKS. Tokens without `kid` are rejected. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwt-verification
- [parameter] Required claims: `sub` must be present. `iat` must be present and not in the future. `exp` must be present and in the future. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwt-verification
- [parameter] Single use: An assertion that carries a `jti` claim can be exchanged only once per issuer: repeating an exchange with the same `jti` is rejected as a replay. The issuer's `check_jti` field (enabled by default) controls this check; assertions without a `jti` claim are not subject to it. See the [Federation issuers API reference](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/admin/federation_issuers). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwt-verification
- [parameter] Maximum lifetime: The token's lifetime (`exp` minus `iat`) must not exceed the issuer's configured maximum (1 hour by default, configurable for each issuer in the Claude Console). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwt-verification
- [parameter] Clock skew: A 30-second leeway is applied to `exp`, `nbf`, and `iat`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwt-verification
- [parameter] `subject_prefix`: Type=string; Semantics=Exact match against the JWT `sub` claim. A trailing `*` makes it a prefix match (the `sub` value must begin with the characters before the `*`). Case-sensitive. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#rule-matching-semantics
- [parameter] `audience`: Type=string; Semantics=The JWT `aud` claim must contain this exact string. When `aud` is an array, any element matching exactly satisfies the check. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#rule-matching-semantics
- [parameter] `claims`: Type=map\<string, string>; Semantics=Each key is a top-level claim name and each value is the required exact string value. For nested, numeric, boolean, or complex claims like lists and maps, use `condition` with a CEL expression instead. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#rule-matching-semantics
- [parameter] `condition`: Type=string (CEL); Semantics=A [CEL](https://cel.dev/) expression that must evaluate to `true`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#rule-matching-semantics
- [parameter] `claims`: Type=map; Contents=The full decoded JWT claim set. Nested objects are accessible as nested maps. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#cel-evaluation-environment
- [parameter] 400: Error=`invalid_request_error`; Cause=`federation_rule_id` is malformed or a required request field is missing.; Resolution=Verify the `fdrl_` ID and that the request body includes all required fields. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-errors
- [parameter] 400: Error=`invalid_request_error`; Cause=`workspace_id` is present but is not a well-formed `wrkspc_...` ID or the literal `default`.; Resolution=Fix the `workspace_id` value; the response message names the expected format. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-errors
- [parameter] 401: Error=`authentication_error`; Cause=The JWT `iss` claim does not equal the registered `issuer_url` exactly.; Resolution=Compare byte-for-byte, including trailing slashes and scheme: `jq -rR 'split(".")[1] \| gsub("-";"+") \| gsub("_";"/") \| @base64d \| fromjson \| .iss' <<< "$JWT"`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-errors
- [parameter] 401: Error=`authentication_error`; Cause=JWKS fetch failed, JWKS is stale, or the JWT was signed with a key not in the JWKS.; Resolution=For `inline` mode, update the issuer with the rotated keys. For `discovery` and `explicit_url`, confirm the JWKS endpoint is reachable on port 443; if the issuer recently rotated its signing key, see [Key rotation and… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-errors
- [parameter] 401: Error=`authentication_error`; Cause=The JWT `exp` claim is in the past (beyond the 30-second skew window).; Resolution=Confirm your identity provider is projecting a fresh token and the SDK is re-reading the token file. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-errors
- [parameter] 401: Error=`authentication_error`; Cause=The JWT was verified but its claims do not satisfy the rule's `match` block.; Resolution=Decode the JWT and compare each claim against the rule. `subject_prefix` is case-sensitive. `audience` requires an exact element match. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-errors
- [parameter] 401: Error=`authentication_error`; Cause=The `federation_rule_id` does not exist, is archived, or the JWT is not authorized for it (consolidated to prevent enumeration).; Resolution=Confirm the rule ID in the Claude Console and that the rule has not been archived. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-errors
- [parameter] 401: Error=`authentication_error`; Cause=The federation rule is enabled for more than one workspace and the request omits `workspace_id`. The authentication history entry shows reason `workspace_id_required`.; Resolution=Set `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` (or the `workspace_id` body field on a raw request) to the `wrkspc_...` ID you want the token scoped to. See [Token exchange… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-errors
- [parameter] SDK reports "no credentials" instead of exchanging: Cause=One of `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID`, or `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN[_FILE]` is unset and no profile is active.; Resolution=Set all four variables, or configure a profile. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#common-sdk-side-failures
- [parameter] SDK authenticates with an API key instead of federating: Cause=`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is set and wins precedence.; Resolution=Unset the key or token variable. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#common-sdk-side-failures
- [parameter] `FileNotFoundError` on first request: Cause=The path in `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` does not exist. The SDK opens the file lazily at exchange time.; Resolution=Confirm the projected-token volume is mounted and the path matches. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#common-sdk-side-failures
- [parameter] Token exchange succeeds but a Claude API request returns 403: Cause=The minted token's scope does not grant access to that endpoint.; Resolution=Check the rule's `oauth_scope` against [OAuth scopes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#oauth-scopes). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#common-sdk-side-failures
- [parameter] Authentication fails with empty credential: Cause=A credential environment variable is exported but set to an empty string. Empty values still win their precedence slot.; Resolution=Unset the variable with `unset VAR` rather than `VAR=""`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#common-sdk-side-failures
- [parameter] `discovery` (default): `jwks` shape=`{ "type": "discovery", "discovery_base": "https://..." }` (`discovery_base` is optional; set it when the discovery URL differs from `issuer_url`); Behavior=Anthropic fetches `<discovery_base or issuer_url>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, reads `jwks_uri` from the discovery document, and fetches the JWKS from there.; Use when=Your IdP serves a standard OIDC… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwks-source-modes
- [parameter] `explicit_url`: `jwks` shape=`{ "type": "explicit_url", "url": "https://..." }`; Behavior=Anthropic fetches the JWKS directly from `url`. The `issuer_url` is used only for string comparison against the JWT `iss` claim and is never dialed.; Use when=Your IdP does not serve a discovery document, or discovery is internal-only but the JWKS is publicly reachable. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwks-source-modes
- [parameter] `inline`: `jwks` shape=`{ "type": "inline", "keys": [...] }`; Behavior=You supply the array of JWK objects inline (the `keys` array from the JWKS document, not the wrapper object). Anthropic makes no outbound request. The `issuer_url` is used only for `iss` comparison.; Use when=Air-gapped environments, self-managed Kubernetes clusters with cluster-internal issuer URLs, or when you want explicit… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwks-source-modes
- [definition] Token exchange request — `POST /v1/oauth/token` accepts a JSON body using the [RFC 7523](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7523) `jwt-bearer` grant. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-request
- [definition] Token exchange response — `POST /v1/oauth/token` returns a standard OAuth 2.0 token response ([RFC 6749 §5.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749#section-5.1)): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-response
- [definition] Environment variables — The SDK reads these variables to perform a federated token exchange with no constructor arguments. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#environment-variables
- [definition] Credential precedence — The SDK resolves credentials in this order. The first source that yields a credential wins. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#credential-precedence
- [definition] Profile configuration file — A profile is a named configuration file that the SDK and the `ant` CLI both read. Profiles let you ship federation parameters with your container image or switch between environments without changing code. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#profile-configuration-file
- [definition] Configuration directory — The SDK locates the configuration directory in this order: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#configuration-directory
- [definition] Active profile — The active profile name resolves in this order: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#active-profile
- [definition] OAuth scopes — The `oauth_scope` you set on a federation rule determines which Claude API endpoints the minted access token can call. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#oauth-scopes
- [definition] Permission boundaries — A federation rule's `oauth_scope` is a ceiling: the minted token can never exceed it. The target service account's `organization_role` (`developer` or `admin`) determines which scopes are grantable, so a rule that grants `org:admin` must target a service account with `organization_role=admin`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#permission-boundaries
- [definition] Validation rules — Anthropic enforces these constraints when you create or update issuers and rules, and when verifying an incoming JWT at exchange time. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#validation-rules
- [definition] URL fields — The `issuer_url`, `jwks.discovery_base`, and `jwks.url` fields are validated: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#url-fields
- [definition] Rule matching semantics — A federation rule's `match` block determines whether an incoming JWT is accepted. All populated fields are evaluated with AND semantics: the JWT must satisfy every populated matcher. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#rule-matching-semantics
- [definition] CEL evaluation environment — The `condition` expression has access to a single variable: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#cel-evaluation-environment
- [definition] Token exchange errors — `POST /v1/oauth/token` returns errors in the standard [API error shape](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors). The SDK wraps exchange failures in a typed `FederationExchangeError` (or language equivalent) that exposes the HTTP status, the response body, and the `request_id`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#token-exchange-errors
- [definition] Troubleshoot a failed exchange — A `401` `authentication_error` response is intentionally opaque and its message is always `Authentication failed`; the deny reason is recorded in the authentication history, not in the response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#troubleshoot-a-failed-exchange
- [definition] Decode the JWT — Decode the assertion you sent so you can compare each claim against your issuer and rule configuration: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#troubleshoot-a-failed-exchange
- [definition] Check iss matches the issuer — The decoded `iss` claim must equal the registered `issuer_url` byte for byte, including scheme, port, and any trailing slash. A mismatch on a single character fails verification. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#troubleshoot-a-failed-exchange
- [definition] Check aud matches the rule — The decoded `aud` claim must contain the rule's `audience` value as an exact match. When `aud` is an array, one element must match exactly. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#troubleshoot-a-failed-exchange
- [definition] Check sub and each claims entry — Compare `sub` against the rule's `subject_prefix` (case-sensitive; a trailing `*` is a prefix match, anything else is exact). Compare every key in the rule's `claims` map against the same-named top-level claim. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#troubleshoot-a-failed-exchange
- [definition] Check exp, nbf, and iat — `exp` must be in the future and `nbf`/`iat` must be in the past, within the 30-second skew window. If the workload host's clock has drifted, an otherwise valid token is rejected. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#troubleshoot-a-failed-exchange
- [definition] Check JWKS reachability — For `discovery` mode, fetch `<jwks.discovery_base or issuer_url>/.well-known/openid-configuration` over public HTTPS on port 443 and confirm `jwks_uri` resolves. For `explicit_url`, fetch the JWKS URL directly. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#troubleshoot-a-failed-exchange
- [definition] JWKS source modes — When you register a federation issuer, the `jwks` field controls how Anthropic obtains the public keys used to verify JWT signatures from that issuer. It is a discriminated union keyed on `type`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#jwks-source-modes
- [definition] Key rotation and caching — In `discovery` and `explicit_url` modes, Anthropic caches the fetched JWKS. If your identity provider publishes a new signing key and immediately starts signing tokens with it, exchanges that present those tokens may fail with a signature error for up to 1 minute while the cache refreshes. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/wif-reference#key-rotation-and-caching

## Concepts
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation>
