- [definition] Concepts — You configure three resources in the Claude Console before any workload can federate. Together they express "tokens signed by issuer X, with claims that look like Y, may act as service account Z." — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#concepts
- [definition] Service accounts — A **service account** (`svac_...`) is a named, non-human identity inside your Anthropic organization. It is the principal that a [service account key](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication#key-types) or a federated token acts as. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#service-accounts
- [definition] Federation issuers — A **federation issuer** (`fdis_...`) registers an OIDC identity provider with your organization. Registering an issuer tells Anthropic "JWTs signed by this provider may assert workload identity for my org." — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#federation-issuers
- [definition] Federation rules — A **federation rule** (`fdrl_...`) is the bridge between an issuer and a service account: "when a JWT from issuer X has claims that look like Y, mint a token for service account Z with scope S." — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#federation-rules
- [definition] How it works — 1. **Your IdP issues a JWT to the workload.** On most platforms this is ambient: a Kubernetes projected service-account token, the Google Cloud metadata server, Azure IMDS, or the GitHub Actions OIDC endpoint. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#how-it-works
- [definition] Set up federation — You need the admin, owner, or primary owner role in your Anthropic organization, an OIDC-capable identity provider with a reachable JWKS endpoint (or a JWKS document you can paste, for air-gapped clusters), and a workload that can obtain an identity token from that provider. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#set-up-federation
- [definition] Open Connect workload — In the Claude Console, go to **Settings → Workload identity** and select **Connect workload**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#set-up-federation
- [definition] Choose your provider — Select the tile for your identity provider: GitHub Actions, AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Entra ID, or Kubernetes. Each tile prefills the issuer URL pattern and the match fields that provider's JWTs support. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#set-up-federation
- [definition] Fill in the guided fields — The wizard walks you through the provider-specific fields: the issuer configuration, the match conditions for incoming JWTs, and names for the service account and federation rule it creates. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#set-up-federation
- [definition] Verify the issuer — Optionally select **Verify issuer** to dry-run the issuer configuration before anything is created. Verification confirms Anthropic can fetch and parse the JWKS from the URLs you entered, which catches reachability and configuration mistakes early. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#set-up-federation
- [definition] Test the connection — The wizard creates the issuer, service account, and federation rule, then listens for a successful token exchange for 15 minutes. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#set-up-federation
- [definition] Authenticate from your workload — With federation configured, your workload exchanges its IdP-issued JWT for an Anthropic token at runtime. The SDKs handle the exchange and refresh loop for you. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#authenticate-from-your-workload
- [definition] Construct the SDK client — You can construct the client with explicit credentials or with no arguments. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#construct-the-sdk-client
- [definition] Credential precedence — Every SDK resolves credentials in the same five-tier order: constructor arguments, then `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, then an explicit `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`, then the federation environment variables, then the implicit active profile. The first source that yields a credential wins. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#credential-precedence
- [definition] Migrate from API keys — To switch an existing workload from a static API key to federation without downtime: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#migrate-from-api-keys
- [definition] Token lifetime and refresh — The minted Anthropic token's lifetime is the lesser of (a) the rule's `token_lifetime_seconds` (default 3,600 seconds) and (b) twice the remaining lifetime of the IdP JWT you presented. The result is never less than 60 seconds. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#token-lifetime-and-refresh
- [definition] Identity providers — Each guide covers where the JWT comes from on that platform, what its claims look like, and the issuer and rule configuration to register. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation#identity-providers

- [definition] How workspaces work — Every organization has a **Default Workspace** that cannot be renamed, archived, or deleted. When you create additional workspaces, you can assign members, service accounts, API keys, and resource limits to each one. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#how-workspaces-work
- [definition] Claude Code workspace — When a member of your organization first signs in to [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) with their Claude Console account, Anthropic automatically creates a **Claude Code** workspace in the organization and adds that member to it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#claude-code-workspace
- [definition] Workspace roles and permissions — Members can have different roles in each workspace, allowing fine-grained access control. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#workspace-roles-and-permissions
- [definition] Managing workspaces — Only organization admins can create workspaces. Organization users and developers must be added to workspaces by an admin. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#managing-workspaces
- [definition] Using the Console — Create and manage workspaces in the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/settings/workspaces). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#using-the-console
- [definition] Open workspace settings — In the Claude Console, go to **Settings > Workspaces**. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#create-a-workspace
- [definition] Configure the workspace — Enter a workspace name and select a color for visual identification. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#create-a-workspace
- [definition] Using the Admin API — Programmatically manage workspaces using the [Admin API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#using-the-admin-api
- [definition] API keys and resource scoping — Every request runs in exactly one workspace and can only access resources within that workspace. Which workspace depends on the [key type](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication#key-types): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#api-keys-and-resource-scoping
- [definition] Identify the workspace behind an API response — Claude API responses include an `anthropic-workspace-id` header alongside the `request-id` and `anthropic-organization-id` [response headers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/overview#response-headers). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#identify-the-workspace-behind-an-api-response
- [definition] Workspace limits — You can set custom spend and rate limits for each workspace to protect against overuse and ensure fair resource distribution. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#workspace-limits
- [definition] Setting workspace limits — You can set workspace limits lower than (but not higher than) your organization's limits: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#setting-workspace-limits

- [definition] Environment separation — Create separate workspaces for development, staging, and production: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#environment-separation
- [definition] Team or department isolation — Assign workspaces to different teams for cost allocation and access control: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#team-or-department-isolation
- [definition] Project-based organization — Create workspaces for specific projects or products to track usage and costs separately. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#project-based-organization
- [definition] Plan your workspace structure — Consider how you'll organize workspaces before creating them. Think about billing, access control, and usage tracking needs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#best-practices
- [definition] Use meaningful names — Name workspaces clearly to indicate their purpose (for example, "Production - Customer Chatbot" or "Dev - Internal Tools"). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#best-practices
- [definition] Set appropriate limits — Configure spend and rate limits to prevent unexpected costs and ensure fair resource distribution. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#best-practices
- [definition] Audit access regularly — Review workspace membership periodically to ensure only appropriate users have access. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces#best-practices

- [parameter] Good: On a held-out test set of 10,000 diverse Twitter posts, the sentiment analysis model should achieve: - an F1 score of at least 0.85 - 99.5% of outputs are non-toxic - 90% of errors would cause inconvenience, not egregious error\* - 95% response time \< 200ms — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests#common-success-criteria

## Context window
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary>

- [definition] Context window — The "context window" refers to the amount of text a language model can look back on and reference when generating new text. This is different from the large corpus of data the language model was trained on, and instead represents a "working memory" for the model. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#context-window
- [definition] Fine-tuning — Fine-tuning is the process of further training a pretrained language model using additional data. This causes the model to start representing and mimicking the patterns and characteristics of the fine-tuning dataset. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#fine-tuning
- [definition] HHH — HHH (helpful, honest, harmless) is a research framework that informs how Claude is trained to be beneficial to society. It is distinct from the Claude product tagline, "AI assistant for life and work." — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#hhh
- [definition] Latency — Latency, in the context of generative AI and large language models, refers to the time it takes for the model to respond to a given prompt. It is the delay between submitting a prompt and receiving the generated output. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#latency
- [definition] LLM — Large language models (LLMs) are AI language models with many parameters that are capable of performing a variety of surprisingly useful tasks. These models are trained on vast amounts of text data and can generate human-like text, answer questions, summarize information, and more. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#llm
- [definition] MCP (Model Context Protocol) — Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs. Like a USB-C port for AI applications, MCP provides a unified way to connect AI models to different data sources and tools. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#mcp-model-context-protocol
- [definition] MCP connector — The MCP connector is a feature that allows API users to connect to MCP servers directly from the Messages API without building an MCP client. This enables seamless integration with MCP-compatible tools and services through the Claude API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#mcp-connector
- [definition] Pretraining — Pretraining is the initial process of training language models on a large unlabeled corpus of text. In Claude's case, autoregressive language models (such as Claude's underlying model) are pretrained to predict the next word, given the previous context of text in the document. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#pretraining
- [definition] RAG (Retrieval augmented generation) — Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that combines information retrieval with language model generation to improve the accuracy and relevance of the generated text, and to better ground the model's response in evidence. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#rag-retrieval-augmented-generation
- [definition] RLHF — Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is a technique used to train a pretrained language model to behave in ways that are consistent with human preferences. This can include helping the model follow instructions more effectively or act more like a chatbot. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#rlhf
- [definition] Temperature — Temperature is a parameter that controls the randomness of a model's predictions during text generation. Higher temperatures lead to more creative and diverse outputs, allowing for multiple variations in phrasing and, in the case of fiction, variation in answers as well. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#temperature
- [definition] TTFT (Time to first token) — Time to First Token (TTFT) is a performance metric that measures the time it takes for a language model to generate the first token of its output after receiving a prompt. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#ttft-time-to-first-token
- [definition] Tokens — Tokens are the smallest individual units of a language model, and can correspond to words, subwords, characters, or even bytes (in the case of Unicode). For Claude, a token approximately represents 3.5 English characters, though the exact number can vary depending on the language used. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/glossary#tokens

- [definition] General principles — The techniques in this section and the sections that follow apply to all current Claude models, including Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#general-principles
- [definition] Be clear and direct — Claude responds well to clear, explicit instructions. Being specific about your desired output can help enhance results. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#be-clear-and-direct
- [definition] Add context to improve performance — Providing context or motivation behind your instructions, such as explaining to Claude why such behavior is important, can help Claude better understand your goals and deliver more targeted responses. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#add-context-to-improve-performance
- [definition] Use examples effectively — Examples are one of the most reliable ways to steer Claude's output format, tone, and structure. A few well-crafted examples (known as few-shot or multishot prompting) improve accuracy and consistency. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#use-examples-effectively
- [definition] Structure prompts with XML tags — XML tags help Claude parse complex prompts unambiguously, especially when your prompt mixes instructions, context, examples, and variable inputs. Wrapping each type of content in its own tag (for example, `<instructions>`, `<context>`, `<input>`) reduces misinterpretation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#structure-prompts-with-xml-tags
- [definition] Give Claude a role — Setting a role in the system prompt focuses Claude's behavior and tone for your use case. Even a single sentence makes a difference: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#give-claude-a-role
- [definition] Long context prompting — When working with large documents or data-rich inputs (20k+ tokens), structure your prompt carefully to get the best results: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#long-context-prompting
- [definition] Model self-knowledge — If you would like Claude to identify itself correctly in your application or use specific API strings: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#model-self-knowledge
- [definition] Communication style and verbosity — Claude's latest models have a more concise and natural communication style compared to previous models: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#communication-style-and-verbosity
- [definition] Control the format of responses — There are a few particularly effective ways to steer output formatting: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#control-the-format-of-responses
- [definition] LaTeX output — Claude's latest models default to LaTeX for mathematical expressions, equations, and technical explanations. If you prefer plain text, add the following instructions to your prompt: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#latex-output
- [definition] Document creation — Claude's latest models create presentations, animations, and visual documents with strong instruction following, and usually produce usable output on the first try. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#document-creation
- [definition] Migrating away from prefilled responses — Starting with Claude 4.6 models and [Claude Mythos Preview](https://anthropic.com/glasswing), prefilled responses (providing a partial assistant message for Claude to continue from) on the last assistant turn are no longer supported. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#migrating-away-from-prefilled-responses
- [definition] Tool usage — Claude's latest models are trained for precise instruction following and benefit from explicit direction to use specific tools. If you say "can you suggest some changes," Claude will sometimes provide suggestions rather than implementing them, even if making changes might be what you intended. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#tool-usage
- [definition] Optimize parallel tool calling — Claude's latest models run independent tool calls in parallel. These models will: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#optimize-parallel-tool-calling
- [definition] Overthinking and excessive thoroughness — Claude Opus 4.6 does more upfront exploration than previous models, especially at higher [`effort`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort) settings. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#overthinking-and-excessive-thoroughness
- [definition] Leverage thinking & interleaved thinking capabilities — Claude's latest models offer thinking capabilities that can be especially helpful for tasks involving reflection after tool use or complex multistep reasoning. - [definition] Long-horizon reasoning and state tracking — Claude's latest models handle long-horizon reasoning tasks with strong state tracking. Claude maintains orientation across extended sessions by focusing on incremental progress, making steady advances on a few things at a time rather than attempting everything at once. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#long-horizon-reasoning-and-state-tracking
- [definition] Balancing autonomy and safety — Without guidance, Claude Opus 4.6 may take actions that are difficult to reverse or affect shared systems, such as deleting files, force-pushing, or posting to external services. If you want Claude Opus 4.6 to confirm before taking potentially risky actions, add guidance to your prompt: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#balancing-autonomy-and-safety
- [definition] Research and information gathering — Claude's latest models can find and synthesize information from multiple sources effectively. For optimal research results: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#research-and-information-gathering
- [definition] Subagent orchestration — Claude's latest models orchestrate subagents natively. - [definition] Chain complex prompts — With adaptive thinking and subagent orchestration, Claude handles most multistep reasoning internally. - [definition] Reduce file creation in agentic coding — Claude's latest models may sometimes create new files for testing and iteration purposes, particularly when working with code. This approach allows Claude to use files, especially Python scripts, as a 'temporary scratchpad' before saving its final output. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#reduce-file-creation-in-agentic-coding
- [definition] Overeagerness — Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 have a tendency to overengineer by creating extra files, adding unnecessary abstractions, or building in flexibility that wasn't requested. If you're seeing this undesired behavior, add specific guidance to keep solutions minimal. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#overeagerness
- [definition] Avoid focusing on passing tests and hardcoding — Claude can sometimes focus too heavily on making tests pass at the expense of more general solutions, or may use workarounds like helper scripts for complex refactoring instead of using standard tools directly. To prevent this behavior and get solutions that generalize: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#avoid-focusing-on-passing-tests-and-hardcoding
- [definition] Minimizing hallucinations in agentic coding — Claude's latest models are less prone to hallucinations and give more accurate, grounded, intelligent answers based on the code. To encourage this behavior even more and minimize hallucinations: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#minimizing-hallucinations-in-agentic-coding
- [definition] Improved vision capabilities — Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 have improved vision capabilities compared to previous Claude models. They perform better on image processing and data extraction tasks, particularly when there are multiple images present in context. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices#improved-vision-capabilities
- [definition] Frontend design — Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 build complex, real-world web applications with strong frontend design. Use subagents frequently, provide explicit guidance about when delegation is appropriate, and prefer asynchronous communication between orchestrator and subagents over blocking until each subagent returns. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5#parallel-subagents
- [definition] Construct a memory system — Claude Fable 5 performs particularly well when it can record lessons from previous runs and reference them. Provide a place to write notes, as simple as a Markdown file: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5#construct-a-memory-system
- [definition] Rare cases of early stopping — Deep into a long session, Claude Fable 5 can occasionally end a turn with a text-only statement of intent ("I'll now run X") without issuing the corresponding tool call, or pause to ask permission when it already has enough to proceed. A "continue" or "go ahead and do it end to end" suffices. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5#rare-cases-of-early-stopping
- [definition] Rare cases of context-budget concern — In very long sessions, Claude Fable 5 can occasionally suggest a new session, offer to summarize and hand off, or trim its own work. This is most often triggered when the harness shows a remaining-token countdown to the model. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5#rare-cases-of-context-budget-concern
- [definition] Give the reason, not only the request — Claude Fable 5 tends to perform better when it understands the intent behind a request: context lets it connect the task to relevant information rather than inferring intent on its own. Provide context about why you're asking, especially for long-running agents drawing on multiple workstreams: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5#give-the-reason-not-only-the-request
- [definition] Readability when communicating with the user — In extended or agentic conversations (many tool calls, large working context), Claude Fable 5 can produce text that's hard to follow: dense arrow-chain shorthand, deep implementation detail, references to thinking the user never saw, or overly technical phrasing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5#readability-when-communicating-with-the-user
- [definition] Create a send-to-user tool — When running long, asynchronous agents, give the agent a way to surface a message the user must see exactly as written, without ending its turn: a deliverable (a generated code snippet or a drafted message), a progress update with specific numbers, or a direct reply to a question the user asked… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5#create-a-send-to-user-tool

- [definition] How to measure latency — When discussing latency, you might come across several terms and measurements: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-latency#how-to-measure-latency
- [definition] 1. Choose the right model — One of the most direct ways to reduce latency is to select the appropriate model for your use case. Anthropic offers a [range of models](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview) with different capabilities and performance characteristics. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-latency#1-choose-the-right-model
- [definition] 2. Optimize prompt and output length — Minimize the number of tokens in both your input prompt and the expected output, while still maintaining high performance. The fewer tokens the model has to process and generate, the faster the response will be. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-latency#2-optimize-prompt-and-output-length
- [definition] 3. Stream responses — Streaming is a feature that allows the model to start sending back its response before the full output is complete. This can significantly improve the perceived responsiveness of your application, as users can see the model's output in real time. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-latency#3-stream-responses

## Models
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5>

- [parameter] Claude Fable 5: API model ID=`claude-fable-5`; Description=Anthropic's most capable widely released model, for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#models
- [parameter] Claude Mythos 5: API model ID=`claude-mythos-5`; Description=Shares Claude Fable 5's capabilities without the safety classifiers. Available through Project Glasswing. Successor to Claude Mythos Preview. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#models
- [definition] Refusals, fallback, and billing on Claude Fable 5 — Claude Fable 5 includes safety classifiers that can decline certain requests. Claude Mythos 5 does not include these classifiers, so this section applies to Claude Fable 5 only. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#refusals-fallback-and-billing-on-claude-fable-5
- [definition] Refusals — When Claude Fable 5 declines a request, the Messages API returns `stop_reason: "refusal"` as a successful HTTP 200 response, not an error. The response also reports which classifier declined the request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#refusals
- [definition] Fallback — A request that Claude Fable 5 refuses can usually be served by another Claude model. There are three ways to retry: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#fallback
- [definition] Billing — You are not billed for a request that is refused before any output is generated. When you retry on another model, [fallback credit](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fallback-credit) refunds the prompt-cache cost of switching, so you avoid paying that cost twice. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#billing
- [definition] Availability — Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 both become available on June 9, 2026: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#availability
- [definition] Prompting — Claude Fable 5 responds to the same prompting techniques as other Claude models, with a few differences in how to structure long-context prompts and reasoning instructions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#prompting
- [definition] Adaptive thinking is always on — Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 always have thinking enabled; passing `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` is not supported. To reduce or otherwise control thinking depth, use the [effort](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort) parameter. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#adaptive-thinking-is-always-on
- [definition] Raw thinking content is never returned — The raw chain of thought is never returned on Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. The `thinking.display` setting controls what thinking blocks contain instead: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#raw-thinking-content-is-never-returned
- [definition] Supported features — At launch, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 support: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#supported-features
- [definition] Migrating from earlier models — Step-by-step instructions live in the migration guide: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#migrating-from-earlier-models

- [parameter] The highest available capability: Consider starting with...=Claude Fable 5; Example use cases=Long-running agents, deep reasoning, long-horizon agentic tasks, advanced research — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#model-selection-matrix
- [parameter] Complex agentic coding and enterprise work: Consider starting with...=Claude Opus 5; Example use cases=Multihour autonomous coding agents, large-scale refactoring, complex systems engineering, advanced research, knowledge work, vision-heavy workflows, computer use — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#model-selection-matrix
- [parameter] Frontier intelligence at scale, built for coding, agents, and enterprise workflows: Consider starting with...=Claude Sonnet 5; Example use cases=Code generation, data analysis, content creation, visual understanding, agentic tool use — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#model-selection-matrix
- [parameter] Near-frontier performance with lightning-fast speed and extended thinking at the most economical price point: Consider starting with...=Claude Haiku 4.5; Example use cases=Real-time applications, high-volume intelligent processing, cost-sensitive deployments needing strong reasoning, sub-agent tasks — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#model-selection-matrix
- [definition] Establish key criteria — When choosing a Claude model, consider first evaluating these factors: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#establish-key-criteria
- [definition] Choose the best model to start with — There are two general approaches you can use to start testing which Claude model best works for your needs. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#choose-the-best-model-to-start-with
- [definition] Option 1: Start efficiency-first — For many applications, starting with a faster, more cost-effective model like Claude Haiku 4.5 can be the optimal approach: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#option-1-start-efficiency-first
- [definition] Option 2: Start capability-first — For complex tasks where intelligence and advanced capabilities are paramount, you may want to start capability-first: implement with the strongest starting point for your task, then optimize to more efficient models down the line: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#option-2-start-capability-first
- [definition] Decide whether to upgrade or change models — To determine if you need to upgrade or change models, you should: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#decide-whether-to-upgrade-or-change-models
- [definition] Combine models — Multi-model strategies pair a lower-cost model with a frontier model so that most tokens are billed at the lower rate. The two common patterns are an executor that escalates hard decisions to an advisor, and an orchestrator that delegates bulk work to lower-cost workers. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model#combine-models

- [definition] Migrating to Claude Mythos 5 and Claude Fable 5 from Claude Mythos Preview — [Claude Mythos 5](https://anthropic.com/glasswing) is the access-gated successor to [Claude Mythos Preview](https://anthropic.com/glasswing), the invitation-only research preview. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/migration-guide#migrating-to-claude-mythos-5-and-claude-fable-5-from-claude-mythos-preview
- [definition] Features not available on Claude Mythos 5 and Claude Fable 5 — 1. **Extended thinking and thinking token budgets:** Manual extended thinking (`thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}`) is not supported on `claude-mythos-5` or `claude-fable-5` and returns a 400 error. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/migration-guide#features-not-available-on-claude-mythos-5-and-claude-fable-5
- [definition] Token counting and billing — `claude-mythos-5` and `claude-fable-5` use the same tokenizer as `claude-mythos-preview` (the tokenizer introduced with Claude Opus 4.7). Token counts are roughly unchanged when migrating from `claude-mythos-preview`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/migration-guide#token-counting-and-billing
- [definition] Migrating to Claude Mythos 5 and Claude Fable 5 from Claude Opus 5 — Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 use the same [Messages API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/working-with-messages) and the same [tool use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview) patterns as Claude Opus 5, with the same [1M token context… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/migration-guide#migrating-to-claude-mythos-5-and-claude-fable-5-from-claude-opus-5
- [definition] What changed — 1. **Thinking can no longer be disabled:** On Claude Opus 5, thinking is on by default and can be turned off with `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` at an [effort](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort) level of `high` or below. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/migration-guide#what-changed
- [definition] Migrating to Claude Mythos 5 and Claude Fable 5 from Claude Opus 4.8 — If your code is on Claude Opus 4.7 or earlier, first apply the relevant [Migrating to Claude Opus 5](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5/migration-guide) from-section for the API-level changes from your current model, then the remaining delta in this section. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/migration-guide#migrating-to-claude-mythos-5-and-claude-fable-5-from-claude-opus-48
- [definition] What changed — The items in this section describe the API and behavior differences worth checking after you swap the model ID. Except where noted, they apply equally to `claude-fable-5` and `claude-mythos-5`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/migration-guide#what-changed

- [parameter] Orchestrator: Saving in these runs=More than 60% below the frontier model beyond one context window; about half on routine tails; Quality cost=2 to 6 points below the frontier model; Latency=Much faster on large inputs; Where=[Orchestrator strategy](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#orchestrator-strategy-delegate-bulk-work) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#measure-on-your-own-workload
- [definition] Cut spend without losing quality — Prompt caching, token hygiene, batch processing, and a prompt audit against your current model all lower what you pay without lowering output quality. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#cut-spend-without-losing-quality
- [definition] Trim input and context tokens — Most agent requests carry tokens that never influence the answer. Trimming them costs nothing in output quality, although not every lever here saved money when measured. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#trim-input-and-context-tokens
- [definition] Batch work that can wait — The [Batch API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing) takes 50% off every token of a request, including cached ones, in exchange for results arriving any time within 24 hours. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#batch-work-that-can-wait
- [definition] Audit prompts against the current model — Each model generation responds to prompts differently, so a prompt accumulates text written for a model you no longer use. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#audit-prompts-against-the-current-model
- [definition] Trade cost against intelligence — These levers set where a single model sits between cost and intelligence: model choice, effort, re-running failures at a higher setting, and the budgets and caps it works within. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#trade-cost-against-intelligence
- [definition] Compare models on cost per task — Price lists are written per token, and per token the frontier model looks expensive: Claude Fable 5's per-token price is several times Claude Sonnet 5's. You pay for completed tasks, though, so compare models on cost per completed task. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#compare-models-on-cost-per-task
- [definition] Upgrade the model — If you are a model or two behind, the cheapest lever is the model string. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#upgrade-the-model
- [definition] Tune effort — Effort is the most direct way to tune a model to your task. The `effort` parameter governs how much thinking, tool calling, and self-verification the model does, and the default (`high`) suits demanding tasks. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#tune-effort
- [definition] Re-run failures at higher effort — When a task's outcome is checkable, the cheapest policy on the effort curve is not a fixed setting: run every task at a low setting and re-run only the failures at a higher one. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#re-run-failures-at-higher-effort
- [definition] Set budgets and output caps — Most agentic task runs are cheap, but a minority spend many times the median cost on searching, re-verifying, and over-testing. A [task budget](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/task-budgets) targets that tail. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#set-budgets-and-output-caps
- [definition] Combine models — Multi-model architectures fit workloads whose task complexity varies enough that different steps are best served by different models. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#combine-models
- [definition] Advisor strategy: escalate hard decisions — In the advisor strategy, a lower-cost executor model runs the agent loop and performs most turns. When it hits a decision that needs deeper judgment, such as choosing an approach or recovering from a failure, it calls a higher-intelligence advisor model for strategic guidance, then continues. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#advisor-strategy-escalate-hard-decisions
- [definition] Orchestrator strategy: delegate bulk work — In the orchestrator strategy, the frontier model holds the loop. It decomposes the task, dispatches subtasks to lower-cost worker models, and merges their results. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#orchestrator-strategy-delegate-bulk-work
- [definition] Choose between the strategies — Most cases come down to one question: does the work split into independent pieces, or is it one answer reached through a chain of dependent steps? — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#choose-between-the-strategies
- [definition] Measure on your own workload — The numbers on this page reflect list prices at the time of measurement and drift as models and prices change. Your escalation rate, how cleanly tasks split, and transcript length move them too. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#measure-on-your-own-workload
- [definition] Benchmarks referenced — Except where a reference says otherwise, measurements are Anthropic-internal runs of these benchmarks. Unless noted, costs are USD at the list prices in effect when each benchmark ran; Claude Sonnet 5 figures use $2 and $10 per million input and output tokens. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#benchmarks-referenced

- [definition] Effort matters more — Claude Opus 5 converts additional [effort](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort) into better results more reliably than any earlier Opus model, so the effort level you choose carries more weight. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5/whats-new-opus-5#effort-matters-more

- [definition] Model behavior differences — Beyond these API changes, Claude Opus 5 behaves differently from Claude Opus 4.8 in ways you may notice without changing any code. - [definition] Capability improvements — Compared with Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5 is a step-change improvement rather than an incremental one, and it delivers frontier intelligence at half the cost of [Claude Fable 5](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5/whats-new-opus-5#capability-improvements

- [definition] Quick start — `ClaudeLanguageModel` is the entry point. Pass it to `LanguageModelSession` and use the session exactly as you would with any Foundation Models provider: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#quick-start
- [definition] Choosing a model — Model identifiers are values of `ClaudeModel`. Use a compiled-in constant, or construct one with explicit capabilities for an ID that isn't compiled in yet (see [Capabilities](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#capabilities)): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#choosing-a-model
- [definition] Capabilities — Each `ClaudeModel` declares what it accepts: sampling parameters, effort levels, adaptive thinking, structured output, and image input. The package uses this to determine which request fields to send, because sending a field a model rejects is a hard error. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#capabilities
- [definition] Effort — Pin a Claude [effort level](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort) for every request with `fixedEffort:`. It takes precedence over the framework's per-request reasoning hints. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#effort
- [definition] When to use Claude versus the on-device model — Apple's on-device model is fast, private, and available offline, but it is sized for lightweight tasks. Escalate to Claude when you need larger context, frontier reasoning, or server-side tools such as web search and code execution. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#when-to-use-claude-versus-the-on-device-model
- [definition] Authentication — Set the credential with the `auth:` parameter. Use `.appAttest` to ship without a back end, `.proxied` to route requests through your own back end, or `.apiKey` to iterate during development. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#authentication
- [definition] App Attest — Each installation of your app uses Apple's [App Attest](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/establishing-your-app-s-integrity) service to prove that it is a genuine, unmodified build of the app you registered. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#app-attest
- [definition] Proxy (production) — For production, route requests through your own back end with `.proxied`. The relay at `baseURL` adds the Claude API credential server-side, so the app ships no key. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#proxy-production
- [definition] API key (development) — Pass an API key directly while developing: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#api-key-development
- [definition] Streaming — `streamResponse(to:)` returns the response incrementally. Each element is a cumulative snapshot of the response so far, not a delta: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#streaming
- [definition] Structured output — Annotate a type with `@Generable` and request it with `generating:`. The model returns a value of that type through [structured outputs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#structured-output
- [definition] Client-side tools — The framework's `tools:` array works unchanged. Conform your types to `Tool`, pass them to `LanguageModelSession`, and the framework invokes them on the device when Claude calls them. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#client-side-tools
- [definition] Server-side tools — [Server tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools) (web search, web fetch, and code execution) run on Anthropic's infrastructure within a single round trip, with nothing for the framework to invoke on the device. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#server-side-tools
- [definition] Images — Models whose capabilities include image input declare the framework's vision capability. Pass image content through the framework's standard session API; the package converts it to the Claude API's image format. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#images
- [definition] Error handling — The package maps Claude API errors onto Apple's `LanguageModelError` cases where one fits: context-window overflow surfaces as `.contextSizeExceeded`, HTTP 429 as `.rateLimited`, a request past the configured timeout as `.timeout`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#error-handling
- [definition] Feature support — The package surfaces the Messages API capabilities that the Foundation Models provider protocol can express. Features with no representation in Apple's protocol are not available through it, including: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/apple-foundation-models#feature-support

- [definition] Request fields — The anthropic library uses the [`omitzero`](https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.24#encodingjsonpkgencodingjson) semantics from the Go 1.24+ `encoding/json` release for request fields. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#request-fields
- [definition] Request unions — Unions are represented as a struct with fields prefixed by "Of" for each of its variants, only one field can be non-zero. The non-zero field will be serialized. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#request-unions
- [definition] Deserializing params — `param.SetJSON` requires SDK v1.20.0 or later. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#deserializing-params
- [definition] Response objects — All fields in response structs are ordinary value types (not pointers or wrappers). Response structs also include a special `JSON` field containing metadata about each property. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#response-objects
- [definition] Response unions — In responses, unions are represented by a flattened struct containing all possible fields from each of the object variants. To convert it to a variant use the `.AsFooVariant()` method or the `.AsAny()` method if present. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#response-unions
- [definition] Error handling — When the API returns a non-success status code, the SDK returns an error with type `*anthropic.Error`. This contains the `StatusCode`, `*http.Request`, and `*http.Response` values of the request, along with the JSON of the error body (much like other response objects in the SDK). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#error-handling
- [definition] Retries — Certain errors will be automatically retried 2 times by default, with a short exponential backoff. The SDK retries by default all connection errors, 408 Request Timeout, 409 Conflict, 429 Rate Limit, and >=500 Internal errors. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#retries
- [definition] Timeouts — Non-streaming Messages requests time out after 10 minutes by default; other requests have no default timeout. Use context to configure a timeout for a request lifecycle. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#timeouts
- [definition] Long requests — Consider using the streaming Messages API for longer running requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#long-requests
- [definition] File uploads — Request parameters that correspond to file uploads in multipart requests are typed as `io.Reader`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#file-uploads
- [definition] Pagination — This library provides some conveniences for working with paginated list endpoints. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#pagination
- [definition] RequestOptions — This library uses the functional options pattern. Functions defined in the `option` package return a `RequestOption`, which is a closure that mutates a `RequestConfig`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#requestoptions
- [definition] HTTP client customization — For request middleware (`option.WithMiddleware`) and replacing the default `http.Client` (`option.WithHTTPClient`), see [SDK middleware](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#http-client-customization
- [definition] Platform integrations — For detailed platform setup guides with code examples, see: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#platform-integrations
- [definition] Accessing raw response data (for example, response headers) — You can access the raw HTTP response data by using the `option.WithResponseInto()` request option. This is useful when you need to examine response headers, status codes, or other details. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#accessing-raw-response-data-for-example-response-headers
- [definition] Making custom/undocumented requests — This library is typed for convenient access to the documented API. If you need to access undocumented endpoints, params, or response properties, the library can still be used. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#making-customundocumented-requests
- [definition] Semantic versioning — This package generally follows [SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) conventions, though certain backward-incompatible changes may be released as minor versions: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/go#semantic-versioning

- [definition] Retries — The SDK automatically retries 2 times by default, with a short exponential backoff between requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#retries
- [definition] Timeouts — Requests time out after 10 minutes by default. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#timeouts
- [definition] Long requests — Consider using [streaming](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#streaming) for longer running requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#long-requests
- [definition] Pagination — The SDK provides convenient ways to access paginated results either one page at a time or item-by-item across all pages. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#pagination
- [definition] Auto-pagination — To iterate through all results across all pages, use the `autoPager()` method, which automatically fetches more pages as needed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#auto-pagination
- [definition] Manual pagination — To access individual page items and manually request the next page: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#manual-pagination
- [definition] Immutability and builders — Each class in the SDK has an associated builder for constructing it. Each class is immutable once constructed. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#immutability-and-builders
- [definition] Requests and responses — To send a request to the Claude API, build an instance of some `Params` class and pass it to the corresponding client method. When the response is received, it is deserialized into an instance of a Java class. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#requests-and-responses
- [definition] Undocumented parameters — To set undocumented parameters, call the `putAdditionalHeader`, `putAdditionalQueryParam`, or `putAdditionalBodyProperty` methods on any `Params` class: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#undocumented-parameters
- [definition] JsonValue creation — The most straightforward way to create a `JsonValue` is using its `from(...)` method: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#jsonvalue-creation
- [definition] Forcibly omitting required parameters — Normally a `Builder` class's `build` method will throw `IllegalStateException` if any required parameter or property is unset. To forcibly omit a required parameter or property, pass `JsonMissing`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#forcibly-omitting-required-parameters
- [definition] Response properties — To access undocumented response properties, call the `_additionalProperties()` method: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#response-properties
- [definition] Response validation — By default, the SDK does not throw an exception when the API returns a response that doesn't match the expected type. It throws `AnthropicInvalidDataException` only if you directly access the property. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#response-validation
- [definition] HTTPS / SSL configuration — Most applications should not call these methods, and instead use the system defaults. The defaults include special optimizations that can be lost if the implementations are modified. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#https-ssl-configuration
- [definition] Platform integrations — For detailed platform setup guides with code examples, see: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#platform-integrations
- [definition] Raw response access — To access HTTP headers, status codes, and the raw response body, prefix any HTTP method call with `withRawResponse()`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#raw-response-access
- [definition] Logging — The SDK uses the standard OkHttp logging interceptor. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#logging
- [definition] Undocumented API functionality — The SDK is typed for convenient usage of the documented API. However, it also supports working with undocumented or not yet supported parts of the API. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#undocumented-api-functionality
- [definition] Beta features — Beta features are available before general release to get early feedback and test new functionality. You can check the availability of all of Claude's capabilities and tools in the [build with Claude overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#beta-features
- [definition] Semantic versioning — This package generally follows [SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) conventions, though certain backward-incompatible changes may be released as minor versions: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/java#semantic-versioning

- [parameter] HTTP 429: `RateLimitException` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#error-handling
- [parameter] HTTP >= 500: `InternalServerException` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#error-handling
- [parameter] Other HTTP error: `APIStatusException` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#error-handling
- [parameter] Timeout: `APITimeoutException` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#error-handling
- [parameter] Network error: `APIConnectionException` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#error-handling
- [definition] Installation — The SDK uses [PSR-18](https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-18/) for HTTP and discovers any installed PSR-18 client automatically. [Guzzle](https://docs.guzzlephp.org/) is recommended because the SDK configures it for streaming with no additional setup: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#installation
- [definition] Usage — This library uses named parameters to specify optional arguments. Parameters with a default value must be set by name. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#usage
- [definition] Value objects — It is recommended to use the static `with` constructor `Base64ImageSource::with(data: "U3RhaW5sZXNzIHJvY2tz", ...)` and named parameters to initialize value objects. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#value-objects
- [definition] Streaming — The SDK provides support for streaming responses using Server-Sent Events (SSE). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#streaming
- [definition] Error handling — When the library is unable to connect to the API, or if the API returns a non-success status code (that is, a 4xx or 5xx response), a subclass of `Anthropic\Core\Exceptions\APIException` is thrown: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#error-handling
- [definition] Retries — Certain errors are automatically retried two times by default, with a short exponential backoff. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#retries
- [definition] Pagination — List methods in the Claude API are paginated. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#pagination
- [definition] Undocumented properties — You can send undocumented parameters to any endpoint, and read undocumented response properties, as follows: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#undocumented-properties
- [definition] Undocumented request parameters — If you want to explicitly send an extra parameter, you can do so with the `extraQueryParams`, `extraBodyParams`, and `extraHeaders` options under `RequestOptions::with()` when making a request, as seen in the preceding example. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#undocumented-request-parameters
- [definition] Undocumented endpoints — To make requests to undocumented endpoints while retaining the benefit of authentication, retries, and other client features, you can make requests using `client->request`, as follows: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#undocumented-endpoints
- [definition] Platform integrations — For detailed platform setup guides with code examples, see: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#platform-integrations
- [definition] Semantic versioning — This package follows [SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) conventions. As the library is in initial development and has a major version of `0`, APIs might change at any time. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/php#semantic-versioning

- [definition] Getting results from a batch — Once a Message Batch has been processed, indicated by `.processing_status == 'ended'`, you can access the results with `.batches.results()`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#getting-results-from-a-batch

- [definition] Retries — Certain errors are automatically retried 2 times by default, with a short exponential backoff. Connection errors (for example, because of a network connectivity problem), 408 Request Timeout, 409 Conflict, 429 Rate Limit, and >=500 Internal errors are all retried by default. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#retries
- [definition] Timeouts — By default requests time out after 10 minutes. You can configure this with a `timeout` option, which accepts a float or an `httpx2.Timeout` object: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#timeouts
- [definition] Long requests — Consider using the streaming [Messages API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#streaming-responses) for longer running requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#long-requests
- [definition] Auto-pagination — List methods in the Claude API are paginated. You can use the `for` syntax to iterate through items across all pages: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#auto-pagination
- [definition] Default headers — The SDK automatically sends the `anthropic-version` header set to `2023-06-01`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#default-headers

- [definition] Accessing raw response data (for example, headers) — The "raw" `Response` returned by `httpx2` can be accessed through the `.with_raw_response` property on the client. - [definition] Logging — The SDK uses the standard library `logging` module. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#logging
- [definition] Making custom/undocumented requests — This library is typed for convenient access to the documented API. If you need to access undocumented endpoints, params, or response properties, the library can still be used. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#making-customundocumented-requests
- [definition] Configuring the HTTP client — The SDK sends requests with [httpx2](https://httpx2.pydantic.dev), an API-compatible fork of `httpx`. To customize the HTTP client, including proxies and transports, pass your own [httpx2 client](https://httpx2.pydantic.dev/api/#client) as `http_client`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#configuring-the-http-client
- [definition] Managing HTTP resources — By default the library closes underlying HTTP connections whenever the client is [garbage collected](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__del__). You can manually close the client using the `.close()` method if desired, or with a context manager that closes when exiting. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#managing-http-resources

You can determine the version being used at runtime with: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/python#determining-the-installed-version

- [definition] Streaming — The SDK provides support for streaming responses using Server-Sent Events (SSE). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#streaming
- [definition] Streaming helpers — This library provides several conveniences for streaming messages, for example: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#streaming-helpers
- [definition] Input schema and tool calling — The SDK provides helper mechanisms to define structured data classes for tools and let Claude automatically execute them. For detailed documentation on tool use patterns including the tool runner, see [Tool Runner (SDK)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-runner). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#input-schema-and-tool-calling
- [definition] Structured outputs — For complete structured outputs documentation including Ruby examples, see [Structured outputs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#structured-outputs
- [definition] Handling errors — When the library is unable to connect to the API, or if the API returns a non-success status code (that is, 4xx or 5xx response), a subclass of `Anthropic::Errors::APIError` is raised: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#handling-errors
- [definition] Retries — Certain errors will be automatically retried 2 times by default, with a short exponential backoff. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#retries
- [definition] Timeouts — By default, requests time out after 10 minutes. You can use the `timeout` option to configure this: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#timeouts
- [definition] Pagination — List methods in the Claude API are paginated. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#pagination
- [definition] File uploads — Request parameters that correspond to file uploads can be passed as raw contents, a [`Pathname`](https://rubyapi.org/3.2/o/pathname) instance, [`StringIO`](https://rubyapi.org/3.2/o/stringio), or more. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#file-uploads
- [definition] Sorbet — This library provides comprehensive [RBI](https://sorbet.org/docs/rbi) definitions, and has no dependency on sorbet-runtime. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#sorbet
- [definition] Enums — Since this library does not depend on `sorbet-runtime`, it cannot provide [`T::Enum`](https://sorbet.org/docs/tenum) instances. Instead, the SDK provides "tagged symbols", which is always a primitive at runtime: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#enums
- [definition] BaseModel — All parameter and response objects inherit from `Anthropic::Internal::Type::BaseModel`, which provides several conveniences, including: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#basemodel
- [definition] Concurrency and connection pooling — The `Anthropic::Client` instances are threadsafe, but are only fork-safe when there are no in-flight HTTP requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#concurrency-and-connection-pooling
- [definition] Undocumented properties — You can send undocumented parameters to any endpoint, and read undocumented response properties, like so: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#undocumented-properties
- [definition] Undocumented request params — If you want to explicitly send an extra param, you can do so with the `extra_query`, `extra_body`, and `extra_headers` under the `request_options:` parameter when making a request, as seen in the examples above. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#undocumented-request-params
- [definition] Undocumented endpoints — To make requests to undocumented endpoints while retaining the benefit of auth, retries, and so on, you can make requests using `anthropic.request`, like so: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#undocumented-endpoints
- [definition] Platform integrations — For detailed platform setup guides with code examples, see: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#platform-integrations
- [definition] Semantic versioning — This package follows [SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) conventions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/sdks/ruby#semantic-versioning

## Registering middleware
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware>

- [snippet] Registering middleware: sequenceDiagram — `sequenceDiagram` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware
- [snippet] Python: def logging_middleware(request: APIRequest, call_next: CallNext) -> APIResponse[Any]: — `def logging_middleware(request: APIRequest, call_next: CallNext) -> APIResponse[Any]:` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#registering-middleware
- [snippet] TypeScript: import type { Middleware } from "@anthropic-ai/sdk"; — `import type { Middleware } from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#registering-middleware
- [snippet] C#: AnthropicClient client = new() — `AnthropicClient client = new()` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#registering-middleware
- [snippet] Go: client := anthropic.NewClient( — `client := anthropic.NewClient(` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#registering-middleware
- [snippet] Java: AnthropicClient client = AnthropicOkHttpClient.builder() — `AnthropicClient client = AnthropicOkHttpClient.builder()` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#registering-middleware
- [snippet] PHP: $loggingMiddleware = function (RequestInterface $request, callable $next): ResponseInterface { — `$loggingMiddleware = function (RequestInterface $request, callable $next): ResponseInterface {` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#registering-middleware
- [snippet] Ruby: logging_middleware = lambda do |request, call_next| — `logging_middleware = lambda do |request, call_next|` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#registering-middleware
- [definition] Registering middleware — Each middleware is a function that receives the outgoing request and a `next` callable. Call `next` to forward the request to the rest of the chain (or directly to the SDK core if this is the last middleware), and return its response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#registering-middleware
- [definition] Middleware ordering — When you register multiple middleware, they apply in the order given: the first middleware's "before" code runs first, and its "after" code runs last. Middleware registered on the client runs before middleware passed as a per-request option. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#middleware-ordering
- [definition] Replacing the HTTP client — Each SDK also accepts a custom HTTP client (for proxy configuration, custom TLS, or connection pooling). Only one HTTP client is used per SDK client; setting it replaces the default. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#replacing-the-http-client
- [definition] Built-in middleware — The SDKs ship a refusal-fallback middleware that automatically retries requests Claude Fable 5 declines on a fallback model. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/middleware#built-in-middleware

The result prints without JSON quotes and is ready to assign to a shell variable: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/cli/using#extract-a-scalar
- [definition] Passing request bodies — The right input mechanism depends on the shape of the data: use **flags** for scalar fields and short structured values, pipe a **stdin** document for nested or multiline bodies, and use **`@file` references** to pull file contents into any string or binary field. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/cli/using#passing-request-bodies
- [definition] Flags — Scalar fields map directly to flags. Structured fields accept a relaxed YAML-like syntax (unquoted keys, optional quotes around strings) or strict JSON: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/cli/using#flags
- [definition] Stdin — Pipe a JSON or YAML document to stdin to supply the full request body. Fields from stdin are merged with flags, with flags taking precedence. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/cli/using#stdin
- [definition] File references — Flags that take a file path, such as `--file` on the upload command, accept a bare path: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/cli/using#file-references
- [definition] Debugging — Add `--debug` to any command to print the exact HTTP request and response (headers and body) to stderr. API keys are redacted. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/cli/using#debugging
- [definition] Available resources — Every API resource the CLI exposes is documented in the [API reference](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/cli/messages/create). - [parameter] `order`: Location=Query parameter; Description=Sort direction for the results (`asc` or `desc`), on list endpoints that support sorting. A `page` cursor is only valid with the `order` it was created with. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/overview#pagination
- [parameter] `next_page`: Location=Response field; Description=Cursor for the next page, or `null` if there are no more results. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/overview#pagination
- [parameter] `prev_page`: Location=Response field; Description=Cursor for the previous page on endpoints that support backward pagination (currently `GET /v1/sessions`), or `null` if you are on the first page. Other list endpoints omit the field. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/overview#pagination
