- [definition] HTTP errors — The API follows a predictable HTTP error code format: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#http-errors
- [definition] Error shapes — The API always returns errors as JSON, with a top-level `error` object that always includes a `type` and `message` value. The response also includes a `request_id` field for easier tracking and debugging. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#error-shapes
- [definition] SDK error types — The official SDKs raise typed exceptions for these errors instead of returning raw JSON, and the class names and namespaces differ by language. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#sdk-error-types
- [definition] Request ID — Every API response includes a unique `request-id` header. This header contains a value such as `req_018EeWyXxfu5pfWkrYcMdjWG`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#request-id
- [definition] Long requests — Consider using the [streaming Messages API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming) or [Message Batches API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages/batches/create) for long-running requests, especially those over 10 minutes. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#long-requests
- [definition] Prefill not supported — Claude 4.6 and later models and [Claude Mythos Preview](https://anthropic.com/glasswing) do not support prefilling assistant messages. Sending a request with a prefilled last assistant message to any of these models returns a 400 `invalid_request_error`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#prefill-not-supported
- [definition] Thinking blocks cannot be modified — If the most recent assistant message contains `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks that were edited, reordered, filtered out, or reconstructed before being sent back to the API, the request returns a 400 `invalid_request_error`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#thinking-blocks-cannot-be-modified
- [definition] Extended thinking not supported — Claude 4.7 and later models have removed extended thinking. Sending `thinking: {"type": "enabled"}` to any of these models returns a 400 `invalid_request_error`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#extended-thinking-not-supported
- [definition] Adaptive thinking not supported — Models that support only extended thinking (Claude 4.5 and earlier models) reject `thinking: {"type": "adaptive"}` with a 400 `invalid_request_error`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#adaptive-thinking-not-supported
- [definition] Thinking cannot be disabled — On Claude Fable 5, [Claude Mythos 5](https://anthropic.com/glasswing), and [Claude Mythos Preview](https://anthropic.com/glasswing), thinking is always on. Sending `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` to any of these models returns a 400 `invalid_request_error`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#thinking-cannot-be-disabled
- [definition] Outbound web identity federation disabled (Claude Platform on AWS) — If every request to [Claude Platform on AWS](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws) returns `"Outbound web identity federation is disabled for your account"`, run `aws iam enable-outbound-web-identity-federation` once per AWS account. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#outbound-web-identity-federation-disabled-claude-platform-on-aws

- [definition] Reaching your spend cap — Once you reach your tier's spend cap, API usage pauses until 00:00 UTC on the first day of the next month, unless you request a higher limit sooner. While usage is paused, API requests return HTTP 429: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#reaching-your-spend-cap
- [definition] Setting your own spend limit — You can also set your own spend limit below your tier's cap to control costs: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#setting-your-own-spend-limit
- [definition] Navigate to the Billing page — Go to [Settings > Billing](https://platform.claude.com/settings/billing) in the Claude Console. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#setting-your-own-spend-limit
- [definition] Open the spend limit editor — In the **Spend limits** section, click **Adjust limit** (or **Set limit** if no limit is currently set). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#setting-your-own-spend-limit
- [definition] Adjust your spend limit — Enter a new value. Your spend limit cannot exceed your current tier's cap. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#setting-your-own-spend-limit
- [definition] Rate limits — The rate limits for the Messages API are measured in requests per minute (RPM), input tokens per minute (ITPM), and output tokens per minute (OTPM) for each model class. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#rate-limits
- [definition] Cache-aware ITPM — Many API providers use a combined "tokens per minute" (TPM) limit that may include all tokens, both cached and uncached, input and output. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#cache-aware-itpm
- [definition] Message Batches API — The Message Batches API has its own set of rate limits which are shared across all models. These include a requests per minute (RPM) limit to all API endpoints and a limit on the number of batch requests that can be in the processing queue at the same time. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#message-batches-api
- [definition] Managed Agents — [Claude Managed Agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview) endpoints are rate-limited per organization. These limits are separate from the Messages API rate limits above. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#managed-agents
- [definition] Files API — [Files API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files) requests have their own per-organization limit, shared across upload, list, retrieve, download, and delete operations and separate from the Messages API limits described earlier on this page. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#files-api
- [definition] Fast mode rate limits — When using [fast mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode) (research preview) with `speed: "fast"` on Claude Opus 5 or Opus 4.8, dedicated rate limits apply that are separate from standard Opus rate limits. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#fast-mode-rate-limits
- [definition] Monitoring your rate limits in the Console — You can monitor your rate limit usage on the [Usage](https://platform.claude.com/usage) page of the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#monitoring-your-rate-limits-in-the-console
- [definition] Requesting higher limits — To request higher rate limits or a higher monthly spend cap, use **Request rate limit increase** on the [Rate limits](https://platform.claude.com/settings/limits) page. Anthropic support can also raise limits; for urgent needs, contact [Anthropic support](https://support.claude.com). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#requesting-higher-limits
- [definition] Setting lower limits for Workspaces — For more about workspaces, see [Workspaces](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#setting-lower-limits-for-workspaces
- [definition] Response headers — The API response includes headers that show you the rate limit enforced, current usage, and when the limit will be reset. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#response-headers

- [definition] Standard Tier — The standard tier is the default service tier for all API requests. The API prioritizes these requests alongside all other requests with best-effort availability. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers#standard-tier
- [definition] Priority Tier — The API prioritizes requests in this tier over all other requests. This prioritization helps minimize ["server overloaded" errors](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#http-errors), even during peak times. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers#priority-tier
- [definition] How requests get assigned tiers — When handling a request, Anthropic decides to assign a request to Priority Tier in the following scenarios: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers#how-requests-get-assigned-tiers
- [definition] Using service tiers — You can control which service tiers can be used for a request by setting the `service_tier` parameter: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers#using-service-tiers
- [definition] Supported models — Priority Tier is supported on all available Claude models except Claude Mythos 5, [Claude Mythos Preview](https://anthropic.com/glasswing), Claude Opus 5, and Claude Sonnet 5. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers#supported-models

- [snippet] Trigger a routine: POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/claude_code/routines/{routine_id}/fire — `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/claude_code/routines/{routine_id}/fire` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#trigger-a-routine

- [snippet] GitHub Actions: - if: failure() — `- if: failure()` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#trigger-a-routine
- [snippet] Response: { — `{` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#response
- [snippet] Errors: { — `{` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#errors
- [parameter] Authentication: This endpoint=`Authorization: Bearer` with a per-routine token (`sk-ant-oat01-...`) created at [claude.ai/code/routines](https://claude.ai/code/routines); Claude Platform APIs=`x-api-key` with a Claude API key from Claude Console — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#differences-from-the-claude-platform
- [parameter] Token scope: This endpoint=One routine only; no read access; Claude Platform APIs=Workspace-level — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#differences-from-the-claude-platform
- [parameter] SDK support: This endpoint=None; Claude Platform APIs=Available in all [client SDKs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/overview) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#differences-from-the-claude-platform
- [parameter] Billing: This endpoint=Claude Code subscription usage on claude.ai; Claude Platform APIs=Claude Platform usage — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#differences-from-the-claude-platform
- [parameter] Path namespace: This endpoint=`/v1/claude_code/...`; Claude Platform APIs=`/v1/...` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#differences-from-the-claude-platform
- [parameter] Stability: This endpoint=Experimental; requires `anthropic-beta: experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01`; Claude Platform APIs=Stable or standard beta — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#differences-from-the-claude-platform
- [parameter] `Authorization`: Required=Yes; Description=`Bearer <token>`. The per-routine token created in the Claude Code web UI, prefixed `sk-ant-oat01-`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#headers
- [parameter] `anthropic-beta`: Required=Yes; Description=Must include `experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#headers
- [parameter] `anthropic-version`: Required=Yes; Description=The [API version](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/versioning), for example `2023-06-01`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#headers
- [parameter] `Content-Type`: Required=When body is present; Description=`application/json`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#headers
- [parameter] `routine_id`: Type=string; Description=The routine's identifier. Despite the parameter name, the value is prefixed `trig_` rather than `routine_`. Included in the URL the modal window shows when you add an API trigger. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#path-parameters
- [parameter] `text`: Type=string; Required=No; Description=Initial context for this run, such as an alert body, a failing log line, or a git diff. The value is freeform text and is not parsed; if you send JSON or another structured payload, the routine receives it as a literal string. Passed to the routine alongside its saved prompt. Maximum 65,536 characters. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#request-body
- [parameter] `type`: Type=string; Description=Always `routine_fire`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#response
- [parameter] `claude_code_session_id`: Type=string; Description=The ID of the Claude Code session created for this run. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#response
- [parameter] `claude_code_session_url`: Type=string; Description=A link to the session on claude.ai. Open it in a browser to watch the run, review changes, or continue the conversation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#response
- [parameter] 400: Error type=`invalid_request_error`; Cause=Missing or invalid `anthropic-beta` header, `text` exceeds 65,536 characters, or the routine is paused (see [Edit and control routines](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines#edit-and-control-routines)). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#errors
- [parameter] 401: Error type=`authentication_error`; Cause=No bearer token in the `Authorization` header, or the token does not match this routine. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#errors
- [parameter] 403: Error type=`permission_error`; Cause=The account or organization does not have access to this endpoint. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#errors
- [parameter] 404: Error type=`not_found_error`; Cause=The routine does not exist. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#errors
- [parameter] 429: Error type=`rate_limit_error`; Cause=The account's routine run limit or usage limit has been reached. The response includes a `Retry-After` header indicating when the window resets. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#errors
- [parameter] 500: Error type=`api_error`; Cause=An unexpected server error. Retry with exponential backoff; if the error persists, contact support with the request ID. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#errors
- [parameter] 503: Error type=`overloaded_error`; Cause=The service is temporarily overloaded. Retry after a short delay. The Claude Platform returns 529 for this error type; this endpoint returns 503. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#errors
- [definition] Differences from the Claude Platform — The routine fire endpoint belongs to the Claude Code product surface, which differs from the Claude Platform APIs and SDKs in a few ways: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#differences-from-the-claude-platform
- [definition] Response — A successful request returns `200 OK` with the new session details: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#response
- [definition] Errors — Errors use the standard Anthropic [error envelope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors): — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#errors
- [definition] Authentication — The bearer token is scoped to a single routine. A compromised token can only trigger that routine; it grants no read access, no access to other routines, and no access to account data. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#authentication
- [definition] Idempotency — Each successful request creates a new session. There is no idempotency key. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#idempotency
- [definition] Rate limits — Routine runs count against a per-account daily allowance that varies by plan, and the resulting sessions draw down the same Claude Code subscription usage as interactive sessions. When either limit is reached, the endpoint returns `429 rate_limit_error` with a `Retry-After` header. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#rate-limits
- [definition] SDK support — This endpoint is not in the Anthropic SDKs. Its token model differs from API key authentication, and typical callers such as CI jobs and alerting webhooks send the request directly. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/claude-code/routines-fire#sdk-support

- [definition] Supported languages — The skill detects your project's language automatically by examining project files (for example, `requirements.txt` for Python, `tsconfig.json` for TypeScript, `go.mod` for Go) and loads the appropriate documentation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/claude-api-skill#supported-languages

When you ask Claude to help build something with the Claude API, or when your project already imports an Anthropic SDK, the skill activates automatically. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/claude-api-skill#in-claude-code-bundled

You can install it using the `npx` command: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/claude-api-skill#from-the-skills-repository

## Webhooks
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/webhooks>

- [definition] Unwrap — Verifies the webhook signature from the `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` headers using your webhook signing key, then parses the payload into an event. Fails if the signature is missing or invalid. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/webhooks#unwrap
- [definition] Parse Unverified — Parses a webhook payload into an event without verifying its signature. Prefer `unwrap()` unless you have already verified the signature yourself. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/webhooks#parse-unverified

- [parameter] `name`: The name of the tool. Must match the regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#specifying-client-tools
- [parameter] `description`: A detailed plaintext description of what the tool does, when it should be used, and how it behaves. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#specifying-client-tools
- [parameter] `input_schema`: A [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) object defining the expected parameters for the tool. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#specifying-client-tools
- [definition] API usage primer for Claude — > This guide is designed to give Claude the basics of using the Claude API. It gives explanation and examples of model IDs/the basic messages API, tool use, streaming, thinking, and nothing else. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#api-usage-primer-for-claude
- [definition] Multiple conversational turns — The Messages API is stateless, which means that you always send the full conversational history to the API. You can use this pattern to build up a conversation over time. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#multiple-conversational-turns
- [definition] Prefilling Claude's response — You can prefill part of Claude's response in the last position of the input messages list. Use this technique to shape Claude's response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#prefilling-claudes-response
- [definition] Vision — Claude can read both text and images in requests. Both `base64` and `url` source types are supported for images, along with the `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, and `image/webp` media types. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#vision
- [definition] Thinking — Thinking can sometimes help Claude with very hard tasks. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#thinking
- [definition] How thinking works — When thinking is on, Claude creates `thinking` content blocks where it outputs its internal reasoning. The API response includes `thinking` content blocks, followed by `text` content blocks. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#how-thinking-works
- [definition] Thinking with tool use — Thinking can be used alongside tool use, allowing Claude to reason through tool selection and results processing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#thinking-with-tool-use
- [definition] Interleaved thinking — Interleaved thinking enables Claude to think between tool calls, reasoning about tool results before deciding the next step. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#interleaved-thinking
- [definition] Specifying client tools — Client tools are specified in the `tools` top-level parameter of the API request. Each tool definition includes: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#specifying-client-tools
- [definition] Forcing tool use — You can force Claude to use a specific tool by specifying the tool in the `tool_choice` field: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#forcing-tool-use
- [definition] JSON output — Tools do not necessarily need to be client functions. You can use tools anytime you want the model to return JSON output that follows a provided schema. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#json-output
- [definition] Chain of thought — When using tools, Claude often shows its "chain of thought," that is, the step-by-step reasoning it uses to break down the problem and determine which tools to use. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#chain-of-thought
- [definition] Parallel tool use — By default, Claude may use multiple tools to answer a user query. You can disable this behavior by setting `disable_parallel_tool_use=true`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#parallel-tool-use
- [definition] Handling results from client tools — The response has a `stop_reason` of `tool_use` and one or more `tool_use` content blocks that include: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#handling-results-from-client-tools
- [definition] Handling the `max_tokens` stop reason — If Claude's response is cut off because it hits the `max_tokens` limit during tool use, retry the request with a higher `max_tokens` value. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#handling-the-max-tokens-stop-reason
- [definition] Handling the `pause_turn` stop reason — When using server tools such as web search, the API may return a `pause_turn` stop reason. Continue the conversation by passing the paused response back as-is in a subsequent request. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#handling-the-pause-turn-stop-reason
- [definition] Tool execution error — If the tool itself throws an error during execution, return the error message with `"is_error": true`: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#tool-execution-error
- [definition] Invalid tool name — If Claude's attempted use of a tool is invalid (for example, missing required parameters), try the request again with more-detailed `description` values in your tool definitions. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#invalid-tool-name
- [definition] Streaming messages — When creating a Message, you can set `"stream": true` to incrementally stream the response using server-sent events (SSE). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#streaming-messages
- [definition] Event types — Each server-sent event includes a named event type and associated JSON data. Each stream uses the following event flow: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/claude_api_primer#event-types
